News.title: All the new driving licence rules introduced in October
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

New driving licence restrictions have come into effect, banning young people from carrying certain passengers at night and restricting when learner drivers can take a test.

The changes, which have been launched in Northern Ireland, are aimed at reducing fatal road crashes involving young people.

According to official figures, 17- to 23-year-old drivers were responsible for almost a quarter of all collisions in Northern Ireland in 2024. That is despite them only accounting for 8 per cent of licence holders.

Data also shows that 251 people were killed or seriously injured in collisions involving a young driver in 2024. In 65 per cent of cases, the young driver was at fault.

The changes come after the government announced in January that learner drivers in England and Wales could face a wait of six months between sitting their theory and practical tests.

Here are the changes that have been made to driving licences.

The photocard driving licence was introduced to the UK in 1998 ( PA )

What changes have been made in Northern Ireland?

Northern Ireland has become the first part of the UK to introduce new rules for new drivers.

Graduated driver licensing (GDL), for learner and newly qualified drivers, now applies to all new drivers, but the changes are aimed at those aged 17 to 23 years old.

Learners must spend at least six months getting driving experience before they can take a practical test, and those under 24 face restrictions on carrying young passengers at night.

The rule changes were announced in January 2026, and drivers who do not follow the restrictions could receive three penalty points or a fine of up to £1,000.

What proposals are being considered for drivers born after 2002?

As part of the Road Safety Strategy that was initially developed under Sir Keir Starmer's former government, drivers born after 2002 may face stricter measures.

Andy Burnham’s new government is weighing proposals to implement a "minimum learning period for learner drivers".

Learners, the majority of whom are in their late teens and early 20s, could have to wait six months between their theory test and practical driving test as part of the plans.

Drivers under the age of 25 represent 6 per cent of licence holders but were involved in 24 per cent of fatal and serious crashes in 2024, according to Government figures.

Ministers believe minimum learning periods could help to reduce such collisions by up to 32 per cent, based on evidence from other countries.

Currently, someone can start learning to drive from the age of 17 with lessons on the road.

What has been proposed for drivers in their 70s?

Rather than take a whole new test, the proposal plans for drivers in their 70s to have their vision checked every three years to keep driving on UK roads.

This is also not a new policy announced by Mr Burnham but a policy which was first discussed in August 2025 during Sir Keir Starmer’s premiership, as part of a new road safety strategy.

The proposal went to consultation earlier this year between January and May.

What are the current rules for drivers over 70?

Currently, drivers aged 70 and over must renew their licence every three years and self-declare that they can meet the eyesight standards required to drive. Drivers also must declare any listed medical conditions.

However, the new proposal means drivers will no longer be able to simply say that their eyesight is good – instead, there will be mandatory eyesight tests as part of the licence renewal process.

News.title: Ukrainian Vampire drones drop food on town besieged by Russian army
News.content:
On Ukraine’s front lines, drones are the deadliest weapons in Kyiv’s arsenal, hunting Russian soldiers one by one with chilling precision.

But across the Dnipro River, the same machines have been given a very different mission: keeping trapped civilians from dying of starvation.

Since March, Ukrainian drones have been flying food and medicine into occupied Oleshky, on the river’s left bank, where residents are surviving on grass and weeds.

The town is less than three miles from Kherson, a city battered by Russian drones and shelling.

Since December, Oleshky has been under an effective blockade. Its roads are mined and shops have closed, with no food arriving by road since late May. Humanitarian agencies are blocked from entering, and the health system has all but collapsed.

Only around 2,000 of its 24,000 pre-war residents remain. For them, the drones are now their only lifeline.

“With the onset of winter, the situation is only getting worse,” said Elvina Osmanova of the Kherson regional military administration. “Food supplies are running out. People are facing a life-threatening choice: risk their lives trying to find food outside the city or remain without food.”

News.title: Man City dismantled by Paris St-Germain in breathless Champions League battle
News.content:
When Manchester City play like this what a loss their football will be to the Premier League – and the Champions League – if they are heavily sanctioned later this season.

In what turned out to be a match for the ages, a night of brilliant, unbridled attack, we were treated to the ultimate game of two halves as the back-to-back European champions Paris St-Germain took City apart for 45 minutes. And then were left holding on.

City will hope this is a sign of what is to come in their Premier League fight. But with a different result. After suffering a resounding defeat at the hands of the Premier League’s independent commission, with 114 of the 115 charges against them proven, they maintain their innocence and are mounting an appeal.

Could they make a comeback? It would be incredible and highly improbable if they did so but, out on the pitch, and 3-0 down after a first half in which they were in danger of being humiliated by PSG, they created enough opportunities to save themselves.

The data backed that. City’s expected goals (xG) was 2.57 while PSG’s was 1.83. City had 27 shots to 15 and had more possession and more passes. Enzo Maresca made a triple substitution to devastating effect, especially with the introduction of new signings Ayyoub Bouaddi and Iliman Ndiaye.

In the end they clawed back two goals, both scored by Erling Haaland, who now has 61 in 60 games in this competition – seventh outright in the all-time list, before Ruud van Nistelrooy. And 37 of those for City, overtaking Sergio Agüero’s club record.

News.title: Barcola starts to justify £123m price tag with hat-trick as Liverpool hit LASK for six
News.content:
Of the five Premier League teams in the Champions League this season, Liverpool have the friendliest league-phase fixtures and they can secure back-to-back wins against Austrian side LASK in this evening’s early kick off.

Having already vanquished one of their pot one opponents by beating Atletico Madrid at Anfield, Andoni Iraola’s team really should be targeting one of the top spots.

They travel to Linz without some key players, though. Alexander Isak, Cody Gakpo and Dominik Szoboszlai missed the defeat by Manchester City and remain sidelined, while Hugo Ekitike is a long-term absentee.

There were positive aspects to Liverpool’s performance against City, but they collapsed like a deck of cards after Ryan Gravenberch’s harsh second yellow card.

Tonight’s game is one they should dominate, and it is a presentable opportunity for Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola to kick-start their seasons and respond to the recent criticism of their performances. Iraola hopes to have a stronger squad to choose from at the weekend, when Liverpool face a stringent test at Brentford. This is the second of nine matches in 28 days for Liverpool.

“You don’t have a lot of time to train,” said Iraola. “You try to prepare the games now a lot of times just with the videos and the tactics boards, just a little bit outside. You have to prioritise the freshness of the players.

“Especially now we are playing four games in 10 days, it’s keeping all the legs, all the energy in the games.

LASK are currently third in the Austrian league, but booked their place in this season’s Champions League proper with a remarkable comeback from 4-0 down on aggregate against Celtic.

They have injury problems of their own to contend with George Bello and Moses Usor limping off in the weekend’s defeat by league leaders Rapid Wien and Ramiz Harakate tearing his anterior cruciate ligament in July.

They do play on a grass pitch at the Raiffeisen Arena though Kasper Schmeichel, the former Celtic goalkeeper who was working as a TV pundit for the game, was critical of the playing surface.

Full team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Second Ebola case confirmed in Kenya
News.content:
Kenya has recorded its second-ever case of Ebola after a relative of a patient who died last week tested positive for the virus, officials have said.

A 39-year-old man fell ill on Tuesday and has since been confirmed to be infected with Ebola, according to Kenyan health authorities.

The patient, who is now isolated, is a family member of Kenya’s first-ever Ebola case, who died in a hospital in Nairobi last Monday.

The index case, a 40-year old businessman, had travelled to Kenya from the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), the epicentre of the deadly outbreak of the rare Bundibugyo strain of Ebola, which has so far killed more than 4,300 people.

Kenyan authorities have identified 128 of his contacts and have successfully tracked down 113 of them, who are having their temperatures checked daily for a period of three weeks, the country’s Director-General for Health, Dr Patrick Amoth, said in a statement.

“There is no evidence of spread in the wider community,” the statement, issued on Wednesday, added.

However, questions remain over whether more cases will crop up in the coming weeks.

News.title: I tried Apple’s new smart home hub – the brand faithful will love it
News.content:
HomeView can control smart lights, heating, security cameras and video doorbells via touch or voice, but devices must support Matter – the cross-brand smart home standard. That means you aren’t confined to Apple-approved gadgets, but you are still limited – Ring video doorbells, for example, aren’t Matter-compatible, so they won’t work with HomeView, which could be a deal-breaker for even the biggest Apple fan.

But for anyone put off by the complexity of setting up a smart home, Apple is trying to simplify things. It has partnered with LG on Home Collection – a range of devices, including security cameras and a video doorbell – that connect with a single tap, just as AirPods do with an iPhone. They won’t be available until later in the year, but they could mark a major step towards making smart home set-up less complicated.

My early verdict

HomeView is built for the Apple faithful: set-up requires an iPhone or iPad, personalised AI features need a recent Apple Intelligence-capable iPhone, and some apps work only when your phone is nearby. In a household split between iPhone and Android, Android users will get a much thinner experience, and Apple’s own services come first at every turn.

Still, HomeView is the most polished smart display I have seen. Face recognition makes it both a great shared and personalised device; the sound quality is excellent; and Siri AI is finally worth talking to, especially when it can draw on your personal context. I’ll need to live with it for a few weeks before giving a final verdict, but so far it’s a beautifully designed device I’d be happy to invite into my home.

News.title: Ed Miliband calls for ‘new deal on debt’ as developing countries face spiralling borrowing costs
News.content:
Ed Miliband, the foreign secretary, has called for a “new deal on debt” as spiralling borrowing costs force developing countries to spend more on interest payments than on education or health.

In a speech in Bangkok on Wednesday, Mr Miliband warned that the global financial system is failing emerging markets, and promised to use the UK’s diplomatic heft to push for urgent reform.

He said: “The short-term repayments are crippling, and while many are not defaulting on their payments they are being forced, if you like, to default on the lives and prospects of future generations.

“So we need a new deal on debt, a deal that supports countries to repay over longer time horizons and, crucially, refinancing with better rates to give developing countries precious fiscal space.”

Although public debt is not inherently problematic, servicing costs are at a 25-year-high – squeezing government coffers just as conflict, climate change and a ‘Godzilla’ El Niño push food and fuel prices ever higher.

Emerging economies in particular have little headroom: according to the Rockefeller Foundation, average interest payments now exceed 10 per cent of revenue in developing nations, while UN Trade and Development (UNCTAD) analysis found 3.7 billion people live in countries where debt servicing costs exceed spending on health or education.

At the same time, overseas development aid (ODA) spending from wealthy countries has plummeted – hitting social, infrastructure and humanitarian projects, and disaster response.

The mounting global debt pile has dominated discussions in Bangkok this week, where some 15,000 people have descended for the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and World Bank annual meetings.

This included the first meeting of the newly formed Borrowers’ Platform on Monday. A group of finance ministers and central bank governors from some 30 countries, it was formed to exchange ideas about how to deal with debt burdens – and how to avoid pitfalls.

News.title: Trump backs down in Zambia mineral and data-sharing row
News.content:
Zambia has signed a five-year health financing agreement with the US government after the US dropped demands for access to sensitive health data and separated the deal from negotiations over the country’s mineral resources.

The agreement follows months of negotiations over a $2.49 billion health aid package, with Zambia pushing back against US demands to share medical data and give preferential access to the country’s rich mineral reserves in exchange for money to provide lifesaving healthcare.

Under the final agreement, Zambia will not be required to hand over individual patient records or biological specimens, which the US had previously argued was important for global disease surveillance.

Data sharing will be restricted to monitoring and evaluating US-funded health programmes.

A separate agreement covering US access to Zambia’s critical minerals has also been decoupled from the health financing deal, it was confirmed last week.

“The government will not be sharing any specimens with the United States because we removed all those aspects that raised concern,” Zambian Health Minister Roma Chilengi said last week as the agreement was signed.

Zambia’s Foreign Minister Mulambo Haimbe also confirmed that the health and mineral agreements had been separated.

“There was this [memorandum of understanding] on health and another on critical minerals, and we were saying that these need to be decoupled, and this has been done,” he said.

News.title: Progress against HIV stalls in South Africa, research shows
News.content:
South Africa’s progress in tackling the Aids and HIV crisis has stalled in one of its most populous provinces, new research has found.

The number of new cases of the infection in KwaZulu-Natal province, centred around the eastern port of Durban, have stopped falling after years of steep declines.

Data from a long-running study following thousands of people also showed those with detectable levels of virus in their blood had risen slightly despite years of medics prescribing antiretroviral drugs.

Researchers said the peer-reviewed study published in The Lancet HIV medical journal “provides a stark warning on prevailing HIV trends in rural South Africa, where ground is being lost in the fight against the HIV epidemic”.

The researchers, led by scientists at Durban’s Africa Health Research Institute (AHRI) and Stellenbosch University’s South African Centre for Epidemiological Modelling and Analysis (SACEMA), used a 20-year study which has tested nearly 60,000 people.

Analysis showed that after steep reductions in HIV incidence from 2013 to 2018, incidence rates for both males and females showed little or no decrease from 2019 onwards.

Incidence rates had continued to fall for young people under 35, but that had been offset by a lack of progress for those in middle age.

Sports.title: Kiss vows Wallabies will 'return fire' vs All Blacks | Rennie: Quality win was coming
Sports.content:
New Zealand vs Australia: Les Kiss vows Wallabies will 'return fire' vs All Blacks in Bledisloe Cup Test | Dave Rennie: Quality was coming

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of New Zealand vs Australia in the first Bledisloe Cup Test at Eden Park Highlights of New Zealand vs Australia in the first Bledisloe Cup Test at Eden Park

Australia head coach Les Kiss has vowed the Wallabies will "return fire" against the All Blacks in Saturday's return Bledisloe Cup Test in Sydney, live on Sky Sports.

Last week, Australia's six-Test unbeaten run came to a shuddering halt when New Zealand ensured they will retain the Bledisloe Cup for a 24th year after powering to a 50-19 victory over the Wallabies at Eden Park.

A competitive first half, perhaps even edged by Australia, saw the All Blacks three points ahead at the break as the sides traded two tries each.

But the second half proved altogether different, as the All Blacks added five further tries in a display of clear dominance.

"It's like anything. You get a knockback, you find out more about yourself and that's what we'll do. We'll work hard on what we have to do," said Kiss.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player New Zealand performed their famous haka before facing Australia at Eden Park last Saturday New Zealand performed their famous haka before facing Australia at Eden Park last Saturday

"Belief is created and sustained by not just wins and losses, they're created by other things. These boys have a strong culture, a strong belief in themselves and a confidence about what they can do.

"But the lessons are there: if you can't get your strengths going and their strengths grow, it makes it a difficult game.

"We'll go back and we'll work on what we have to and try and turn the dial in the right areas that can go to Sydney and return fire."

⁠Australia face some injury issues and will be without ​key centre Len Ikitau, who ​left Saturday's game in the first half ⁠with a head knock, while Hunter Paisami has been suspended.

Jordan Petaia ⁠is also unavailable due to ​an ankle injury, with Corey Toole ​and Kadin Pritchard coming in as replacements.

"Over the last five Tests, we didn't lose the run of ourselves; the boys always said we've got work to do. It doesn't change now," Kiss said.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The Wallabies picked up a stunning victory over South Africa in Perth last month, finishing with just 11 players The Wallabies picked up a stunning victory over South Africa in Perth last month, finishing with just 11 players

"We'll have a good look at that game, like we have, get into the nuts and bolts of what we need to get right. How do we get our strengths into the game? How do we just nullify their strengths, and that's what we look at.

"We need to make sure we do the work that gets that done. It'll be making sure we get the things that we feel that can make a difference, that's for sure.

"Once they got their momentum, it was hard to wrestle back."

Rennie: Quality performance from All Blacks had been coming

For the All Blacks, four players have been ruled ‌out of Saturday's Test in ‌Sydney.

New Zealand will be without hooker Asafo Aumua and back-row Anton Segner after both failed ​their second head-injury assessments (HIAs).

Flanker Ethan ⁠Blackadder has picked ⁠up a calf injury, and wing Leroy Carter has been ‌ruled out due to a high ankle sprain, which he suffered while scoring a ‌try in the second half.

New Zealand's Leroy Carter is one of four players out through injury for this weekend's contest

"I thought a quality performance was coming, but we're also playing a really good side," said New Zealand head coach Dave Rennie.

"So the arm wrestle in the first half [vs Australia at Eden Park], I thought we probably left a couple of opportunities out there, and then they scored late."

Rennie, who coached the Wallabies for three seasons before being dismissed in favour of the ill-fated return of Eddie Jones in 2023, pinpointed a couple of specific areas he feel turned last week's Test in the All Blacks' favour.

"We did a good job looking after the ball, and we played in the right parts of the field. Created good momentum and pressure and benefited from that.

"We're happy. We talked about a number of areas that needed to be better coming out of South Africa, and we saw good shifts. We're confident in our ability, and we felt in Africa that we just lost key moments.

"We had a really good edge around training, and we were well aware of the importance of winning and also the Bledisloe Cup. So it was nice to nail that."

A tight first half was eventually blown open by the All Blacks at Eden Park

The All Blacks head coach admitted the 31-point defeat at Eden Park won't define this Wallabies side under Kiss, and he expects a stronger performance in Sydney.

"Yeah, look, it's a tough end for them, but it was nice to catch up with a number of those guys post-game. Oh, they'll be hurting.

"They've had a really good year, and I'm confident they'll bounce back next week. Look, I'm very happy with the mindset and the work ethic brutality, and it was spot on."

Sports.title: Martinez releases statement to clarify outburst - but does not apologise
Sports.content:
Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez has clarified his outburst after Tuesday's Champions League loss at Atletico Madrid in a statement - but stopped short of an apology.

Martinez launched an extraordinary attack on the club's hierarchy after the 2-0 defeat in Madrid, as he criticised the lack of summer investment in the squad, said he expected more from "upstairs" and singled out technical director Jason Wilcox.

But 24 hours on from his astonishing post-match interview, the Argentina international released a statement on Instagram on Wednesday night to clear up his comments.

He said: "Following everything that has been said about my comments yesterday, I want to share some thoughts on what I said and how I feel.

"After the match, I spoke out of anger and frustration at not getting the result we all wanted.

"Those who know me know how I live football, with passion, commitment and a huge desire to win. And when things don't go our way, it hurts, especially when representing a club with the history and stature of Manchester United.

"My words reflect how I feel and how much I want to see this club competing for the biggest honours. Those high standards are part of how I see football and the responsibility that comes with wearing this shirt.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kaveh Solhekol and Rob Dorsett answered your questions about Martinez's post-match outburst

"When I talk about wanting more, I'm talking about the ambition we must all have as part of this club. To keep growing, to become stronger and to have everything we need to compete at the highest level. These are standards we must all hold ourselves to, starting with me.

"I know that, first and foremost, it's us, the players, who have to deliver, and I put myself at the front of that responsibility. We need to demand even more of ourselves and work together to take Manchester United back to the top.

"I believe in my team-mates, our manager and everyone working to help this club move forward. I'm convinced that the way forward is to keep working together, with ambition and commitment.

"My goal has been the same since day one, to win, to compete at the highest level and to give everything I have for this badge."

Sky Sports News' Football Correspondent Rob Dorsett:

There are real doubts about whether Martinez's contract will be extended when it expires in the summer.

United will focus on revamping their defence in the next transfer windows and have the formal option to prolong Martinez's stay for a further year.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jamie O'Hara criticised Martinez following comments made by the defender aimed at the Manchester United hierarchy

Sky Sports News has also been told United are looking at new centre-backs, as well as left-backs.

United's bosses have yet to decide whether to discipline Martinez for his comments, when he said: "I expect more from our technical director [meaning director of football, Jason Wilcox]. We expect more from the top, from upstairs, to bring in more players to compete."

Sky Sports News has been told there is anger and bemusement at what Martinez said, both in the United boardroom and in the changing room, with at least one other player challenging him over his comments as the squad got on board the plane to fly back to Manchester.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Soccer Special pundits react to Lisandro Martinez's comments aimed at Manchester United's hierarchy after their Champions League defeat to Atletico Madrid.

It is also understood that there is no pressure on Wilcox internally regarding his position.

The implication that Martinez doesn't think his team-mates are good enough to compete has not gone down well with other players.

Martinez has been keen on a move away from Old Trafford for some time.

In the summer, he pushed for a move to Atletico Madrid, the side that beat United in the Champions League on Tuesday night, to follow his good friend and international team-mate, Cristian Romero, who left Spurs for Spain.

No suitable bid for Martinez came in for Manchester United to consider.

The 28-year-old made similar explosive comments about his bosses when at Ajax in 2022. Martinez, who again wanted a move away, called their sporting director Gerry Hamstra a "nobody".

Martinez remains a key part of Michael Carrick's squad and United's bosses know they have to handle this situation carefully.

Sports.title: Man City beaten by PSG in thriller as Guardiola returns to Etihad
Sports.content:
Manchester City were beaten 4-2 by a majestic Paris Saint-Germain as Pep Guardiola watched on from the stands in an enthralling Champions League encounter.

The reigning back-to-back European champions were keen to make their power felt early at the Etihad, in a game that made clear where the greater concentration of quality resides. Luis Enrique's side were breathtaking in the first half, a masterclass in effortless control with and without the ball.

Desire Doue scored from range. Ousmane Dembele rounded off a wonderful team move 99 seconds later. And Vitinha finished a brilliant first 45 minutes with a thumping finish from Warren Zaire-Emery's instinctive flick. "If you don't go toe-to-toe, you struggle," reflected Enzo Maresca.

Image: Former Man City manager Pep Guardiola was in the stands for the first time since leaving the club

A pair of Erling Haaland goals made the scoreline respectable after the interval, and City were good value for both breakthroughs, doing to PSG what had been done to them in the first period. They hit the woodwork a further two times in a half that became increasingly more frantic and transitional.

Despite wave after wave of attack and big chances missed, it was Gianluigi Donnarumma who failed to escape the glare of the spotlight, his poor handling gifting Maghnes Akliouche and the visitors a fourth. He atoned by denying Ferran Torres' woeful penalty attempt late on.

PSG's first-half blitz proved decisive and sobered the atmosphere around a fairly muted Etihad, but Maresca will take comfort from the way his side turned a would-be rout into a thrilling clash of titans.

Image: Man City stage an inquest after conceding three first-half goals

PSG come out on top in battle of recent winners

As well as being two of the earliest clubs to fall foul of UEFA's financial rules back in 2014, Man City and PSG shared one other thing in common before combining to win three of the past four Champions League titles: They had won none of the previous 67.

Each lost their first Champions League final - PSG to Bayern in 2020 and City the following year to Chelsea. But with both clubs backed by free-spending owners from the Middle East, boasting some of the most talented squads in world football, that deficiency has since become a surplus.

With City now fighting against charges of financial rule-breaking on a domestic front, all of which the club deny, the decision was made for a show of unity on home turf. Guardiola was flanked by high-ranking executives in the terraces, including Chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak and chief executive Ferran Soriano.

Image: Manchester City Chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak and CEO Ferran Soriano in the stands before kick off

They will have seen plenty they liked on the pitch, City's players appearing laser-focused on the job at hand despite the cloud of uncertainty that surrounds them. Ultimately, this is a defeat of fairly insignificant jeopardy where chances and goals made for a superb watch between two European contenders.

The world of football will continue to tune in to see how City handle whatever might come next. Whenever that might be.

A difficult night to make sense of!

Image: Haaland hangs his head after defeat to PSG

Sky Sports' Ben Ransom at the Etihad:

Where do you start trying to make sense of that?

Pep Guardiola was back for a bonkers night, with his former side showing plenty of the strengths and weaknesses that displayed themselves in different ways during his tenure. The City fightback at least means his visit won't be characterised by a humbling defeat.

PSG were the better side overall and deserved the win, but on another night the scoreline could have been reversed, given the number of chances that went begging for the home side.

The City fans might not get to see their side in this competition next year, but as they made clear before kick-off, this is a fanbase that has stood by the club during dark times before, and is promising to do so again.

Maresca believes City can match PSG

Man City boss Enzo Maresca:

"It was a strange game. Two goals in two minutes created some problems for us. We were dead in the game, and then second half we created so many chances. Second half, we were good.

"We lost a bit of balance, distance between players, and we struggle first half. Second half we made changes and adjusted some things, then we were much better. These kind of teams, if you don't go toe-to-toe you struggle. We had to be more brave. Second half, we were.

"We are there, to be honest. My feeling is that we are close. It's already difficult against PSG, but then you concede two quick goals. We can learn from that and move on."

Man City's next fixtures...
