Sports.title: Quickfire Doué and Dembélé inspire PSG to thrilling win at Manchester City
Sports.content:
A penny for Pep Guardiola’s thoughts. The legendary Manchester City manager was back at the Etihad Stadium for the first time since his departure at the end of last season and, well, the announcement of you-know-what.

Sporting a flat cap, Guardiola took his seat in the stands behind the City chair, Khaldoon al-Mubarak, and the chief executive, Ferran “Not” Soriano, and, certainly, the TV director seemed intent on scrutinising him – if the number of cutaway shots to him were any guide.

Everybody knows where Guardiola stands on the great City scandal; the numerous guilty verdicts handed down to them on the 100-plus charges they have faced for breaking the Premier League’s financial rules. He has backed his former employers to somehow disprove them. But what did he make of his old team here against the might of the defending European champions, Paris Saint-Germain?

Not much in the first half would have been a reasonable conclusion. PSG played football from a higher plane and they might have led by more than the three unanswered goals they scored. But if defiance has been the theme for City – and it fed into Guardiola’s presence here – they produced plenty more of it during a thrilling second half.

City refused to accept the inevitable. They threw everything at PSG. Erling Haaland ran on adrenaline as City created a flurry of openings. The No 9 was unplayable at times; he finished with two goals and a few near misses. City were a goal away from worrying PSG.

The problem for them was the one that Maghnes Akliouche scored to put PSG 4-1 in front. It meant that City’s dream of an astonishing fightback was only an illusion. What a terrible concession it was for Gianluigi Donnarumma – and not for the first time.

View image in fullscreen The former City manager Pep Guardiola takes his seat at the Etihad. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

It was a spin and blast from Akliouche on the edge of the area and Donnarumma appeared to have palmed the ball up and away. Except that it dropped all the way back down – quite a way back down – and into the net. How did it happen? It was one of many head-scratchers; the sheer weight of chances was difficult to process. PSG even threw in a late penalty fail by Ferran Torres, who came on as a substitute; his kick was weak and too close to Donnarumma. Are you missing it all, Pep?

City must play under a cloud, certainly until their appeal against the charges is completed, and they ran into a PSG team that shimmered with menace. Luis Enrique’s starting XI featured seven players who are on the 30-strong Ballon d’Or shortlist. The manager had another three from it among his substitutes, including João Neves and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia.

PSG bristled with their trademark assurance on the ball; the beautifully grooved combinations. It does not matter how tight the spaces are. They back themselves to get out of them. Witness the opening goal and a scintillating piece of team play that began deep on the right-hand side of their defensive third.

In the blink of an eye, PSG were surging up the flank and then opening out the move, Fabián Ruiz playing the final pass to Désiré Doué on the left. The winger cut inside and shot low for the near corner from outside the area. It was the precision that did for Donnarumma, although the former PSG goalkeeper had to do better at his post.

View image in fullscreen Ousmane Dembélé doubles PSG’s lead in the first half. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

When PSG landed the follow-up punch just 75 seconds later, City were reeling, the home crowd stunned. It was a goal that featured two crosses, the first from Ousmane Dembélé out to Doué on the left. He took the ball down and crossed back for Dembélé, who stole in behind Marc Guéhi. The run was too cute, the header straightforward.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

It was no exaggeration to say that PSG could have had five by the interval. City had no defence to their cut and thrust; the sheer pace of it, the positional fluidity too. Achraf Hakimi appeared to be playing almost anywhere but right-back. He popped up inside the six-yard box in the 32nd minute only to send a free header against the post, but City were swiftly disabused of the notion that the danger had passed.

View image in fullscreen Vitinha sweeps home PSG’s third before the interval. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

PSG won the ball back and went for the jugular once again. Akliouche was involved, there was a lovely backheeled assist from Warren Zaïre-Emery and Vitinha lashed home a low drive. When Hakimi blew a one-on-one with Donnarumma on 39 minutes, it felt as though his team were toying with City.

Enzo Maresca made a triple change at the interval, introducing Matheus Nunes, Ayyoub Bouaddi and Iliman Ndiaye – and the effect was immediate. City played with devil-may-care abandon. Their toothless first half was forgotten. Enzo Fernández blew a gilt-edged headed opportunity and Ndiaye worked Matvey Safonov before Haaland pulled one back. It was a whipped ball in from Ndiaye, which Haaland sent into the far corner with a flex of the neck muscles. He was not close in, either.

Could City take the lifeline? Antoine Semenyo ran through and dinked against the crossbar. The offside flag was raised, although he looked to have been level. City needed the next goal to make it interesting. Instead, they lost the initiative after another Donnarumma lapse.

It was the prompt for a whirlwind finale. Josko Gvardiol saw a header cleared off the line by Nuno Mendes, Fernández rattled the outside of a post and Haaland looped a header against the top of the crossbar before he scored again – a low finish after good work from Bouaddi. Haaland was denied the hat-trick when he stretched to prod at Nunes’ cross at goal – it was an excellent save by Safonov – and City finished with 27 shots and 52 touches in the opposition box. Those numbers would be enough for victory on most nights. Just not this one.

Sports.title: ‘I expect more’: the key questions from Martínez’s Manchester United broadside | Jamie Jackson
Sports.content:
After Manchester United’s 2-0 loss at Atlético Madrid, Lisandro Martínez teed off at the director of football, Jason Wilcox, and the rest of the executive. “We don’t have the best squad at the moment compared with other top teams,” said the defender. “I expect more [investment], 100%. I expect more from our technical director [Jason Wilcox] … Really poor [the Atlético defeat] – I have to control myself a lot but something is a reflection of the mirror of how our club is at the moment.” Here we consider the key questions emerging from Martínez’s explosive remarks.

Is Martínez’s view reflective of the squad generally?

Yes is the short answer. The Guardian has been told the decision to target three midfielders in Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans and Carlos Baleba caused bemusement in the squad that no other areas were strengthened in the summer. Carrick led United to third last term after the side only had 17 league games remaining when he took over in January, having been eliminated from the other competitions. The need for defensive reinforcements is particularly acute because the back four of Diogo Dalot, Martínez, Harry Maguire and Luke Shaw has been together since 2022. Martínez is out of contract next summer and it is thought the 28-year-old may not be offered a new deal or have his one-year option triggered by the club, so teammates are conscious his outburst also came because he expects to leave.

How culpable is Wilcox?

As United’s director of football the 55-year-old wields near-unilateral power on football decisions, with only Sir Jim Ratcliffe, who controls sporting policy, above him. If the buck stops with the executive, the most recent transfer window was Wilcox’s responsibility. This was the latest in a line of missteps on his United record. One concerns when Dan Ashworth (Wilcox’s predecessor) was on gardening leave from Newcastle in the first half of 2024, Wilcox interviewed potential replacements for Erik ten Hag before, oddly, deeming that the head coach should stay. The Dutchman signed a fresh contract but was sacked that autumn. Another involves Wilcox’s major falling out with the man he hired as the Dutchman’s successor, Ruben Amorim, after which the Portuguese said the director of football had told him he should change his favoured 3-4-3 shape. “I came here to be the manager of Manchester United – not to be the coach of Manchester United,” said Amorim, after a 1-1 draw at Leeds on 4 January (his job title was head coach). He was sacked the next day. Wilcox worked with Omar Berrada, United’s chief executive, at Manchester City, where Berrada rose to become chief football operations officer, and Wilcox became academy director. Wilcox moved to Southampton and became director of football from summer 2023 until April 2024, when he joined United, having been identified by Berrada, so there is scrutiny of his experience at elite level.

View image in fullscreen Lisandro Martínez’s post-match interview has exposed the divisions at Manchester United. Photograph: Ash Donelon/Manchester United/Getty Images

How much blame is Carrick’s?

The 45-year-old’s ability to prosper is related to the quality of Wilcox’s work, primarily in the market, so he cannot be solely responsible for a dire six points from six league games and two victories in all competitions all season. Yet by definition his role as head coach demands Carrick do the best with his resources, and that progress is made on the training ground. On matchdays there is scant excuse for United’s disjointedness, inferior running stats and inability, twice, to take advantage against 10 men: the 1-0 loss to City and Saturday’s 1-1 draw with Tottenham. How is Carrick viewed by his players? According to Santos they back him. “We believe in the manager, we believe in the whole staff, we believe in [ourselves as] players,” he said after the Atlético game. “We are in a bad moment but we have to work to change this result.”.

Is United’s unity and discipline crumbling?

For further evidence see Amad Diallo’s Snapchat post after the defeat by Atlético: “Fucking disgrace; I have no words.” So United have a World Cup-winner, Martínez, aiming shots at Wilcox and by implication Ratcliffe and Berrada, and a fellow senior player, Diallo, cursing but in ambiguous fashion, adding to the sense of meltdown at the club because it is unclear whether the “disgrace” meant the performance, Martínez’s diatribe, the squad his teammate referred to as not good enough, or something else. All of this is mirrored on the pitch, where United’s 671.4km run in the Premier League is the fifth-lowest (Arsenal’s 716.2 is the highest), and their 581 sprints the fourth-lowest (Brentford’s 765 the most).

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Michael Carrick has support from his squad but Manchester United’s form has dropped significantly this season. Photograph: Susana Vera/Reuters

Where are the Glazers in all this?

In mitigation Wilcox can point to the six American siblings, who remain majority owners and whose family has placed an eye-watering £1.1bn-plus debt on the club that severely restricts the transfer budget. Wilcox oversaw a £155m summer outlay and a net spend of about £100m in a summer when City’s corresponding figures were £457.5m and about £175m. City buying players such as Enzo Fernández (for a British record-equalling £125m), Elliot Anderson (£115m), Ayyoub Bouaddi (£81m) and Iliman Ndiaye (£65m) showed their greater financial muscle, helped by being much better sellers of talent. How they have reached this point has, though, been thrown into sharp focus by last month’s verdict that they have serially cheated.

Are there positives for United?

Any straw should be clutched at so Carrick and his staff can view the first 97 minutes of Baleba’s United career as a rosy augury. After entering on 59 minutes against Spurs, a cute swivel and deft chip to Bruno Fernandes was a moment as impressive as the rest of his debut, and at Atlético the 22-year-old hunted down opponents and crunched into tackles, suggesting his game contains energy, muscularity and skill. It’s early days but perhaps if Baleba had been fit to start the campaign (he was recovering from an ankle problem) he might have affected one or more of the defeat at Hull, the 2-2 draw at Everton when Ainsley Maitland-Niles equalised late, the 1-0 loss to City when Phil Foden was sent off after 23 minutes or the Carabao Cup elimination by Brighton.

Sports.title: Jackson and Barkley doubles sink feeble Fenerbahce in record Aston Villa win
Sports.content:
It may be a bit early for the pantomime season but the Holte End enjoyed acclaiming their heroes and villains as Aston Villa won at home for the first time this season with their biggest victory in European competition. Every touch for Mason Greenwood, playing his first game in England since January 2022, was booed, but even louder applause was reserved for Aston Villa’s rediscovered attacking prowess.

Johan Manzambi celebrated his 21st birthday by opening the scoring on his first Champions League appearance, before Nicolas Jackson took the game beyond Fenerbahce’s reach with two more goals before half-time to help banish any fears about playing in front of the demolished North Stand.

With Prince William cheering on from the stands, Ross Barkley made this a night to remember as he scored twice, the first goal from a penalty earned by Manzambi, and Tammy Abraham helped Villa score six in a game for the first time since beating Brighton in 2023. No team has won more games (15) in European competition since the start of last season.

Villa’s supposed hex about playing in front of the empty North Stand was put to bed as they scored three times at the end of the ground that is being redeveloped this winter. “Greenwood, Greenwood, what’s the score,” echoed around the three packed stands at Villa Park. Chants of a less salubrious nature were also given regular renditions. This was the former England forward’s first game in this country since he played in Manchester United’s 1-0 win against West Ham United in nearly five years ago.

View image in fullscreen Johan Manzambi scores his deflected goal for the opener. Photograph: Tim Keeton/EPA

Greenwood was charged in 2022 with attempted rape, controlling and coercive behaviour and assault occasioning actual bodily harm. The Crown Prosecution Service discontinued the case in February 2023 after key witnesses withdrew their involvement and new material came to light. The player had denied the charges.

He had played for Marseille in a friendly against Villa 14 months ago, when he allegedly spat at Amadou Onana. So it was no surprise when his name was booed as the teams were announced and at every subsequent involvement.

Far more palatable was the freedom with which Villa played. Jackson now has five goals for Unai Emery’s team since signing from Chelsea for £65m in the summer while Manzambi, a £59.5m capture from Freiburg, was a joy to watch in the No 10 role, combining deft touch with wiry physicality. “My first Champions League game and my first goal, on my birthday,” he said. “My family are here. That’s very nice for me.”

The Switzerland international composed himself to score after Mattéo Guendouzi had inadvertently headed on John McGinn’s cross following a short corner.

Zion Suzuki twice saved well from Vedat Muriqi but Villa created umpteen chances themselves. Jackson, collecting Boubacar Kamara’s pass, struck home cleanly from the edge of the penalty area just after the half-hour mark before repeating the trick six minutes before the interval. In between, Oguz Aydin shot against the Villa bar, but, truth be told, Villa’s 11th successive home win in European competitions was already safely banked.

Villa’s free-scoring spell is in stark contrast to their start to the season, when they only managed one goal in their opening four games. Now they have scored at least three times in four of their past six matches.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Should they beat Viking here next Wednesday, Villa would be well on their way to qualifying from the league stage with nine points from three games. “We are being ambitious,” Unai Emery, the Villa manager, said. “We want to be protagonists in the Champions League.”

View image in fullscreen Nicolas Jackson drills the ball between Nathan Aké’s legs to score Aston Villa’s third. Photograph: Andrew Boyers/Action Images/Reuters

Manzambi was tripped by Ismail Yuksek midway through the second half for the penalty from which Barkley made it 4-0, even if Jackson admitted he had fancied the chance to keep the match ball. “Yeah I wanted to take it but the most important thing is we win,” the striker told TNT Sports. “Hopefully next time I’ll get the hat-trick.”

The cheers that followed that goal were promptly matched by the jeers for Greenwood as he was substituted. The pantomime was over as a contest.

Barkley swiftly added a fifth with a deflected shot. But even before Abraham turned in Alysson’s cross for the sixth goal, some Villa minds were turning to Saturday evening’s trip to Newcastle United and the perennial autumnal challenge of resurrecting a difficult start to the league season. In Emery they trust.

Sports.title: Bradley Barcola’s clinical hat-trick inspires Liverpool to 6-3 rout of Lask
Sports.content:
Liverpool cleansed themselves from the stains of defeat by Manchester City at the earliest opportunity. A rampant display in Austria saw Bradley Barcola ignite his Liverpool account with the first hat-trick of his professional career and Andoni Iraola’s team devastate Lask’s big night in the Champions League. The major surprise was how the hosts managed to score three.

Iraola’s pre-match faith in the big-money signings Barcola and Florian Wirtz was repaid as the pair helped dismantle limited opponents. But it was not all about the money and the £123m signing from Paris Saint-Germain scoring the first goals of his Liverpool career. Lewis Koumas registered his first goal in the competition and replaced Steven Gerrard as the youngest player to score and assist in a Champions League game for Liverpool. A total of 26 shots equalled Liverpool’s record in a Champions League away game.

“I’m really happy for Bradley,” said the Liverpool head coach. “Yesterday you were asking me a lot about his numbers, and also Flo [Wirtz], and both of them played really well. They made a difference. Apart from the hat-trick Bradley was a threat one-v-one, helped us control the game and defended the pockets. It will do their confidence good for sure.”

The home end was full and in strong voice over an hour before kick-off as Lask supporters came to savour their club’s first home game in the Champions League proper. The Lask team proved to be much less impressive though, in fairness to the Austrian crowd, their support rarely wavered even as a rout unfolded before their eyes. Liverpool revelled in their superiority and the invitation to recover from Sunday’s first defeat of the season.

Iraola rested Virgil van Dijk, delaying the defender’s 200th game as Liverpool captain, and Alexis Mac Allister as he managed workloads ahead of Saturday’s visit to Brentford. A new-look central defence of Ronald Araújo and Jérémy Jacquet were given a physical test by the Lask strikers Samuel Adeniran and Krystof Danek but handled the host’s rudimental approach comfortably.

View image in fullscreen Bradley Barcola slides the ball into the bottom corner to score his second in the first half. Photograph: Dénes Erdős/AP

Liverpool were utterly dominant against an opponent that struggled to retain possession in all areas of the pitch. The breakthrough was inevitable but also a result of a mix-up in the Lask defence between Alemão and the goalkeeper, Lukas Jungwirth. From the second corner that followed their error, Araújo towered above his marker to head home Kostas Tsimikas’s delivery. It was the Uruguay international’s first Liverpool goal and the start of an onslaught.

Merely 96 seconds later it was 2-0 as Barcola also scored his first Liverpool goal. The summer recruit found himself under scrutiny ahead of the game, along with Wirtz, having gone six appearances for his new club without a goal or an assist. That issue was put to bed when Rio Ngumoha weaved in from the right and Koumas laid the ball back to the lurking winger. Barcola swept a first-time shot inside Jungwirth’s far post. Liverpool were enjoying themselves.

Wirtz soon found himself with a much-needed assist for Barcola’s second goal. The Germany international has looked more at home for Liverpool in the Champions League than Premier League and this was no exception. Wirtz picked out Barcola’s run into the Lask area and the winger rolled a cool finish beyond the exposed keeper.

Lask could have been seriously embarrassed before half-time. Koumas had a fine finish disallowed for offside and, following another neat exchange between Wirtz and Barcola, Ryan Gravenberch’s shot kissed the inside of the far post. Liverpool’s 19 attempts on goal were the most by an away side in the first half of a Champions League game since records began in 2003-04.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Liverpool’s Lewis Koumas jumps for joy after opening his Champions League account. Photograph: Michael Zemanek/Shutterstock

There would be no letup from Iraola’s team after the interval. Jeremie Frimpong morphed into an old-fashioned centre-forward to rise above Yvan Dibango and bury a textbook header into the bottom corner from Tsimikas’s cross. Koumas had a second goal disallowed for offside before Alisson’s clean sheet was ruined by the Lask substitute Robert Ljubicic sweeping home inside his near post. Barcola was presented with his hat-trick when Ngumoha released Frimpong and the full-back flashed a low cross through the Lask six-yard box. Barcola applied a simple finish at the back post.

Frimpong also supplied the assist for Koumas’s deserved goal, converted from close range after the home side were caught playing out from the back. The Lask substitute Florian Flecker brought a touch of respectability to the scoreline with two goals in four minutes, both set up by Dibango, but there was no disguising the emphatic manner of Liverpool’s victory nor the surge of confidence it should give to Barcola.

Sports.title: Champions League: Mourinho’s Real Madrid stage wild comeback on Roma return
Sports.content:
José Mourinho enjoyed a Roma reunion to remember as Real Madrid completed an astonishing comeback by scoring three late goals to claim a 4-3 away win in the Champions League on Wednesday.

Marten de Roon gave the hosts a deserved opener before Kylian Mbappé struck back on his 100th Champions League appearance to level the scores at the break. Two Donyell Malen strikes in the space of six minutes early in the second half seemed to take the game away from the 15-time European champions as Roma ran rampant.

But Madrid scored three goals in the final six minutes, all stemming from corners, to turn the game on its head as Carlos Espí, Endrick and the former Roma defender Antonio Rüdiger struck at a stunned Stadio Olimpico.

Mourinho was a popular figure as he led Roma to the Conference League title and Europa League final during two-and-a-half years in charge. The Portuguese coach was honoured with banners and chants by the home crowd in Roma’s first home Champions League match in more than seven years.

View image in fullscreen José Mourinho is given a hero’s welcome on his return to Roma. Photograph: Alessandra Tarantino/AP

The Real Madrid winger Vinícius Júnior, who featured in the win, was handed a four-match ban for pulling an opponent’s hair during Saturday’s league win over Villarreal. The decision was announced shortly before the game kicked off in Rome – a situation that left Mourinho furious with Spain’s football authorities.

“They do things shamelessly now,” Mourinho said. The cat is out of the bag now. Two hours before the match, a player must know he has a four-match suspension. Couldn’t they do it now? Couldn’t they do it tomorrow morning? Do we have to come by bus and almost arrive at the stadium when we find out?”

Fredrik Sjøvold’s 52nd-minute strike secured a 1-0 victory for Bodø/Glimt over Borussia Dortmund, extending the Norwegian side’s remarkable home record against Europe’s elite.

Bodø were a cut above the 2024 Champions League runners-up and took the lead through Sjøvold just after the break. Dortmund improved in the final half hour but were unable to strike back, despite a late chance for Felix Nmecha.

“There’s nothing we can complain about, we deserved to lose,” said the Dortmund coach, Niko Kovac. “We didn’t bring enough passion today – that’s something Bodø did much better. They took the lead and after that we woke up, but by then it was too late.”

View image in fullscreen Fredrik Sjøvold celebrates after scoring what proved to be the winner for Bodø/Glimt. Photograph: NTB/Reuters

Dortmund join Manchester City, Inter and Sporting as recent big-name scalps on the artificial turf of Bodø’s Aspmyra Stadium. Bodø’s run to the last 16 last season was underpinned by an excellent record at their 8,200-capacity home, officially the smallest venue in this year’s competition.

Nomadic Ukrainian champions Shakhtar Donetsk celebrated moving into their new Champions League “home” at Stamford Bridge by storming back to beat AEK Athens 3-1.

The Greek side took the lead in the 28th minute through Lovro Majer but Pedrinho levelled confidently from the penalty spot just six minutes later. With about 10 minutes of normal time to go, Vinicius Tobias found the net from a tight angle and the substitute Gleiker Mendoza made the game safe, smashing home after cutting in from the left.

Shakhtar, from the east of Ukraine, are using Chelsea’s ground as the base for their European fixtures this season, with the Londoners absent from continental competition.

View image in fullscreen Shakhtar Donetsk fans make themselves at home at Stamford Bridge. Photograph: Kirsty Wigglesworth/AP

Since the beginning of Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, the UK has provided refuge to 265,000 Ukrainians, according to the Ukrainian embassy in London. Fans from the expat population turned out in force on Wednesday, swelling the crowd to 29,000.

Isco scored the winner and Abde Ezzalzouli netted a contender for goal of the week as Real Betis defeated Porto 3-2 in a bad-tempered game in Seville.

Ezzalzouli struck the ball from the corner of the penalty area into the top corner at the far post after the break. Gabriel Veiga equalised with a fine free-kick and set off a kerfuffle between rival players with his celebration. Three players were booked.

The Porto substitute Samu Aghehowa – a Spain international – scored just two minutes after coming on, only for Cucho Hernández – another substitute – to equalise in the 74th. Isco got the winner late with a penalty.

Stuttgart continued their 100% record in this season’s league phase with a 3-0 win against Slovan Bratislava in Slovakia. Earlier, Anis Hadj Moussa scored twice as the Dutch leaders, Feyenoord, came from behind to beat visiting Como 3-2.

Sports.title: Championship roundup: Soucek doubles up as West Ham hit nine-man Lincoln for six
Sports.content:
West Ham returned to winning ways as they cruised to a 6-0 Championship victory against nine-man Lincoln at the ProAmpac Stadium.

The hosts had Tom Hamer sent off after just three minutes and Conor McGrandles followed him off the pitch 20 minutes later, with Konstantinos Mavropanos heading West Ham ahead on the stroke of half-time.

The second half was dominated by West Ham, with further goals coming from Edvin Austbø, Jarrod Bowen, Pablo and Tomas Soucek, who scored twice, as the beleaguered home side desperately tried to keep the score down.

“I credit Lincoln as even with one man down, they were in the game and still creating a lot of problems for us,” said the West Ham manager, Nuno Espírito Santo, after watching his club’s biggest away win for 103 years.

“I think we made mistakes in terms of trying to rush things,” Nuno added. “It changed after the second goal and we played much better, in terms of being patient, recycling the ball and being clinical.”

Southampton recorded their second hard-fought 1-0 win in the space of four days as they condemned their hosts, Norwich, to a fourth successive league defeat.

Tonda Eckert’s side followed up Sunday’s victory over their local rivals, Portsmouth, with their first away win of the campaign in the league, with Kuryu Matsuki scorijng what proved to be the winner early in the second half.

Southampton are now well-placed in the top half of the table after 10 games, despite starting the campaign with a four-point deduction, while Norwich remain too close to the bottom for comfort after another disappointing display.

“To be fair there have been some good performances away from home when we just needed to finish better, ” Eckert said. “Tonight we have put in another good performance and on this occasion, we have got our reward. I am very happy for the boys because they worked very hard out there.”

Ebou Adams scored an 89th-minute winner as Portsmouth recovered after giving away a 2-0 lead to beat 10-man Sheffield United 3-2 at Fratton Park.

The hosts had been in cruise control after Zak Swanson’s stunning blast into the top corner and Adrian Segecic’s tap-in either side of Hamza Choudhury’s dismissal for two bookings. But Japhet Tanganga and Tom Cannon levelled the score and the visitors were somehow hunting back-to-back victories for the first time this season.

View image in fullscreen Southampton manager Tonda Eckert celebrates with his players after their 1-0 win at Norwich. Photograph: Nigel French/PA

Adams had the last word when he jumped off the bench to convert with a minute to go to give Portsmouth their third win of the campaign. After the game, Sheffield United manager Chris Wilder criticised referee Oliver Langford for his decision to send Choudhury off.

“There were a number of decisions which were incredibly frustrating,” Wilder said. “That is three players that have been sent off in the last two games he [Langford] has refereed us. Where are the young and up-and-coming referees who would be refereeing in the Championship now, instead of the ones that are just surviving?

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“No doubt we will have another survivor ref on Saturday. Where is the quality? Where are the ones coming through?” Wilder added. It is a tough one for the players, but there is more frustration and anger towards somebody. We have to deal with it.”

The Portsmouth head coach, John Mousinho, was frustrated by his team’s display despite their late winner. “I am happy that we won the game but the nature and circumstances of it … we have a large amount to learn and a long way to come.

“There was a little bit of relief when the winner went in, but there was fury through the game and I still am furious,” he added. “I think the players are on the same page as me and that is why there was muted celebrations at the end.”

QPR continued their impressive early season form with a thumping 4-1 win at home to struggling Derby. Three of the goals came in the first half, with Alfie Lloyd scoring, Nicolas Madsen tucking away a penalty and Harvey Vale adding the third.

Paul Smyth made it four with a deflected effort midway through the second half before Lars-Jørgen Salvesen scored a late consolation goal for Derby. Rangers’ victory was marred by a potentially serious knee injury to defender Amadou Mbengue, who was carried off on a stretcher late on.

Derby have now gone six league games without a win but their head coach, John Eustace, remains optimistic despite increasing pressure. “It’s a long season. We’ve had some difficult moments and I’m confident we’ll come through it,” Eustace said. “I don’t think the players will need picking up. I think they’ll be angry and ready to go for the next game.”

Sports.title: Manchester City staff invited on government trade trip to India
Sports.content:
A club representative from Manchester City was invited on a government-backed trade delegation to India this week, despite the club being found guilty of 114 breaches of Premier League rules.

Andy Burnham’s successor as Manchester mayor Bev Craig took a representative from the club to Delhi and Mumbai on a trip organised by business secretary Jonathan Reynolds, where she and other northern mayors have been promoting British trade and tourism.

She defended the decision to invite City even as the prime minister came under fire for his own contacts with the club, telling the Guardian it had played a vital role in helping build infrastructure in her city.

“If a football club has broken the rules, a football club should be punished for breaking the rules, and that is pretty clear in an independent process,” she said.

“I think what can also be true at the same time though, if you ask residents in east Manchester, have they benefited from a new library, a new leisure centre, a new sixth-form college, infrastructure investment, the job opportunities that come from them being a good employment charter signee and an early adopter of the real living wage – then they will have felt that benefit.”

City, which says it is innocent of the charges and has appealed against them, declined to comment.

The revelation comes as Burnham faced pressure over his relationship with City’s owners during his time as mayor of Greater Manchester. The prime minister was forced to clarify on Wednesday that he had two additional dinners with the club chair, Khaldoon al-Mubarak, at the Etihad Stadium, having previously declared those only as matchday hospitality.

Speaking at PMQs, Burnham said no one from the club had raised the Premier League charges with him.

Craig’s defence of the club came as her mayoral authority published details of Burnham’s contacts with City officials when he was mayor.

The release showed the prime minister had attended a formal meeting with al-Mubarak, chatted to him in the stands at a player’s testimonial game and was accompanied by staff from the club on official overseas visits.

But the Sun newspaper revealed later on Monday that Burnham had twice attended a pre-match dinner with the chair, which was declared in now-deleted council paperwork. No 10 said it was routine for the records to be deleted when a new mayor was in place.

View image in fullscreen Andy Burnham with Khaldoon al-Mubarak. Photograph: Martin Rickett/PA

Burnham’s initial response to the findings against City had drawn criticism after he said he would be “really concerned” if its Abu Dhabi owners sold the club in the wake of the Premier League findings, calling them a “huge partner in the building of modern Manchester”.

As the prime minister came under fire for his comments, Downing Street clarified that he believed where wrongdoing had been established, those responsible should face the consequences.

City attended the trade delegation alongside several other northern sports and leisure organisations, including Lancashire cricket club and Visit Lake District. While in India, the football club took part in an event in Delhi promoting British tourism.

The Great North – a coalition of mayors from the north of England which organised the India event – said its aim was “to shine a spotlight on the great tourism products across the north of England”.​

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to First Edition Our morning email breaks down the key stories of the day, telling you what’s happening and why it matters Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The Greater Manchester mayoral authority said on Tuesday that representatives of Greater Manchester sporting clubs would “routinely join business delegations” on international visits during Burnham’s time as mayor.

Burnham’s defence of City and its owners has focused attention not only on his links to the club but on how reliant he was on investment from Abu Dhabi to power Manchester’s strong growth rates when he was mayor.

View image in fullscreen Andy Burnham with Bev Craig after her victory in the Greater Manchester mayoral election. Photograph: Annabel Lee-Ellis/PA

Other senior politicians on this week’s trade delegation include Jonathan Reynolds, the business secretary, Douglas Alexander, the Scotland secretary, and Angela Eagle, the environment secretary.

Reynolds took part in a Premier League event on Tuesday, where he met schoolchildren being taught by British-trained coaches. He denied afterwards that the charges against City had tainted the league’s reputation. It is otherwise one of Britain’s most successful cultural exports.

“The brand of the Premier League – one of the UK’s most important brands … that is incredibly powerful,” he said.

Asked whether it was appropriate for City to have been invited, given the charges it faced, he said: “That’s a Greater Manchester issue, and obviously they are a major participant in the economy in Greater Manchester.

“I understand the interest – the relationship between Manchester and Manchester City – but in terms of the allegations, their appeal, that is a football matter.”

Sports.title: Millwall’s Alex Neil criticised for his comments on stoppage for alleged racism
Sports.content:
The Millwall head coach, Alex Neil, has been criticised by the anti-racism campaign group Kick It Out after complaining that a stoppage in play over alleged racist abuse “killed the momentum” in Tuesday’s home defeat to Swansea City.

The Championship fixture was suspended for around seven minutes after reports of abusive chants being aimed at the Swansea midfielder Eom Ji-sung. The referee, Edward Duckworth, halted the match in the 65th minute before speaking with both teams’ managers, the fourth official and a safety officer.

After the game, Neil told BBC Radio London: “I understand, obviously, there’s been an incident. That’s not something I’m going to get involved in, that’ll be for the authorities to deal with. But the fact that it stops the game, I just don’t see the point.

“The referee was wanting to speak to whoever the safety officer is, and when he spoke to him [the game] restarted. That’s partly my frustration. I want to get the game restarted, I want to get the game played. It needs to get dealt with … [but] stopping the game doesn’t deal with anything. All it does is kill the momentum.”

In a statement published on social media, Kick It Out said: “Player welfare should always take precedence over the momentum or flow of a match, and it’s essential that managers and all leaders recognise this and set the tone with their language so that everyone can stand up to discrimination.

“We’re disappointed to hear reports of racist abuse towards Swansea’s Eom Ji-sung during Tuesday’s Championship game at Millwall. Both clubs have condemned the incident, and it’s positive that Millwall and match officials followed the right protocols so that action can be taken to identify any individual responsible.”

The statement added: “Protocols are in place to help match and security officials respond appropriately. That ensures players are protected and key details are captured so that accountability can follow, regardless of how long it takes.”

View image in fullscreen The match referee, Edward Duckworth, speaks to both managers during the break in play. Photograph: Ben Whitley/PA

Millwall have not responded to the Kick it Out statement, but said on Tuesday: “The club operates a zero-tolerance policy towards any form of discriminatory abuse. Any individual found to have engaged in such behaviour will face the strongest possible action.

“The club is working alongside the relevant authorities to establish the facts and is unable to comment further as tonight’s alleged incident is the subject of an ongoing police investigation, which the club fully supports.”

Swansea won the game 1-0, with Ronald scoring a late winner after the restart, and Neil admitted afterwards: “If we score, I probably don’t feel this way.” The 45-year-old added that the alleged abuse “has been reported and it’s not acceptable.”

The Swansea head coach, Vítor Matos, praised the referee and Millwall’s club staff for their responses to the incident. “The referee followed the protocol for these sort of situations, they did the right thing,” he said.

“Millwall did the right thing by announcing there is no place for this sort of thing. I’m happy with how it was handled, but really sad that it happened.”

Sports.title: Crystal Palace's John Textor nightmare: BOBBY MANZI reveals the blazing rows with Steve Parish, his crumbling football empire and why Lyon can't stand him either
Sports.content:
Crystal Palace's John Textor nightmare: BOBBY MANZI reveals the blazing rows with Steve Parish, his crumbling football empire and why Lyon can't stand him either

When the full-time whistle went at Wembley and Crystal Palace had defied all the odds to win the FA Cup, John Textor leaned over a row of Royal Box seats to embrace Steve Parish.

After Eberechi Eze's goal won them the first trophy in their 120-year history, the image depicted an ownership group that was united and jubilant. In reality, their relationship was anything but.

On Thursday, Palace will reopen old wounds when they travel to Lyon for the Textor Derby. The disgraced former owner of both clubs will be nowhere to be seen and that's probably for the best, given the acrimony towards him in both France and south London.

Without his cross-Channel multi-club network, Palace may well have been playing in the Europa League last season. Instead they were demoted by virtue of no two clubs being able to play in the same UEFA competition and Nottingham Forest - now Public Enemy No1 in Croydon - took Palace's place. And the animosity extends beyond the supporters.

Textor arrived at Palace in August 2021, acquiring the largest minority stake in the club for £87.5million before increasing his shareholding to 43 per cent three years later. Yet, despite his attempts, Textor failed to convert his equity into control. On several occasions, he tried to purchase a majority stake but was consistently blocked.

That irked him. Chairman Parish, the club's ultimate decision-maker despite owning significantly less of it than Textor, angered him. Textor deemed Parish risk-averse, while Parish viewed Textor as a risk to the club. But Parish had the measure of him, using the Missouri-born former competitive skateboarder's capital to pay off debt during Covid, develop the academy site and strengthen the playing squad without giving him decision-making power.

Former Crystal Palace director John Textor (left) had regular slanging matches with fellow part-owner Steve Parish (right)

Textor's ownership of Lyon meant that Palace were kicked out of the Europa League last season, as no two teams in the same competition can have the same controlling partner

Meanwhile, Textor wanted Palace to be the cornerstone of his multi-club ownership group, Eagle Football, which owned Lyon, Brazilian top-flight side Botafogo and the now-defunct RWD Molenbeek of Belgium. Given that Textor has since lost all the clubs amid financial mismanagement, Parish's wariness has been vindicated.

Textor wanted Parish to prioritise the playing squad and was aggrieved by ring-fencing cash for Selhurst Park's new Main Stand. Some believe Textor never supported the development, with the issue often prompting bust-ups.

In fact, sources told Daily Mail Sport that Parish and Textor had regular slanging matches in the boardroom while employees were present. One source recalled occasions when Textor stormed out, explaining that the pair clashed over their respective self-righteousness.

Publicly, Parish and Textor mostly put on a united front, though Textor made some snide digs about the 'red Ferrari driving chairman' in an interview with talkSPORT. Behind the scenes, however, the pair never hid their dislike or the tension between them – and Textor eventually lost much of his interest in Palace after realising his sway was limited and he could not further his multi-club network ambitions.

The most disruptive period came during Textor's exit. He had been looking to sell for some time but the process was accelerated after the FA Cup win granted Palace entry into the Europa League for the following campaign, where the Lyon problem reared its head.

There was perhaps another reason for Textor's expediency. Lyon had problems of their own - the seven-times French champions were in the process of being kicked out of Ligue 1 by the French football authorities (DNCG).

But when Textor's money came in from selling his Palace stake to Woody Johnson, the former US Ambassador to the UK and owner of the NFL's New York Jets, they satisfied the DNCG's demands and were reinstated not just to the French top flight but also the Europa League.

So in the end, selling Palace and releasing them from the multi-club network resulted in Lyon taking their Europa League place. Palace were demoted to the Conference League - which they went on to win to again qualify for the Europa League - because Textor still had 'decisive influence' on the March 1, 2025 deadline for ownership conflicts to be resolved for the following season.

Palace fans had voiced their distrust of Textor long before the multi-club ownership issue hit them hard - with this banner in January 2023

Textor (centre) owned around 40 per cent of Palace from August 2021 to July 2025, when he sold his stake to New York Jets owner and former US Ambassador to the UK Woody Johnson

To this day, Textor is one of three parties Palace supporters blame for their expulsion, alongside Nottingham Forest owner Evangelos Marinakis and UEFA.

'F*** UEFA, f*** John Textor, f*** Marinakis' has become a staple chant at matches and will almost certainly be heard throughout the match at the Groupama Stadium on Thursday night.

Textor has both publicly and privately suggested that supporters are naive for blaming him. Of course, the Europa League demotion is the emotional source of their frustration. However, the Textor resentment originated in concerns over his ambition to put Eagle Football Holdings on the stock market and fears over whether he had suitable funding.

Having previously held stakes in four clubs, Textor now has none.

Palace and Lyon are under new management, Botafogo voted him off their board this summer a few months after the club were hit with a three-window transfer ban for non-payment of a transfer fee, and Molenbeek lost their Belgian football league licence in August over financial difficulties. At the top of it all, Eagle Football Holdings went into administration in March.

It should be said that Palace had not planned well enough for the possibility of playing European football. Had they done so, Textor's shares could have been placed in a blind trust before the deadline and the situation avoided. Whether Textor would have agreed to that while trying to sell up, though, is another matter.

Intriguingly, one Palace source defended Textor when speaking to Daily Mail Sport. The source argued that Textor was the driving force behind Palace appointing Oliver Glasner two years ago and that the investment he made helped to pay for the signings of Marc Guehi and Michael Olise, suggesting that none of Palace's three trophies in the last 18 months would have been possible without the American. That is an unpopular opinion among fans to say the least, though.

Even after his exit, there remains a tenuous link to the club. John Textor's son, Addison, is employed by Velocity Capital – an American private equity firm owned by minority Palace shareholder David Abrams. The firm invested more than £75m in leading football agency Unique Sports Group, which represents past and present Palace players Dean Henderson, Maxence Lacroix, Marc Guehi and Dwight McNeil.

Under Textor's ownership, Botafogo won the Copa Libertadores in 2024 but he was voted off the club's board in July this year

One source argued that Textor was the driving force behind Palace appointing Oliver Glasner, and as such none of Palace's three trophies in the last 18 months would have been possible

It was Textor who appointed now-Palace boss Pierre Sage as Lyon head coach in 2023. He led them to the French Cup final in his first season but was sacked the following January

Palace fans will use their trip to Lyon to lambast Textor once again and the home crowd is likely to join in. Although Lyon's involvement prevented Palace from competing in the Europa League, there is no bitterness between the two clubs – both equally disdain Textor.

Lyon endured persistent battles with the DNCG thanks to Textor building up debt, the provisional relegation last summer and being forced to sell key players because of their financial situation. Ironically, supporters also fumed over his decision to sack now-Palace boss Pierre Sage, a decision Textor admits he now regrets.

When Palace won the Conference League to qualify for the Europa League last season, they were almost destined to face Lyon.

This is the final chapter in their Textor debacle and, unless it's in their favourite chant, everyone at Palace will hope Thursday night is the last time he enters their thoughts.

Sports.title: Channelling your inner Phil Brown, Nuno? Unhappy West Ham boss Espirito Santo delivers half-time team-talk ON THE PITCH as they struggle at nine-man Lincoln - as Hammers eventually win 6-0 after his words!
Sports.content:
Channelling your inner Phil Brown, Nuno? Unhappy West Ham boss Espirito Santo delivers half-time team-talk ON THE PITCH as they struggle at nine-man Lincoln - as Hammers eventually win 6-0 after his words!

West Ham boss Nuno Espirito Santo delivered a Phil Brown-esque half-time team-talk away at Lincoln on Wednesday night... and it seems to have been a stroke of genius.

Premier League fans of a certain vintage will fondly remember former Hull City manager Brown's iconic team-talk away at Manchester City in 2008, but it seems to have caught on in the Championship, 18 years later.

The bizarrely comedic moment is one that sticks in the mind of every fan luckily enough to witness it.

Nuno must be spending his days off watching Premier League Years on TV. With his side only 1-0 up after playing against a nine-man Lincoln team for the best part of the first half, he thought an on-field talking to would be the perfect way to whip them into shape.

And what do you know? It did. Nobody except the Hammers' staff and players will know what Nuno said but whatever it was it did the trick. West Ham came out looking like a completely different side in the second half and scored five more, demolishing Championship new boys Lincoln City.

The Irons will hope this will be another three points towards promotion and that they won't have to travel to the ProAmpac Stadium again next season but, if they were to, Jarrod Bowen and Co might think of pulling a Jimmy Bullard and recreating Nuno's team-talk as part of a celebration.

Unlike Brown, Nuno's stern approach go the job done as West ham got their fifth win of the campaign

Phil Brown delivered his legendary on-field half time team talk back in 2008

Brown delivered his infamous team talk on Boxing day in 2008 but there was nothing cheery about it at the time. He masterminded Hull's first ever promotion to the Premier League in the season prior by winning the play offs in dramatic fashion, and went on to enjoy a fine start to the 2008-09 Premier League season.

After nine games and six wins the Tigers were sat joint top of the Premier League table going into the final game of October, but this form did not last. The next nine games saw just one win and four defeats and pressure began to mount on Brown.

And on Boxing Day the red mist descended. After 45 minutes away at Manchester City they were 4-0 down and an incensed Brown was so disappointed with his squad he humiliated them by making them sit on the turf and take a tongue lashing in front of their travelling fans.

For the neutral it was a strange yet hilarious moment and unfortunately for the Tigers had no effect on the final score, as City ran out 5-1 winners.

Sports.title: Defiant Enzo Maresca believes Man City are at the same level as PSG despite 4-2 Champions League defeat - as boss insists he sees 'many good things'
Sports.content:
Enzo Maresca claimed that Manchester City should be close to challenging for the Champions League this season after losing a European classic against Paris Saint-Germain. City’s first game back at the Etihad Stadium since being found guilty of breaching financial rules was watched by Pep Guardiola as they went down 4-2 to the defending champions. Guardiola sat in the directors’ box behind chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak as a show of support for the club heading into their appeal during the largest legal case in British sporting history. Maresca saw Erling Haaland net a brace to leapfrog Sergio Aguero as the club’s record scorer in the Champions League but they could not complete a dramatic comeback from three goals down. The Italian, however, believes there is evidence that his team can place themselves in the mix to lift this trophy amid the threat of huge sporting sanctions by the Premier League domestically. ‘We are there, we are close,’ Maresca said. ‘I really like to play against PSG. They are brave. I know the way they want to press. They don’t care, they are quite dynamic, go man to man. Enzo Maresca believes Man City should be close to challenging for the Champions League this season despite a 4-2 home defeat by PSG Man City were stunned in the first half as PSG raced into a 3-0 lead at the Etihad Pep Guardiola watched in the stands on his return, as he showed support for the club heading into their appeal during the largest legal case in British sporting history ‘[PSG manager] Luis [Enrique] said to me they had been quite lucky during the 90 minutes. We lost, we move on.’ Maresca apologised to the City supporters for a first-half display which saw them trail 3-0 at the break but believes there was reason for optimism thereafter. While rejecting the idea that the toil of the past fortnight, and the emotion of Sunday’s victory at Anfield, affected his players as they conceded twice in 99 seconds, Maresca did suggest his team will need to keep mentally switched on in future ties against Europe’s best. ‘We can learn many things from the game,’ he added. ‘That even if we concede two against the best team in Europe, we (should) keep doing the right things. ‘Against this kind of team it’s already difficult. We lost balance, the distance between players. The reason we struggled in the first half is when we conceded… you think “oh my God, we are 2-0 down”. ‘But I have only been here three months and see many good things.’

Sports.title: Plenty to smile about, your highness! Prince William celebrates wildly as his beloved Aston Villa score SIX goals in Champions League clash against Fenerbahce
Sports.content:
A delighted Prince William was seen celebrating in the stands as Aston Villa earned a dominant 6-0 victory in their Champions League tie against Fenerbahce.

The Prince of Wales – who has supported Villa since his school days – was watching on as Unai Emery's side took on the Turkish giants in their second league phase match.

Prince William punched the air in delight as Aston Villa took an early lead through summer signing Johan Manzambi.

Aston Villa doubled the advantage on the half hour mark through Nicolas Jackson, with the forward adding a third before half-time.

The home side's dominance continued in the second half with Ross Barkley scoring twice, the first from the penalty spot, before Tammy Abraham added a last sixth.

The result saw Aston Villa continue their perfect start in the league phase of the Champions League, with Emery's side having won their opening two fixtures.

Prince William celebrated as Aston Villa made a superb start to the Champions League tie

Prince William watched on as Aston Villa raced into a 3-0 lead before half-time against Fenerbahce

The Prince of Wales continued his wild celebrations as Aston Villa score three in the second half

Aston Villa continued their perfect start to the Champions League by thrashing Fenerbahce

Prince William has been a regular presence at Villa Park in recent years and attended matches throughout their run to winning the Europa League last season.

He had joined players and staff following their triumph in the final in Istanbul back in May, after Emery's side claimed the club's first European trophy in 44 years.

Aston Villa's Europa League success saw the club qualify for their year's Champions League, where Prince William will be hoping for a similarly successful European run.

A die-hard Villa supporter since his school days, William once explained how he chose the club while studying in Berkshire, resisting the pull of more popular teams.

'A long time ago at school I got into football big time. I was looking around for clubs. All my friends were either Man United fans or Chelsea fans and I didn’t want to follow the run-of-the-mill teams,' he told the BBC in 2015.

'I wanted to have a team that was more mid-table that could give me more emotional rollercoaster moments.

'Aston Villa’s always had a great history. I have got friends of mine who support Aston Villa and one of the first FA Cup games I went to was Bolton v Aston Villa back in 2000. Sadly, Villa went on to lose to Chelsea (in the final),' he said

'It was fantastic, I sat with all the fans with my red beanie on, and I was with all the Brummie fans and had a great time.

'It was the atmosphere, the camaraderie and I really felt that there was something I could connect with.'

Sports.title: Kristaps Porzingis denies having 'HIV or AIDS' as NBA star addresses mystery absence from Warriors for health reasons
Sports.content:
Kristaps Porzingis denies having 'HIV or AIDS' as NBA star addresses mystery absence from Warriors for health reasons

Kristaps Porzingis has responded to ongoing speculation about his health after his mystery absence from the Golden State Warriors throughout preseason.

The NBA veteran, 31, has been away from the team and ruled out indefinitely due to an undisclosed health issue ahead of the new season but has now returned to the facility.

The situation has sparked much speculation and wild theories about why the Latvian has not been on the court.

It has led him to provide an update on social media and insist: 'I don't have HIV or AIDS' in a direct response to baseless suggestions from 'internet doctors' trying to weigh in.

Porzingis wrote: 'Hello people, I'm working with doctors and experts to figure out how to be fully back to good health asap.

'Honestly, I'm getting better and better. I just have to stay patient, and I believe I'll be feeling great again soon.

Kristaps Porzingis has provided an update on his health after being away from the team

Porzingis signed a two-year, $40M contract with the Golden State Warriors earlier this year

'It has definitely been frustrating dealing with some health stuff that you can't exactly pinpoint, on top of injuries throughout my career, so it has added up for sure, but we will get through it

'Health is wealth. Thank you for all the support. I appreciate all the internet doctors trying to diagnose and help, but I'm in the best hands.

'So everyone can relax now...and I don't have HIV or AIDS.'

Porzingis provided the update via his social media after the Golden State Warriors issued a statement on his situation before a preseason win over the Los Angeles Lakers.

The team said: 'Golden State Warriors forward/center Kristaps Porzingis, who missed training camp and the team's first five (5) preseason games due to a health-related matter, returned to the Warriors' practice facility yesterday and met with Warriors General Manager Mike Dunleavy and Vice President of Player Health & Performance Dr. Rick Celebrini.

'The specific contents of that meeting will remain private. Porzingis will remain out indefinitely due to the same health-related matter but will be around the team.

'An update on his status, including the potential resumption of practice, playing status, or timeline, will be provided when available and appropriate.'

Porzingis signed a two-year, $40 million contract with the Warriors earlier this summer, with the second year being a player option.

Golden State begins their new season on October 21 against the Lakers in Los Angeles, with Porzingis' status as yet unclear as Steve Kerr hopes he can play a big role this upcoming season.

Sports.title: Mason Greenwood booed by Aston Villa fans as former Man United star plays in England for the first time in over FOUR years - after Old Trafford career unravelled following rape arrest
Sports.content:
Mason Greenwood booed by Aston Villa fans as former Man United star plays in England for the first time in over FOUR years - after Old Trafford career unravelled following rape arrest

Mason Greenwood was booed repeatedly on his first appearance in an English football stadium since 2022.

Greenwood joined the Turkish giants for £36million from Marseille last summer after being cut from the United first team when he was arrested and charged with attempted rape, assault and controlling and coercive behaviour in October 2022, before charges and the case were dropped in February 2023 when key witnesses withdrew. He has denied any wrongdoing.

The former Manchester United player was one of Fenerbahce’s highest-profile signings last summer and he has history with Aston Villa.

Greenwood’s name was booed when the teams were announced and Villa supporters targeted him with chants and catcalls whenever he touched the ball in the early stages.

Operating on the right of Fener’s attack, Greenwood was facing his former Manchester United team-mate Aaron Wan-Bissaka, who had switched to left-back with Ian Maatsen and Matteo Ruggeri injured.

There were tussles with Wan-Bissaka in the early exchanges, with Greenwood occasionally dropping much deeper to receive the ball. In the 19th minute, after a burst by the lively Oguz Aydin, Greenwood steered a shot from 20 yards straight at Zion Suzuki.

Mason Greenwood (pictured) was roundly booed by Aston Villa fans tonight

He has a solitary England cap, from a Nations League meeting in Iceland in September 2020. He is also eligible for Jamaica but last year he decided against accepting the call from then-boss Steve McClaren. Before tonight, Greenwood had six goals in 14 appearances for the Istanbul giants.

He played 69 minutes in total as his side were humbled at Villa Park, losing 3-0.

This was not the first time Greenwood had crossed swords with Villa, having been hurled to the ground by Tyrone Mings during a pre-season friendly against Marseille in August 2025, following an altercation with Villa midfielder Amadou Onana. Greenwood, 25, was perhaps grateful that the 6ft 5ins Onana missed this match due to injury.

Sports.title: Lisandro Martinez admits he 'spoke out of anger and frustration' during bombshell interview criticising Man United hierarchy - as Argentine insists he 'believes in everyone' but fails to say sorry in 271-word statement
Sports.content:
Lisandro Martinez took to social media in a late bid to dilute his scathing comments 24 hours on from his blistering criticism of club bosses.

United’s players had Wednesday off after flying straight back from Spain following Tuesday’s Champions League defeat to Atletico Madrid and Martinez’s bombshell television interview in which he accused the Old Trafford board and director of football Jason Wilcox of failing in the transfer market last summer.

United remained tight-lipped on what action – if any – was to be taken against the Argentina international ahead of a return to training, but it the defender took matters into his own hands by explaining – but crucially not apologising – what he meant.

‘When I talk about wanting more, I’m talking about the ambition we must all have as part of this club,’ Martinez said, in part of his statement.

‘To keep growing, to become stronger and to have everything we need to compete at the highest level. These are standards we must all hold ourselves to, starting with me.’

He added: ‘We need to demand even more of ourselves and work together to take Manchester United back to the top. I believe in my team-mates, our manager and everyone working to help this club move forward.

Lisandro Martinez has broken his silence after Tuesday night's extraordinary post-match rant

‘I’m convinced that the way forward is to keep working together, with ambition and commitment. My goal has been the same since day one, to win, to compete at the highest level and to give everything I have for this badge.’

The impact of Martinez’s initial statement is still likely to be felt through until Sunday’s trip to face Leeds United at Elland Road, while team-mate Amad Diallo is also in the spotlight after he added more fuel to the fire with a message on social media which read ‘f***ing disgrace, I have no words’, although it’s unclear what the Ivorian was referring to.

United will likely need to call on Martinez at Leeds with a number of injuries in defence. Luke Shaw, Patrick Dorgu and Noussair Mazraoui have been out of action, and Matthijs De Ligt only returned on the bench as an unused substitute in Madrid after nearly a year out with a back injury.

Martinez’s long-term future is more uncertain, however. He is out of contract at the end of June, although United can extend it by another year.

They are unlikely to let a 28-year-old World Cup winner leave as a free agent five years after his £57million move from Ajax, but could trigger the extension so they can demand a transfer fee for him.

Martinez took aim at the United hierarchy in the wake of a fourth defeat in nine games in Madrid when he was asked if the club have backed Michael Carrick enough. ‘I don't think so,’ he said. ‘He does his best. You can't keep changing, changing, changing the manager.

‘What about other areas? Tonight it is easy to say the coach and easy to say the players, but also we have to see other areas.

‘I expect more (investment) 100 per cent. I expect more from our technical director. I have to be honest, as players we have to do more but it is also important when you make a strong squad to be ready for this kind of night.

‘I have to control myself a lot but sometimes is a reflection of the mirror of how is our club at the moment.’

Sports.title: Pep Guardiola returns to Manchester City: Legendary former boss attends PSG clash after insisting he will 'always be behind' former club following Premier League's bombshell cheating verdict
Sports.content:
Pep Guardiola returns to Manchester City: Legendary former boss attends PSG clash after insisting he will 'always be behind' former club following Premier League's bombshell cheating verdict

Pep Guardiola has returned to Manchester City for the first time since his emotional farewell in the summer, with his former club marooned in the biggest scandal in English football history.

The Spaniard, who won six Premier League titles during his ten-year stint in Manchester, threw his support behind his former side as they took on Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League on Wednesday night.

Guardiola was sat in Manchester City's directors' box for the tie, seated two rows behind chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak and chief executive Ferran Soriano.

The 55-year-old watched on as his former side fell 3-0 down to reigning European champions PSG in the first half and ultimately succumbing to a 4-2 defeat despite a spirited display in the second.

Guardiola has been replaced by Enzo Maresca, with the new boss now having to contend with the explosive fallout of the Premier League bombshell verdict, in which City have been found guilty of the vast majority of the 115 charges against them.

The era covering the charges - from 2009 to 2018 - laid the foundations for Guardiola's huge success at the Etihad Stadium, and has called into question the legendary manager's legacy as a result.

City have strenuously denied any wrongdoing and have launched an appeal against the verdict, while Guardiola took to Instagram in the wake of the findings to publicly back his former club.

Pep Guardiola has returned to Manchester City for the first time since leaving the club

Guardiola was seated two rows behind Man City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak and chief executive Ferran Soriano

Man City chairman Khaldoon warmly embraced PSG chief executive Nasser Al-Khelaifi before the match

'I want every single Manchester City fan across the world to know I am here; more than ever. I am, always have been, always will be behind my club, my owner, my chairman, Ferran, the players, staff, Enzo and you, our unique supporters.

'Let me be clear: we will get through this together.

'I love you all.'

City received an overwhelmingly positive reception in their first match back at the Etihad following the seismic verdict, with supporters rallying around the club despite the sheer volume of charges found against the Premier League leaders.

Prior to kick-off, Man City fans created a tifo reading 'CTID', meaning 'City 'til I die'.

Maresca's side were treated to an altogether more hostile welcome by Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday, in their first competitive fixture since the guilty findings.

But the visitors rode the early storm to run away with a convincing 3-0 victory, with their jubilant celebrations the subject of criticism from the watching football world.

Erling Haaland, Jeremy Doku and Rayan Cherki all scored in the space of 13 second-half minutes, with wild scenes in front of an exuberant away end.

Maresca danced down the touchline and stuck fingers in his ears, with staff and players branded arrogant by their detractors.

Maresca hit back at critics before their Champions League tie against Paris Saint-Germain at the Etihad.

'Criticised for what?' he said. 'We won 3-0 at Anfield! What do you want us to do? And even if it was 0-1, it would be exactly the same.

'I'm here today, and the players are here today, to win tomorrow's game. And we work every day to win games. It's the only thing, again, that we can think and be focussed.

'The rest? It's just things from outside that we need to deal with, but we were so, so, so happy inside the pitch, and you cannot imagine inside the changing room.'

Maresca added: 'We were very happy, sharing time with our fans. Probably it's been more tough for our fans than our players or for me.

Guardiola watched on as his former side went 3-0 down to European champions PSG in the first half

Man City players huddled on the pitch after going 3-0 down and ultimately suffered a 4-2 loss

Man City fans made a display reading 'CTID' - City 'til I die - before the Champions League tie

'It's more complicated for them because if I am an Arsenal fan or Utd fan, I look at City fans and say 'hey my friend, you are a cheat'. Inside the changing room we were very happy because we knew how difficult Anfield is. Anfield was unbelievable.'

City skipper Ruben Dias stood behind Maresca's words – and claimed they will continue to celebrate with passion.

'We'll celebrate however we feel in the moment,' Dias said. 'It'll be a show of how much things mean to us.

'Yes there is a lot of noise and it's almost impossible to not see something – even us being so private. But I feel like we're also very good at focusing on ourselves.

'You build yourself against any kind of noise. I feel like I speak for the whole group when I say we're very calm. We trust the club. We know the team we've got and want to win. It's the same noise as before because people don't love us.'

Sports.title: Man City charges news: Pep Guardiola returns as appeal and punishment timeline emerges
Sports.content:
Thierry Henry says the qualities of Man City's heroes will remain, irrespective of any punishment.

He said: "I don't have to go back to what I'm thinking, the world of football but what I know is I'm not qualified to talk about what comes next (or) what the punishment is going to be. I'm not a judge, definitely not a lawyer, I always say, 'stay in your lane'.

"At one point, we talked about fans, a lot of people, the great players we've seen wearing that journey, I used to look at City and think, 'wow'.

"I feel sorry for them because it has nothing to do with them, they don't know what happened. Whatever outcome, punishment, it's not what I believe (but) it's always going to be, 'ah, did you really win?' That's unfair for those guys, Vincent Kompany was a hell of a player, Kevin de Bruyne was a hell of a player.

"There is a procedure that we have to respect, the facts are the fact, yes when they've been found guilty and when you appeal it doesn't erase everything but it gives hope that maybe you might not be guilty. I respect everyone's opinion, we've talked about a lot of things but those great players, for me, will always be great regardless of what the punishment will be."

Sports.title: Lisandro Martinez reiterates 'anger and frustration' in follow-up to bombshell interview
Sports.content:
Lisandro Martinez reiterates 'anger and frustration' in follow-up to bombshell interview

Lisandro Martinez has come out with a fresh statement in the aftermath of his fiery interview, where the Manchester United defender took aim at senior figures over a lack of ambition

View 2 Images Lisandro Martinez has attempted to explain his rant on Tuesday night

Lisandro Martinez's post-match rant on Tuesday has split the Manchester United squad with players divided as the defender released a fresh statement admitting he spoke in "anger and frustration" - but doubling down on his desire for more.

‌



‌



In the aftermath of another loss for the Red Devils, who went down 2-0 at Atletico Madrid, their Argentine defender let rip at the hierarchy, specifically director of football Jason Wilcox, regarding a lack of investment in the summer.

‌



Martinez was keen to make the point that, whilst the players and manager Michael Carrick need to take some responsibility of the run of poor results, he feels they have not been suitably equipped to fight on all fronts after an impressive period of results last season.

‌



United's return to Europe, coupled with the domestic competitions, was always going to place more onus on resources and Martinez said in a bombshell interview: "I expect more [investment]. 100%. I expect more from our technical director. I have to be honest, as players we have to do more but it is also important when you make a strong squad to be ready for this kind of night. Tonight it is easy to [blame] the coach, easy to say the players but also we have to see other areas."

‌



Martinez came out late on Wednesday night and put out some words on his social media account, explaining his comments and his reaction.

He admits he "spoke out in anger and frustration" but added: "When I talk about wanting more, I'm talking about the ambition we must all have as part of this club. To keep growing, to become stronger and to have everything we need to compete at the highest level. These are standards we must all hold ourselves to, starting with me.

"I know that, first and foremost, it's us, the players, who have to deliver, and I put myself at the front of that responsibility. We need to demand even more of ourselves and work together to take Manchester United back to the top.

‌



"I believe in my teammates, our manager and everyone working to help this club move forward. I'm convinced that the way forward is to keep working together, with ambition and commitment."

View 2 Images Man Utd's players have been divided over whether to back Lisandro Martinez

The Sun reports that some players have appreciated Martinez's willingness to be so honest, with his comments ultimately him defending his manager, who is under mounting pressure.

‌



Other teammates have been reluctant to side with the defender however. One senior player feels Martinez’s comments changed the coverage of United’s loss to Atletico with many feeling as if they played well despire the loss. Another believes the absence of certain teammates has affected the harmony in the squad.

It was well documented that United did miss out on a host of targets in the summer. Several of those, including the likes of Elliot Anderson, were players they chose not to pursue due to their sky high valuations.

Midfield was ultimately the only area that was strengthened with no forwards or defenders coming in, which already looks a poor move with Carrick having to work with a backline that has had no new arrivals for several summers.
