Sports.title: Fabio Wardley Puts Rematch Pressure on Daniel Dubois
Sports.content:
Fabio Wardley believes Daniel Dubois faces the greater pressure in their rematch, with the champion needing to repeat his victory against a challenger who believes he has corrected the mistakes that cost him their first fight.

Dubois recovered from two early knockdowns to win. Wardley admits he became overconfident after that success, giving the champion an opportunity to recover. If Wardley avoids those mistakes, Dubois could face a different task this time.

“I think that for me, like again, it’s something Daniel’s gone through, but now he’s got three losses on his record,” Wardley told Fight Wire. “Two of those to Oleksandr Usyk, so you chalk them up a bit differently.”

Wardley argues that another defeat would put Dubois in a difficult position, while he views his own first loss as something he can repair.

“It just frees me up. It’s okay, we had a loss. Things didn’t go too great. Not the end of the world,” he said.

The pressure on Dubois goes beyond the number of defeats. He needs to demonstrate that his previous victory was repeatable, rather than a result that depended on Wardley getting careless after putting him down twice.

Wardley believes he has identified how he let that opportunity slip. Better decisions could leave Dubois with fewer chances to recover, although maintaining pressure without wasting energy or walking into punches will require more than determination.

“There’s a few adjustments to be made, a few things we need to capitalize on better, and then the fight’s ours,” Wardley said.

Dubois proved he could beat Wardley that night. Whether he can handle a more disciplined version remains unanswered. Wardley still has to deliver those improvements under fire, but the champion cannot assume the same openings will appear again.

Wardley also questioned Dubois’s conflicting comments about his punching power, suggesting some of his opponent’s remarks sound rehearsed.

“Especially when the camera comes out, some of the lines you can very much tell are forced, or they’ve at least been told to him to put in there,” he said.

The verbal sparring adds to Wardley’s portrayal of himself as the more relaxed fighter. Dubois’s harder task is showing that he has answers for the changes Wardley brings into the ring.

Sports.title: Edgar Berlanga Calls Sebastian Fundora A Cheat Code
Sports.content:
Edgar Berlanga can’t understand how Sebastian Fundora fits into the 154-pound division. Looking at a workout photo of the WBC champion, he compared Fundora to a video game character and suggested he should be making his money in the NBA.

Fundora’s long legs and arms dominate the picture. Berlanga fights two divisions above him at super middleweight, yet even he sounds taken aback by the sight of someone that tall competing at light middleweight.

How do they allow him to box at 154lb he’s a cheat code character from GTA WTF 🤣🤣🤣 listen he would have been a 200 million dollar NBA player. This is unacceptable he looks like a building https://t.co/AYW3y9aSuM — Edgar Berlanga Jr (@EdgarBerlangaJr) October 15, 2026

Berlanga isn’t the first fighter to reach for a video game comparison. After Fundora stopped Erickson Lubin in April 2022, Terence Crawford called him “a cheat code,” comparing him to a created Fight Night boxer with the height turned up in a smaller weight class.

It’s an understandable reaction. Finding sparring partners who can prepare an opponent for Fundora is difficult enough. Then comes the task of getting past those long arms and landing on a head that sits well above the usual target.

The odd thing is that Fundora often gives opponents a chance by coming to them. He likes fighting up close, throwing short punches rather than spending every round keeping shorter men at the end of his jab. They don’t always have to chase him to get their shots off.

That makes him entertaining, even if Berlanga thinks his dimensions look unfair. Fundora can make 154. The men across from him have to figure out the rest.

His WBC title defense against Ermal Hadribeaj this Saturday is a harder sell. Hadribeaj is the mandatory challenger, but most fans know little about him. They’re waiting to see Fundora against the bigger names in a division with plenty to offer.

Hadribeaj gets his chance to make himself known once the fight starts. Until then, Fundora’s unusual frame is likely to draw more conversation than the matchup itself.

Sports.title: Liam Paro Faces Long Wait For Ryan Garcia
Sports.content:
Liam Paro booking another defense puts more distance between him and Ryan Garcia, though Garcia’s alternative choices present a far bigger hurdle. Matchups with Teofimo Lopez or Devin Haney carry massive commercial appeal, which could strand Paro well past his ideal timeline.

“We’re not going to sit on the sideline,” Paro told Fox Sports Australia.

Staying active is the smartest move Paro can make. Continuing to take bouts keeps him sharp instead of burning months chasing an opponent who sees little urgency to fight him.

Teofimo gives Garcia an established American audience. A return bout with Haney carries built-in personal drama. Paro holds a world championship belt, yet hardware alone might not outweigh the bigger paydays Garcia could chase instead.

The calendar for Ryan creates another headache. If Garcia sits out until May, that single appearance eats up the first half of 2027. Another high-profile date could easily swallow the remaining months, leaving Paro on the outside looking in despite handling his business in the ring.

Teofimo’s mandatory duty against Jack Catterall adds some problems, but it will not kill a potential Garcia meeting. The WBA might grant Teofimo an exception so he can keep the strap. Teofimo could also surrender the belt outright to lock down the more lucrative bout.

That situation does not assure Teofimo gets the nod. Still, Paro cannot count on sanctioning body politics to eliminate a popular name from contention.

Title dynamics bring further chaos. If Garcia meets Teofimo first, Paro must hope Garcia wins so the WBC unification prize remains intact. A Garcia loss instantly ruins that scenario before Paro ever secures a signed contract.

Paro holds the power to defend his title and keep his phone line open. He cannot dictate Garcia’s opponent, dictate fight results, or force Garcia to pursue undisputed status.

Taking another bout makes complete sense. Chasing Garcia is worth the ambition, but Paro must build an active calendar that keeps rolling even if Garcia never calls. Paro landing that fight in 2027 makes zero sense from Ryan’s financial perspective.

Ryan operates purely on box office scale. A return match with Devin Haney already has massive public heat, personal grudge, and built-in history that sells pay-per-view buys effortlessly. A fight with Teofimo Lopez brings two huge American fanbases together for an absolute blockbuster. Those two events generate monster gates. Paro simply cannot generate that kind of revenue in the United States.

On top of the financial gap, Paro presents a terrible risk profile for Ryan. Paro is a tough southpaw with an awkward style who makes life miserable inside the ring. Taking on that kind of stylistic headache for a fraction of the money Ryan can make elsewhere is bad business. Fighters in Ryan’s tax bracket do not volunteer for difficult nights unless huge checks back it up.

Then you have the calendar reality. Ryan is not fighting four times a year. If he takes a marquee date in the spring, that eats up the first half of 2027. A massive fall date takes care of the rest. Between Teofimo, Haney, or other lucrative names floating around, 2027 fills up instantly.

Paro holding a title belt does not move the needle for Ryan either. Ryan transcended the need for sanctioning body belts long ago because his name alone drives the promotion.

Sports.title: Carlos Adames Approval Leaves Meiirim Nursultanov Waiting
Sports.content:
Carlos Adames got the green light to take an interim bout before dealing with mandatory challenger Meiirim Nursultanov. The WBC approved a November 17 date above 160 pounds, but it includes a massive catch. If Adames loses, he loses his middleweight world title on the spot, even with the belt not officially on the line.

The WBC confirmed the ruling in an October 14 update. They left out the opponent, the venue, plus the exact weight limit. Because of that, nobody knows how tough this assignment will actually be.

Meiirim Nursultanov gets stuck waiting again. Holding the mandatory slot didn’t lock down his crack at the belt. Now he has to sit back, hoping Adames survives this detour so their scheduled clash can take place.

It puts Nursultanov in a weird spot. If Adames wins, Nursultanov still gets his shot at the active champion. If Adames stumbles, the title gets stripped, which leaves the top contender waiting on fresh orders for a vacant belt.

The WBC laid out clear terms. An Adames win routes him directly into the Nursultanov defense. Whoever walks away with the victory there has to face interim titlist Jesús Ramos Jr next.

There is a road map to clean up the division, but getting there takes three separate bouts. Every detour before the mandatory introduces the threat of an injury or an upset that blows up the entire schedule.

NEWS: Per sources, Carlos Adames’ @Zuffa_Boxing debut in a nontitle bout OK’d by the WBC is planned for November in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, where Zuffa is planning a show in November & one in December (obviously depends on status of the war & unrest in the region). #boxing — Dan Rafael (@DanRafael1) October 15, 2026

That vacant title rule also creates a bizarre setup for whoever steps into the ring on November 17. If the opponent beats the middleweight champ, Adames loses the belt, yet the winner walks away empty-handed without claiming it. Anyone signing that contract needs to realize what a victory actually delivers.

Adames lands the flexibility he wanted, while Nursultanov collects yet another promise about future dates. Until the promotion names a foe, nobody can tell if Adames is taking a dangerous test or just booking a tune-up above middleweight. Either way, Nursultanov stays on the sidelines waiting for his turn.

It sends a terrible message when a sanctioning body lets a champion put their mandatory obligations on ice just to chase an untitle bout above the weight class.

The whole point of a mandatory challenger is that you earn the number one spot through actual ring results, not politics. Nursultanov did the work, secured the position, and now he is forced to sit on the shelf watching the champion go hunt for bigger money elsewhere.

Nursultanov is not getting compensated while Adames takes this detour. Time away from the ring burns prime years, brings zero purse money, and creates ring rust. If Adames gets hurt on November 17, the layoff stretches out even longer. If Adames loses, Nursultanov does not even get the satisfaction or the profile boost of taking down the sitting champion. He gets stuck in a vacant title match that generates far less fanfare and a smaller check.

Sports.title: Sebastian Fundora Rules Out Saudi Arabia For Boots Fight
Sports.content:
Sebastian Fundora wants the winner of Jaron Ennis against Josh Kelly next, but the WBC junior middleweight champion insists Saudi Arabia will not host it. Fundora aims for spring 2027 to stage a unification bout, making it clear that facing Boots will not convince him to travel abroad to Riyadh.

That stance sets a firm condition on his future plans before his title defense against Ermal Hadribeaj on Saturday. Fundora expects Ennis to defeat Kelly, calling Boots the premier matchup at 154 pounds.

“I think the winner of Boots and Kelly should be the opponent for our next fight,” Fundora said to Ariel Helwani. “I think that’s early, early maybe springtime of next year, 2027.” Asked whether that reflected discussions or simply his preference, Fundora clarified: “That’s what I want. I think that’s what I’ll get as well.”

His preferred schedule remains a target rather than a signed contract, yet his refusal regarding Saudi Arabia sounded absolute.

“There’s a reason why I haven’t fought in Saudi Arabia,” Fundora said. “I wouldn’t feel comfortable, me being an American and everything like that.”

Asked directly if he would turn down an Ennis bout in the Gulf nation, Fundora confirmed he would walk away because that option feels unrealistic to him.

Securing an Ennis encounter would require common ground on location alongside purses. If promoters propose Saudi Arabia, Fundora makes it obvious that organizers must secure an alternate venue to get his signature.

He has not turned down an active offer to box Ennis. The scenario remains hypothetical right now, even while his desire to face the Ennis vs. Kelly victor is genuine.

Fundora must handle business against Hadribeaj first. Once Saturday concludes, his focus centers on collecting the remaining belts at 154 pounds in an arena he can accept. His stance puts him in a tricky spot financially. Crossing Riyadh off the list immediately shrinks the money pool, because nobody in the United States or the UK is writing those blank checks right now.

“My mother being a veteran and all the politics and that. It’s bigger than boxing. It’s way bigger than boxing,” said Fundora.

If PBC or another promoter has to finance an Ennis against Fundora unification on regular domestic pay-per-view, the numbers have to make sense organically, and that means significantly smaller paydays for both men.

Boots wants the belts, but he also wants to get paid like an elite fighter. If Fundora demands the bout take place in Vegas or Los Angeles, Ennis might look at the revenue split and decide the headache is not worth the discount, especially when other opportunities exist.

None of it matters if he looks past Saturday, either. Hadribeaj is not flying in just to collect a check and hand over the belt. If Fundora gets sloppy or gets caught while daydreaming about spring 2027, the whole discussion vanishes overnight. He will have priced himself out of an imaginary payday while holding empty hands.

Sports.title: Daniel Dubois’ Odd Preparations For His World Title Fight On Saturday
Sports.content:
As the WBO world title fight between Champion Daniel Dubois and Challenger and former WBO Champion Fabio Wardley in The O2 Arena in London, England approaches, it is interesting to observe how both fighters are preparing during fight week.

Both Dubois and Wardley are taking part in the usual media engagements this week to promote their fight. Other than that, Wardley is more low-key in his preparations. However, Dubois is attracting much more attention in the pre-fight buildup not just because he is the reigning WBO Champion, but also due to his rather strange pre-fight preparations.

In this regard, he went on a walkabout in Brixton, London, England, at the beginning of this week with his WBO belt. While it is admirable that Dubois is seen with people, and welcoming photos to be taken with him and well-wishers, he gives the impression that he is an all-conquering hero rather than a fighter preparing to defend his world title against a dangerous opponent. It would surely have been better for Dubois to delay his meet and greet until after he had actually beaten Wardley in Saturday’s fight.

Yet, this is not the first time that Daniel Dubois has done something peculiar in the week leading up to a world title fight. Who can forget his baffling presence at a party in the afternoon of his heavyweight world title clash against Oleksandr Usyk on 19 July last year at Wembley Stadium, London, England? On that occasion, some argued that Dubois allowed his focus to wander by attending this party, when it should have been squarely on making last-minute preparations for his fight against Usyk. They had a valid point, as Dubois ended up losing this fight by knockout in the 5th Round, and his IBF title in the process.

This opens up the debate about whether Dubois is taking Wardley’s challenge too lightly. In the buildup to Dubois v Wardley II, the WBO Champion has gone on record saying that beating Fabio Wardley on Saturday night will be easy. However, Wardley is right to say that if this is the case, Dubois would not have been knocked down twice in the early Rounds in their world title fight on 09 May.

Confidence is one thing. But complacency is a different thing altogether, and Dubois should be wary that he does not fall into this trap. To his credit, Wardley says that he has learned from the mistakes he made in his first fight with Dubois, and will correct them on Saturday. The Ipswich fighter is even honest enough to admit the punches, which earned him his two knockdowns of Dubois in the pair’s first fight, did not land completely accurately. Wardley argues that if they had done so, they would have caused more damage. Further, the video footage from this fight seems to bear this out.

We shall see on Saturday night whether Dubois has prepared correctly for the challenges Fabio Wardley brings. Will it be Repeat or Revenge? One thing for sure is that Daniel Dubois would be foolish to underestimate Wardley, who, like Dubois, has beaten convincingly a former World Champion. Wardley did so when he beat former WBO Champion Joseph Parker by TKO in the 11th Round on 25 October 2025 for the WBO interim heavyweight title.

Time will tell who will be the victor on Saturday night. It should be one helluva fight.

Romer Cherubim

Freelance journalist

Sports.title: Canelo Alvarez Needs Strong Finish To Saudi Contract
Sports.content:
Canelo Alvarez is eyeing a quick turnaround in February 2027 right after his October 31 meeting with Christian Mbilli. That timeline puts him on pace to wrap up his massive Saudi deal in just four months. How he performs down this final stretch will likely decide whether another giant contract follows.

“I want to fight quick, like in February,” Canelo said to Ring Magazine. “I have two fights left in Riyadh. So this one and another one.”

He wants February locked in, though nobody has named an opponent yet. Reports place his current four-fight package around $400 million, even if exact numbers stay private.

Canelo hasn’t said publicly that he wants an extension. Still, closing out the agreement forces the big question into the open: will the Saudis want to spend that kind of cash again?

His first two outings didn’t make a convincing pitch. William Scull left Canelo looking gun-shy. That bout really only existed to pick up the missing IBF belt rather than give fans an exciting matchup.

Against Terence Crawford, Canelo faded after round six. His sudden drop in punches looked like an aging fighter struggling with pace. Citing an injured elbow didn’t ease any doubts about his stamina.

Mbilli will push that gas tank immediately. Canelo needs an emphatic showing against a pressure fighter who won’t stop marching forward. Squeaking by with a disputed decision would damage his leverage, even if he leaves with his belts intact.

Assuming he clears Mbilli, February presents the next major hurdle. Hamzah Sheeraz brings strong British interest. David Benavidez or Osleys Iglesias would offer serious championship tests, though neither has received an official offer.

If Canelo dodges those challenges for an easier touch, the Saudis might start wondering what they are actually buying. Nobody knows how much control he holds over opponent selection anyway.

Dominating Mbilli before taking down elite competition would give Canelo real bargaining power. Another sluggish night marked by fading stamina could leave his next payday looking far smaller than what he is used to collecting.

If Riyadh Season is shelling out nine figures, they shouldn’t be subsidizing soft landings or vanity tours. Dropping rounds and gassing out against a 38-year-old blown-up welterweight like Crawford exposed the cliff Canelo is standing on. Pairing that with Scull in a dull performance showed zero return on entertainment value for the money spent.

Throwing him in with Benavidez or Ennis for the February finale would instantly force the issue.

Benavidez is the fight the public demanded for three years while Canelo priced himself out with absurd $150M to $200M demands. If Canelo wants another Saudi mega check, making him face the monster he avoided at 168 pounds is the only legitimate acid test left. He either proves he still possesses elite mettle or Benavidez completely takes the torch.

Jaron “Boots” Ennis would be pure tactical pressure. Boots would jump two weight classes, but his youth, hand speed, dynamic switch-hitting, and blistering volume would test Canelo’s fading stamina even worse than Crawford did down the stretch. Canelo cannot afford to stand flat-footed and rest against a guy throwing 70 punches a round.

IBF super middleweight champion Osleys Iglesias would be pure high risk, zero reward. The Cuban is a knockout artist who would likely batter this diminished version of Canelo, yet he doesn’t have the commercial profile to justify the Saudis burning their golden goose. There is no financial upside in letting an unknown derail the entire enterprise.

If Canelo rejects Benavidez or Ennis in February and insists on a soft touch like Edgar Berlanga 2 or John Ryder-level opposition, the Saudis have every reason to slam the checkbook shut. At this stage of his career, if he isn’t taking genuine risk into the ring, he isn’t worth the freight.

Sports.title: Anthony Olascuaga Faces Seven-Fight Challenger Yuberjen Martinez
Sports.content:
Anthony Olascuaga will defend his WBO flyweight title against seven-fight professional Yuberjen Martinez on November 14 at Dignity Health Sports Park in Carson, California. The unbeaten Colombian brings an Olympic silver medal and a perfect knockout record into a considerable jump in opposition.

Olascuaga (12-1, 9 KOs) makes his sixth title defense on the Diego Pacheco–Darius Fulghum undercard, with the event airing on DAZN and TNT Sports. The newly signed Matchroom fighter will also compete before his home Los Angeles crowd for the first time in his professional career.

Martinez (7-0, 7 KOs) gives the defense an interesting twist. His amateur pedigree separates him from the usual inexperienced challenger, but seven professional appearances leave plenty unanswered when the next opponent is an established world champion.

Stopping every opponent looks good on a poster. Doing it against the opposition Martinez has faced doesn’t establish that his power will have the same effect on Olascuaga. If the champion takes his punches and keeps coming, Martinez will need more than the finishing ability that has carried him through his professional fights.

That is where the scheduled 12-round distance becomes significant. Martinez’s Olympic success provides evidence of his boxing ability, but managing a world title fight requires decisions about pace, punch selection and energy that a short amateur contest cannot fully prepare him for.

Olascuaga has already been operating at championship level while Martinez has been building toward it. The challenger must show he can maintain his work when an experienced opponent forces him beyond the early success reflected in those seven stoppages.

The homecoming gives Olascuaga an opportunity to introduce himself to a local audience after defending his title in Japan. Matchroom gets a champion with Los Angeles roots on a card already headed by Pacheco.

Martinez gets the bigger opportunity: a chance to turn an accomplished amateur career and a brief professional run into a world championship. His medal makes him worth watching. This fight will tell us how far his professional boxing has progressed.

Ghana News.title: Foreign Affairs Ministry procures 20 pickups to improve passport services
Ghana News.content:
The Ministry of Foreign Affairs has procured 20 pickup vehicles for Passport Application Centres across Ghana to improve staff mobility and strengthen the delivery of passport services.

Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa announced the initiative during a working visit to the Ashanti Regional Passport Application Centre in Kumasi, where he assessed logistical challenges affecting operations.

He said the new vehicles would provide staff with the resources needed to perform their duties more efficiently, particularly when delivering mobile passport application services.

Mr Ablakwa explained that the Kumasi centre currently relies on a single vehicle, placing pressure on its operations. He said the centre would receive one of the newly acquired pickups, alongside allocations to the other regions and the ministry’s headquarters in Greater Accra.

The additional vehicle is expected to improve staff mobility and enable officers to respond more effectively to requests for mobile passport services.

The Minister also announced plans to renovate the Kumasi centre, with funding to be provided in the 2027 budget.

He expressed concern about the condition of some furniture and the facility’s general working environment, noting that improvements were necessary to support staff productivity and efficient service delivery.

He said renovation works at the Accra Passport Application Centre had been budgeted for in 2026 and completed, with Kumasi expected to benefit from a similar intervention next year.

The visit, his first to the Ashanti Regional Passport Application Centre since assuming office, was intended to provide first-hand information about the operational challenges facing staff, including the condition of vehicles, furniture and other equipment.

Ghana News.title: Oil prices retreat as investors weigh supply outlook, Middle East tensions
Ghana News.content:
Oil prices fell more than 1% on Thursday ​as investors weighed risks to supply from attacks on shipping through the Strait of Hormuz against US ‌efforts to cut petroleum shipping costs by easing sanctions on vessels.

Brent crude futures fell $1.64, or 1.6%, to $104.42 a barrel by 0337 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate crude futures were down 98 cents, or 1%, to $94.11, reversing gains from the previous session.

WTI rose to a three-week high in the prior ​session after the Houthis attacked Saudi Aramco's headquarters and Iran said it was deploying new tactics to target ships ​in the Strait of Hormuz and keep oil prices high.

A container ship and a dry bulk ⁠carrier both sank near the strait in the past 24 hours after being hit by projectiles in separate incidents, maritime officials said ​on Wednesday.

Attacks around the waterway have surged over the past 10 days, with Iran saying it is stepping up strikes in ​response to the US blockade of its ports and tougher sanctions introduced last month.

With the Iran war having disrupted shipping and driven up freight costs to record highs, the Trump administration is considering easing sanctions on so-called shadow-fleet vessels that have transported oil and petroleum products from countries including Russia, ​Iran and Venezuela to help ease prices, a US official said on Wednesday.

The new talks centre on the United States potentially ​allowing "legal oil" to flow on previously sanctioned vessels, the US official said.

Increased output from Russia and the Middle East has kept a lid on ‌prices. Russia's ⁠crude oil production rose by 65,000 barrels per day in September to 8.43 million bpd but remained down 870,000 bpd year over year, the International Energy Agency said on Wednesday.

The IEA also said crude oil exports from Middle East Gulf producers rose by 4.4 million bpd in September to around 75% of prewar levels.

"While there is little concrete evidence of a near-term peace deal, oil ​continues to find its way to ​buyers through alternative routes ⁠and logistical arrangements," said Phillip Nova's head of market insights, Priyanka Sachdeva, in a client note.

"These workarounds have helped prevent a more severe supply shock, although they come at a higher cost and ​leave global flows vulnerable to further disruption."

In the US, crude oil and distillate inventories fell, ​while gasoline stocks ⁠rose last week, market sources said on Wednesday, citing data from the American Petroleum Institute.

Crude stocks fell by 11.1 million barrels in the week ended October 9, sources said. That was a much bigger draw than analysts polled by Reuters expected.

"Despite the sharp inventory draw, oil prices ⁠barely reacted. ​The failure to rise on bullish news suggests investors are cautious about chasing ​prices higher at current levels," said Haitong Futures in a note on Thursday.

Official numbers from the US Energy Information Administration are due at 12 p.m. EDT (1600 ​GMT), delayed by a day following the Columbus Day holiday on Monday.

Ghana News.title: Mahama Ayariga highlights Jimi reclamation project as effort to tackle flooding
Ghana News.content:
Minister for Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs, Mahama Ayariga, has highlighted the Jimi Land Reclamation Project and Watercourse Rehabilitation Project as important interventions to address flooding, poor drainage and land degradation.

In a Facebook post on Wednesday, October 14, the Minister said the initiatives were aimed at restoring degraded land, improving water flow and promoting environmental sustainability.

He described the projects as important steps towards addressing environmental challenges that affect communities and their safety.

The rehabilitation of watercourses is expected to support better water movement and help address drainage problems, while land reclamation can contribute to restoring damaged areas. The combined interventions are intended to improve environmental conditions and create safer communities.

Mr Ayariga said the government remained committed to protecting the environment and promoting sustainable development for the benefit of present and future generations.

He stressed the importance of initiatives that restore degraded landscapes and improve the conditions in which communities live.

Ghana News.title: Ayine pushes duty-lawyer scheme to protect suspects at police stations
Ghana News.content:
Attorney General and Minister of Justice, Dr Dominic A. Ayine, has called for lawyers to be made available at police stations and courts to protect suspects’ rights and improve access to legal representation during criminal proceedings.

He said suspects were particularly vulnerable during police investigations and their first court appearances, when decisions could have serious consequences for their liberty.

Speaking through a speech read on his behalf at the launch of the Legal Aid Commission’s 2026 Legal Aid Week in Accra on Tuesday, October 13, Dr Ayine advocated a duty-lawyer scheme to give practical effect to Article 14(2) of the 1992 Constitution. The event was held under the theme, “Justice at Your Doorstep.”

Dr Ayine also urged the Commission to review cases involving people in custody regularly to prevent prolonged detention without legal assistance. He called for legal aid services to be expanded beyond regional capitals through district offices and mobile clinics operating at markets, community centres and traditional council halls.

“The Commission’s presence must be felt beyond regional capitals,” he said.

To widen access further, the Attorney General said he intended to engage the Ghana Bar Association to encourage more lawyers to take up pro bono cases.

He also urged law faculties and the Ghana School of Law to establish supervised legal clinics and train paralegals and community volunteers to provide basic legal guidance in rural communities.

He stressed that poverty should not prevent people from exercising their rights or receiving fair treatment, remarking that “a right that cannot be reached is a right denied.”

Dr Ayine further proposed strengthening alternative dispute resolution mechanisms to help settle family, land, tenancy and debt disputes without the costs and delays of full trials.

He also called for a toll-free legal aid line, SMS and WhatsApp intake channels, legal information in local languages and a shared case-management system linking the Legal Aid Commission, the courts and the Attorney General’s Office.

He urged the Commission to secure predictable funding and publish annual performance reports detailing services delivered across districts and the time taken to resolve cases.

Ghana News.title: Fire at GRIDCo’s Mallam Substation cuts power to parts of Accra
Ghana News.content:
A fire at the Ghana Grid Company Limited’s (GRIDCo) Mallam Substation disrupted electricity supply to parts of Accra in the early hours of Wednesday, October 14, 2026.

In a statement issued by its Corporate Communications Section, GRIDCo said a fault occurred at the substation at 2:36 a.m. on October 14, resulting in a fire on one of its transformers.

Personnel from the Ghana National Fire Service responded to the incident and successfully contained and extinguished the blaze.

GRIDCo said power had been restored to some affected areas, with efforts continuing to reconnect the remaining communities as quickly as possible.

The company’s engineers are investigating the cause of the fire, while steps have been initiated to replace the damaged transformer.

GRIDCo apologised for the disruption and thanked affected customers and stakeholders for their patience and understanding.

Ghana News.title: Stephen Amoah criticises 20% digital services tax as excessive
Ghana News.content:
Nhyiaeso MP and Ranking Member of Parliament’s Finance Committee, Dr Stephen Amoah, has challenged the government’s 20% tax on qualifying cross-border digital services, describing the rate as excessive and warning that it could increase the financial burden on consumers.

He acknowledged the need for Ghana to strengthen domestic revenue mobilisation and reduce its dependence on borrowing to finance development.

However, he argued that fiscal consolidation must be pursued without imposing additional hardships on households already facing economic pressures.

Dr Amoah said a balanced tax policy was necessary to protect consumers while helping the country meet its revenue targets and build resilience against future economic shocks. He urged the authorities to consider prevailing economic conditions and the timing of implementation when introducing new tax measures.

Speaking on Citi FM on Wednesday, October 14, Dr Amoah reiterated his objection to the rate, saying: “My only position is that 20% is too much.”

He cautioned that efforts to reduce borrowing and strengthen the country’s fiscal position should not burden citizens beyond what they could reasonably afford.

The Ghana Revenue Authority (GRA) is introducing a system requiring commercial banks to collect applicable taxes on qualifying cross-border digital transactions. The effective 20% rate comprises 15% Value Added Tax (VAT), a 2.5% National Health Insurance Levy and a 2.5% Ghana Education Trust Fund Levy.

The measure covers qualifying payments for services such as Netflix, Spotify, Disney+, Microsoft 365, Adobe, Zoom, ChatGPT and cloud computing platforms. The GRA maintains that the arrangement changes the collection mechanism rather than introducing a new tax or resulting in double taxation.

Ghana News.title: Ghana secures $3.5bn investment commitments to revive oil and gas sector – Jinapor
Ghana News.content:
Minister for Energy and Green Transition Dr John Abdulai Jinapor

Ghana has secured $3.5 billion in investment commitments to expand petroleum operations and drill new wells as the government steps up efforts to revitalise the upstream oil and gas sector, Minister for Energy and Green Transition Dr John Abdulai Jinapor has announced.

The Minister disclosed this during a fireside chat at the opening ceremony of African Energy Week, where he joined Kosmos Energy Chief Executive Officer Andrew Inglis and African Energy Chamber Executive Chairman NJ Ayuk to discuss strategies for attracting fresh investment into Ghana’s petroleum industry.

Dr Jinapor said the government was engaging investors and pursuing legal and fiscal reforms to make the sector more competitive, predictable and attractive to businesses.

He noted that the measures were intended to restore investor confidence, bring in new capital and protect Ghana’s national interests while creating conditions for sustained growth in petroleum production.

He said the government’s next priority was to build on the investment commitments by increasing local participation and expanding domestic value addition.

A key component of the strategy, he explained, was to strengthen Ghana’s refining capacity so that more crude oil could be processed locally, boosting industrial activity, creating jobs and improving energy security.

Dr Jinapor also emphasised that investment in the sector must translate into lasting benefits for Ghanaians rather than simply increase capital inflows.

He commended President John Dramani Mahama for providing strategic direction and support to the energy sector, adding that continued investment, stronger local participation and a more business-friendly environment would be critical to turning Ghana’s petroleum resources into sustainable economic growth.

Ghana News.title: Court to hear Wontumi’s bail application today
Ghana News.content:
The Accra High Court is expected to hear an application for bail by former New Patriotic Party (NPP) Ashanti Regional Chairman, Bernard Antwi Boasiako, popularly known as Chairman Wontumi, on Thursday, October 15, 2026.

His lawyers are seeking his release from custody while he pursues an appeal against his conviction and 20-year prison sentence for illegal mining-related offences linked to a concession at Samreboi in the Western Region.

The application was originally scheduled for hearing on August 19, but the proceedings were postponed after both Mr Boasiako and his lead counsel, Samuel Atta Akyea, failed to appear in court.

The court clerk subsequently informed the parties that the presiding judge was unavailable for the remainder of that week, resulting in the matter being rescheduled for today.

The hearing is expected to allow the defence team to formally present its arguments in support of bail pending the determination of the appeal.

The application was filed in August as part of efforts to secure Mr Boasiako’s release while the appellate process continues.

However, the Attorney-General has opposed the request, arguing that the former NPP regional chairman poses a flight risk.

The court is expected to consider the arguments from both sides in determining whether he should be granted bail pending the outcome of his appeal.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Restoring nature is key to a more resilient future
World.content:
Nature is humanity’s life-support system, but it is being depleted at an alarming rate, leaving our world increasingly vulnerable. From deadly heatwaves and raging wildfires to catastrophic floods and prolonged droughts, the effects of environmental change have been impossible to ignore this year. With El Nino forecast to intensify, the risks to people, nature and economies are only increasing.

These shocks are unfolding against the backdrop of widespread nature loss, with WWF’s Living Planet Report 2026 finding that the average size of monitored wildlife populations declined by 73 percent between 1970 and 2022. Nature loss is increasingly a question of economic and national resilience – affecting food and water security, health, supply chains and geopolitical stability.

The situation is serious, but science shows there are still grounds for hope.

The economic systems driving nature’s decline can be transformed, and change can accelerate much faster than many may expect. Evidence shows that under the right conditions, positive change can cross a tipping point threshold and become self-reinforcing, making a safer, more resilient future not just possible, but inevitable.

The question is: How can we accelerate the actions needed to trigger those tipping points and accelerate the transition?

Positive tipping points and the opportunity for transformational change

In environmental terms, we often think about tipping points in terms of the threats they pose to vital ecosystems, such as coral reefs or the Amazon rainforest, where constant damage risks compounding and becoming increasingly impossible to reverse. These dangers are real and urgent. However, these tipping point dynamics can also work in our favour.



Three economic systems are driving most of nature’s decline: the energy system that fuels climate change; the global food system that leads to habitat loss and climate change; and the finance system that bankrolls it all. Triggering tipping points in those systems would see them rapidly transform for the better and reduce harm to the climate and nature. Once that threshold is passed, change can happen quickly as knowledge and technology advance, with solutions becoming cheaper and more accessible and as people learn from others. Encouragingly, progress is already under way – not everywhere, and not yet at the scale required – but enough to demonstrate that change is possible.

The world does not lack goals for 2030. What it lacks is the pace of implementation. With the Global Biodiversity Framework, the UN Sustainable Development Goals and the Paris Agreement in place, governments have already agreed on a pathway. Focusing on implementing these agreements in full will create the conditions for rapid systemic change.

The global energy system has already passed a tipping point, with the transition away from fossil fuels to renewable energy now accelerating. While far from complete, this transition demonstrates how rapid systemic change is possible, offering valuable lessons for the equally urgent transformation of our food and financial systems.

Twenty years ago, solar power was used mostly in satellites and pocket calculators. Now, it is the cheapest option for new electricity generation in most countries. Affordable solar panels are electrifying rural households and improving the resilience of food and medical supply chains. Renewable technologies are displacing fossil fuels at a pace few people predicted even a decade ago.

Changing the food and finance systems is proving slower but is no less urgent.

To progress towards a food systems tipping point, we need to hit major milestones in the uptake of nature-positive food production and see wider shifts in consumer demand for healthier, more sustainable foods to reinforce and reward this shift. Some progress is under way with efforts to tackle commodity-driven deforestation, and more than 130 countries have national strategic plans for food system transformation, but commitments have not yet translated into the policies and incentives needed to accelerate the transition.

Tipping the finance system so that more finance flows to activities that protect and restore nature than activities that harm it is a fundamental challenge. Reaching this tipping point will require a combination of regulatory change, subsidy reform, and a shift in how the sector values climate and nature as material financial risks. If even a portion of the money currently directed towards harmful activities is redirected to environmental recovery, it could shift the economics of the entire transformation.



Governments meeting at the COP17 biodiversity and COP31 climate conferences have before them a vital opportunity to work together to accelerate the actions needed to trigger positive tipping points and to build resilience into societies and the global economy.

Learning from conservation success

Hidden within the broader picture of global biodiversity decline are inspiring stories of species recovery. Populations of green sea turtles and tigers are rebounding due to dedicated conservation work bringing together governments, communities and organisations.

Creating systemic change will similarly take action from all of us, from governments to businesses, financial institutions, local communities, and individuals. We know where we need to get to and the hurdles we need to overcome together; the task now is to create the conditions in which positive change gathers momentum and starts reinforcing itself.

Building strength and resilience into our natural support system will require the courage to shift from extractive, wasteful economies focused on short-term gain to systems that are sustainable and regenerative for the long-term benefit of all. We have the goals, the solutions and pathways to get there. Yes, there might be setbacks along the way, but science shows nature and the climate can still recover and that change can happen faster than we might think.

The views expressed in this article are the author’s own and do not necessarily reflect Al Jazeera’s editorial stance.

World.title: Israel has detained more than 2,000 Palestinian children since 2023: report
World.content:
At least 350 Palestinian children currently face “harsh conditions” in Israeli prisons.

Share Israel has detained more than 2,000 Palestinian children since 2023: report on social media

Israeli forces have detained more than 2,000 Palestinian children since October 2023, the Palestinian Prisoner’s Society said.

In a report released on Wednesday, the Palestinian rights group said Israeli authorities continue to escalate their targeting of Palestinian children. At least 350 Palestinian children are currently facing “harsh conditions” in Israeli prisons.

On Tuesday, Israeli forces arrested at least six children from Hebron in the occupied West Bank, the report said.

The organisation said information regarding the number of children arrested in Gaza is unclear, given the thousands of missing persons in the besieged Gaza Strip, including children, and the ongoing policy of enforced disappearance.

The group said Israel’s policy of detention without charges or a release date constitutes “an additional violation and crime that leaves children facing the unknown and deprives them of family and educational stability”.

Cases of Palestinian children in prison

The report described Israeli practices that begin with “intimidation and arrest” and extend to “torture, starvation and denial of healthcare”.

The group highlighted the case of 15-year-old Mohammed Hamid, who contracted scabies, a contagious skin infestation, while he was detained in Ofer Prison, where rights groups have long documented abuses. He suffered severe infections, underwent heart surgery and was admitted to intensive care in critical condition. He subsequently had one of his legs amputated.

The organisation also highlighted the case of 17-year-old Walid Ahmed, who died in March 2025 after six months in Megiddo Prison. In December, an Israeli judge halted the investigation into his death, stating that although there was evidence of starvation, no definitive cause of death had been established.

American children in Israeli prisons

Ahmed was imprisoned in Megiddo with his friend Mohammed Ibrahim, a teenager from Florida. Ibrahim was released after months of advocacy from US-based organisations and appeals from high-ranking lawmakers.



Mohammed Ibrahim was not the only young American held in Israeli prison without charge – Israeli forces reportedly took Abdalkareem Issa Ahmed Safi from his West Bank home in a late-night raid in June. He turned 18 in detention, and authorities subsequently moved him from a youth holding area into an adult section at Ofer Prison.

Similarly, Israeli forces arrested 16-year-old Adam Wajeh Abdelfattah Karakrah, also an American, in July. Although he was set for release in August after his family secured bail, Israeli authorities abruptly reversed the decision to free him.

The Palestinian Prisoner’s Society called for “real international action” to ensure the release of arbitrarily detained children, enforce investigations and end torture, starvation and the denial of treatment in Israeli prisons.

Israeli forces have detained more than 25,000 Palestinians in the West Bank, and thousands more in Gaza, since Israel’s genocidal war began in October 2023.

World.title: Heavy rain causes mass pileup in Brazil tunnel
World.content:
Heavy rain causes mass pileup in Brazil tunnel

NewsFeed Heavy rain causes mass pileup in Brazil tunnel

Flooding left vehicles piled up and people stranded inside Sao Paulo’s Anhangabau tunnel. People had to wait for the floodwaters to recede before rescue teams could reach them.

World.title: X suspends 13,000 accounts, alleging foreign influence ahead of US midterms
World.content:
The social platform says networks targeted US political conversation across the spectrum ahead of midterm elections.

The social media platform X has suspended more than 13,000 accounts related to three suspected foreign influence operations linked to Iran, Russia and China that sought to shape the political debate in the United States.

The company announced the suspensions on Wednesday as it outlined measures ahead of the November 3 US midterm elections.

X said its investigations found the networks used fake accounts to post and amplify political content targeting candidates and public figures “across the political spectrum”.

The company said it identified the accounts through “proactive sweeps and investigations” under its rules against spam and coordinated inauthentic behaviour.

“Free speech is the bedrock of a functioning democracy, and we are proud that X is the global town square where these debates happen. Our job is to keep that conversation authentic, open, and safe,” X Global Government Affairs said in announcing the suspensions.

Election Safeguards

X also outlined rules against misleading information regarding how, when or where to vote in the US midterms, as well as attempts to suppress turnout and voter intimidation, including calls for violence near polling stations.

The company said users can report election-related posts through the “civic integrity” option to request a community note providing context. In urgent cases, X may also apply labels to posts that violate its election rules in cases requiring attention, the platform said.

The announcement comes a week after OpenAI said it had shut down two alleged influence operations from Russia and Iran that used ChatGPT to push fake journalist personas and run a “think-tank” that covertly spread anti-Ukraine propaganda.



X has previously acted against suspected foreign influence networks. In 2021, Twitter, as X was then known, said it had suspended 238 accounts purportedly operating from Iran.

World.title: Argentina’s Milei backs Trump for US midterms, calls vote crucial for West
World.content:
The President’s ally says conservatives “cannot give an inch” in Latin America as he accepts an award in Washington.

Share Argentina’s Milei backs Trump for US midterms, calls vote crucial for West on social media

Argentine President Javier Milei has urged his ally, US President Donald Trump, to come out of the United States midterm elections in a stronger position, calling the vote important for the West as a whole.

Milei made the appeal on Wednesday at a Hispanic Heritage gala in Washington, where a Hispanic association gave him an award, ahead of November’s vote.

Conservatives, he said, “cannot give an inch in our reconquest of the hemisphere”, according to Agence France-Presse (AFP).

Milei flew into the US capital on Wednesday for meetings with investors and the gala. He is due to address the US Chamber of Commerce on Thursday.

Milei’s lifeline

Trump firmly backed Milei a year ago, when his government also faced crucial legislative elections. He has called Milei his “favorite president”.

That backing, together with a currency swap agreement with the US Treasury, helped Milei to success in those polls, analysts have argued.

The centrepiece of the package, announced by Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, was a $20bn swap with Argentina’s central bank, in which the US exchanged dollars for pesos. The swap came shortly after Milei’s party lost a key provincial election.

Trump made clear at the time that the support hinged on a Milei victory. “I’m with this man because his philosophy is correct,” he said ahead of a White House lunch with the Argentine leader. “If he wins, we’re staying with him. And if he doesn’t win, we’re gone.”



Trump also warned that the US would not be “generous” if Milei lost. The remarks unsettled Argentine markets, with the main stock index giving up earlier gains and falling about 2 percent, The Associated Press reported.

The package drew criticism in the US. Democratic lawmakers accused Trump of prioritising a foreign bailout while the US government was shut down.

World.title: Albanian Ministry of Justice on fire as education protesters riot
World.content:
Albanian Ministry of Justice on fire as education protesters riot

NewsFeed Albanian Ministry of Justice on fire as education protesters riot

Hundreds of students joined anti-government protests in Tirana, demanding education reforms and Prime Minister Edi Rama’s resignation. Rama has faced growing discontent over corruption allegations and a controversial coastal resort since winning a fourth term in May 2025.

World.title: OpenAI bugging suspect allegedly booked one-way trip to Saudi Arabia
World.content:
Saudi national Abdulrahman Alfozan was due to fly to Saudi Arabia on October 12, US prosecutors say in a court filing.

The Saudi national accused of bugging OpenAI’s headquarters booked a one-way flight to Saudi Arabia before his arrest, US prosecutors have alleged.

Abdulrahman Alfozan, a former OpenAI engineer, had been scheduled to fly to Saudi Arabia with his wife and another family member on October 12, prosecutors said in a court filing unsealed on Wednesday.

The FBI arrested Alfozan, who worked at OpenAI for about 15 months until his termination last week, on October 9, after OpenAI personnel reported the discovery of a hidden listening device in a conference room at the company’s San Francisco headquarters.

Alfozan, 35, has been charged with “using or endeavoring to use an electronic, mechanical, or other device to intercept oral communications”.

The offence carries a maximum punishment of five years in prison and a $250,000 fine.

Prosecutors disclosed the alleged flight booking to a judge on October 8 in a motion seeking to seal the criminal complaint against Alfozan, arguing he had the “means – and will have an incentive – to flee” the United States.

William Pernik, Alfozan’s lawyer, said he and his client planned to contest the criminal allegations and his client’s ongoing detention in court.

“We trust that the American justice system will treat our client fairly, despite the narrative painted in the media at this time,” Pernik told Al Jazeera.

“Our client is a well regarded professional with long standing ties to the community,” Pernik added.

“He is presumed innocent and is entitled to fair treatment and due process of law. The emphasis on his national origin and therefore suggestions of lack of trustworthiness or flight risk harken back to dark chapters of our nation’s history that we intend to fight fully.”



Alfozan’s arrest has shone a spotlight on concerns that frontier tech firms are a target for spying and industrial espionage amid the global race to gain an upper hand in AI.

Before joining OpenAI in July last year, Alfozan worked as a systems engineer at Meta and interned at Microsoft, according to a LinkedIn profile in his name.

Alfozan is also listed as a venture partner at Raed Ventures, a Riyadh-based venture capital firm whose other partners include Prince Khalid bin Bandar bin Sultan bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, a member of the Saudi royal family.

In a statement announcing Alfozan’s appointment in February 2025, Raed Ventures described the engineer as “a seasoned professional with extensive experience in tech startups” and said his role would involve “identifying promising investment opportunities and supporting startups on their journey toward growth and success”.

World.title: North Korea tests two submarine-launched missiles, state media reports
World.content:
The tests showcase North Korea’s war deterrent capabilities in the region, KCNA says.

North Korea has test-fired two types of submarine-launched strategic cruise missiles in the sea off its east coast, state media KCNA reports.

The test-fire on Wednesday aimed to examine the reliability of war deterrents and improve the navy’s skill in performing strategic missions, the outlet said.

One of the missiles fired was a Pulhwasal-3-31, the same type of strategic cruise missile North Korea said it test-fired from land last week, according to KCNA.

Senior military officers observed the tests conducted at sea off the country’s east coast. KCNA added that the tests had no adverse impact on the security of neighbouring countries.

North Korea is not yet believed to have launched a modern missile submarine in full operation. This is a top military priority of the country’s leader Kim Jong Un, who has overseen the development of a range of strategic ballistic and cruise missiles.

Last year, Kim Jong Un criticised a nuclear submarine deal between the US and South Korea while he toured his country’s submarine production facility, where state media images showed an 8,700-tonne nuclear-powered missile submarine under construction. On his tour, he described the deal as a threat to the stability of the Korean Peninsula, KCNA reported.

Recent developments

Pyongyang has fired off a flurry of missiles in recent weeks.

Earlier this week, North Korea fired multiple ballistic missiles towards the sea off its east coast, adding to a series of tests as tensions between Seoul and Pyongyang are on the rise.



On October 3, North Korea also tested a hypersonic intermediate-range missile designed to evade missile defences in South Korea and Japan.

After the ballistic missile launch, Seoul’s Joint Chiefs of Staff spokesperson Jang Do-young said the move appeared to be a show of force as it came days after South Korea tested its own hypersonic weapon.

Last week, South Korean President Lee Jae Myung oversaw the country’s first test firing of a hypersonic missile, a rare public showcase of a missile test by a South Korean president.

Lee’s office said the hypersonic weapon, once fully developed, would enhance South Korea’s ability to strike key targets by surprise in the “Korean Peninsula theatre of operations”.

Inter-Korean relations have further soured as a landmine blast, which Seoul blamed on North Korea, wounded three soldiers in September in the Demilitarized Zone (DMZ) between the two countries.

A joint South Korean-United Nations investigation concluded that two landmines that exploded last month in the DMZ were planted by North Korean forces about a year ago, prompting Seoul to demand an official apology.

Pyongyang has sharply accelerated military fortification along the DMZ as part of leader Kim Jong Un’s “hostile-states” policy, launched in 2023, to permanently sever ties with South Korea.

Diplomatic efforts on the Korean Peninsula have stalled since the collapse of denuclearisation talks between Washington and Pyongyang in 2019 during the first Trump administration. While Trump has floated the possibility of meeting Kim Jong Un in his second term, no such meeting has materialised.

World.title: Musk says US government may be behind slowdown of Ukraine drone speeds
World.content:
Elon Musk has suggested that the US government may be behind restrictions on the speed at which some of Ukraine's weapons can travel and stay connected to SpaceX's Starlink internet network.

Starlink is a vital tool allowing Kyiv to guide drones to Russian targets and also protect its own skies, but on Tuesday night Ukraine said unexpected new speed limits were disrupting its battlefield missions.

An adviser to President Volodymyr Zelensky said he believed the restrictions were not a coincidence and were related to the latest strains between Kyiv and Washington.

Musk said that Starshield, the military-grade sister service to Starlink, is controlled by the US government, and "any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately [the US president]".

Musk - writing on X - had been responding to pleas from Ukrainian officials to restore connectivity, including from Zelensky who told UK media: "I hope that it's a mistake, maybe [a] huge technical problem. I don't know, but we are asking to... switch [it] on."

Starlink, which is owned by Musk's SpaceX, restricted speed limits on Tuesday night to 100mph (160km/h), meaning any weapons that travelled faster than that lost connectivity to the network.

It had been partially restored by Wednesday evening, Ukraine's former defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov said.

"Removing Starshield's speed limit entirely is now critical for Ukraine's defense," he wrote on X, thanking Elon Musk and asking for his "continued support".

About an hour later, Musk replied to that post, defending his company's involvement.

"Starshield systems are owned and controlled by the US government. Any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS," he wrote.

Musk added that Starlink is for "civilian or defensive activities and cannot be used for offensive military action, as doing so would be inappropriate for a commercial company".
