The US government has not commented.

In the early hours of Thursday, Russian strikes killed two people in the Dnipropetrovsk region, regional governor Oleksandr Hanzha said.

While both companies are owned by Musk's SpaceX, Starlink is a civilian service that uses satellites in low Earth orbit to provide internet access, particularly in remote areas, while Starshield is designed for government and military use.

The restrictions on Tuesday night came as Russia launched deadly attacks against Ukraine that killed several people in Kyiv, officials said, and hit communications and energy facilities used by Ukraine's military.

Zelensky said it was "one of the largest attacks" from Russia, and while "a significant part of the drones were shot down" there were "also hits".

At least 600,000 people across Ukraine were left without electricity, and residents said they received no warning of incoming drones before they hit.

"It is clear that this action cannot be a coincidence and is related to the current political situation," Zelensky's adviser Serhiy Beskrestnov wrote on Telegram on Wednesday morning.

World.title: Student protesters attack government buildings in Albania
World.content:
Thousands of students have taken to the streets in the Albanian capital of Tirana, attacking several government buildings on the second day of violent anti-government protests.

The demonstration began outside the ministry of education on Tuesday, as students called for better university conditions and job prospects.

Wednesday saw part of the education ministry's building set on fire, while the prime minister's office, finance and interior ministry, and several surrounding businesses were also attacked.

Albania's Deputy Prime Minister âAlbana KoÃ§iu has called for "calmness, self-restraint and maturity" and said "Albania does not need to burn to change".

World.title: Retired US generals call on Pentagon to cancel 'barbaric' execution livestream
World.content:
A group of 72 retired US generals, admirals, and other high-ranking military officers are pressing the US government to cancel plans to livestream an execution by firing squad.

"We ask the President, our Congressional representatives, and our fellow citizens to act to prevent this barbaric abuse of authority," they wrote in a letter where they also argued the livestream would turn the mass killer into a "martyr".

Last week, the Pentagon announced it would publicly show the 3 December execution of Nidal Hasan, an Army psychiatrist who shot dead 13 unarmed US soldiers at the Fort Hood military base.

Lawmakers from both parties, as well as religious leaders, have criticised the plan.

Last week President Donald Trump said he "absolutely" approved of the livestream plan, but some administration officials are now leaning against it, according to CBS News, the BBC's US media partner. CBS reported that Trump had not yet made a final decision on the livestream as of Tuesday.

In the open letter released on Wednesday, the former military leaders - which included 45 generals, 12 admirals and several former judge advocates general - said they did not oppose the death penalty being carried out.

But they argued a public execution would violate the US Constitution's protections against cruel and unusual punishment and turn what should be a "solemn and grave punishment" into "a carnival for the enjoyment of voyeurs and spectators".

"This type of exploitative broadcasting - that debases human dignity- will taint the honor of the military that employs it, and a nation that allows it," they also wrote.

"It will be used by our nation's enemies to stoke hatred, harm American soldiers and citizens in the future, and will ensure that Hasan becomes a martyr for attacking and killing his fellow soldiers."

The letter's signatories came from throughout the military and included a handful of officers who retired during Trump's first term. Some also had served during the Iraq and Afghanistan wars.

Hasan said in court that he carried out the shooting at Fort Hood, the deadliest ever non-combat attack on an American base, believing he was protecting Muslims and the Taliban in Afghanistan from the US military. Hasan was shot during the attack and now uses a wheelchair.

Retired Maj Gen Tony Taguba, who led the Army's investigation into reported prisoner abuses at Abu Ghraib in Iraq, and retired Air Force Coll Moe Davis, a prosecutor at the Guatanamo Bay detention centre who called waterboarding torture, signed the letter.

So did Charles Bolden, a US Marine Corps Major General who became the head of Nasa, and a retired Lt Gen Claudia Kennedy, the first woman to become a three-star general in the Army.

World.title: White House defends new press secretary amid questions about her legal credentials
World.content:
The White House is defending its new press secretary, Katie Zacharia, as she faces scrutiny over her legal credentials.

President Donald Trump described Zacharia as an attorney when announcing her appointment last week and she has referred to herself as a lawyer.

But when she was asked on Tuesday by a reporter in which state she had passed the bar exam required to be an attorney in the US, she said standing alongside the president: "When I moved to China."

She does not appear to be registered to the bar in any state where she has lived. White House communications director Steven Cheung said Zacharia is "uniquely qualified and whip smart to help inform the American people".

Responding to questions about her credentials, Zacharia said in a statement this week: "I practised international transaction law, with all the appropriate credentials."

On Wednesday, a watchdog group, Campaign for Accountability, filed a complaint with the California State Bar Association.

They are seeking an investigation into whether Zacharia "repeatedly held herself out to the public as entitled to practise law without a licence to do so, conduct California law treats as a crime".

The 42-year-old political strategist graduated from law school at Pepperdine University in California in 2011, the university confirmed.

A law degree is not a licence to practise law in the US.

The new White House press secretary told the New York Times on Wednesday that when she first began appearing on cable news, she had asked Pepperdine how she should identify herself.

She said she was advised by the university president that she could call herself a lawyer, but not an attorney.

Zacharia took the bar exam in California after graduating from law school but did not pass, according to the Wall Street Journal. California's bar exam is widely regarded as one of the hardest in the US to pass.

A person with direct knowledge of the matter told the outlet that Zacharia took the exam around the same time that she was planning a wedding and preparing to move to China with her husband-to-be.

World.title: 'Nowhere to escape' - Indonesians share footage of orange haze blanketing towns
World.content:
A thick orange smog has descended on the Indonesian city of Palangka Raya.

Witnesses captured videos of the haze washing over the Kalimantan region not far from where wildfires continue to burn.

The ISPU air pollution index exceeded 1,200, according to data from the national environment ministry, four times higher than the "hazardous" level of 300 on Wednesday.

Toxic smog is choking millions across Indonesia, Singapore and Malaysia, with authorities partly blaming the agricultural clearing method known as "slash and burn" for compounding the intense haze.

Read more on this story here.

World.title: Brooklyn novelty shop reeling from 'surreal' row with Kelly Clarkson over mechanical bird
World.content:
On a rainy Wednesday afternoon, a novelty toy and games store in a quiet part of New York City was seeing much busier foot traffic than usual.

Inside, the shop was packed with cameramen and customers, while passersby in this Brooklyn neighbourhood of Cobble Hill looked inside, asking: "Where's the bird?"

Art of Play has found itself at the centre of a social media storm since the weekend when Grammy-winning musician Kelly Clarkson complained online that the boutique store would not let her buy a singing and dancing mechanical bird that was perched on the wall.

The Since U Been Gone singer claimed she was "looked at as if I couldn't afford" the bird - which she said had a price tag of $15,000 (Â£11,000).

"Y'all should go check out Art of Play in Brooklyn if you enjoy being treated like Julia Roberts' character in Pretty Woman," she said, referring to a scene from the 1990 romantic comedy film where Roberts' character is treated poorly by staff at a shop, who imply she cannot afford various items.

In a follow-up post on social media, Clarkson said the store had told her the bird cost $15,000 and that they could find her something else "comparable".

Art of Play has defended how it treated the star on social media, saying the wooden bird - which is called Molly - is permanently attached to the wall and is not for sale.

It said that during Clarkson's five-minute visit on Saturday, an employee suggested to her that she could buy an identical bird for $15,000.

They also said they had offered her a different singing bird for $2,000 from a clock-making shop in Germany, which she could have purchased that day.

"Imagine our surprise when our small local business was suddenly attacked by eight million people who have never visited our store," Art of Play said.

"It's been a surreal experience to be the focus of such widespread outrage after just one mention by a celebrity."

World.title: Sally Rooney books withdrawn in UK over Palestine Action support
World.content:
Normal People author Sally Rooney has said her novels will no longer be supplied to booksellers in the UK as a result of her support for Palestine Action.

The Irish novelist said last year she intended to carry on using her royalties to support the group, which is a proscribed terrorist organisation in the UK.

In a statement to BBC News, Rooney said further publication of her work could constitute a "serious criminal offence", so she had agreed with her publisher Faber not to continue supplying her books in the UK.

"I have made every effort to be honest with the public about my beliefs and intentions, and I am wholly prepared to accept the consequences," she said.

Ebook editions have already been removed from sale in the UK, although many book shops still have existing stock of physical copies.

Waterstones confirmed to the BBC that Faber had advised there were no restrictions on booksellers keeping their current copies on the shelves.

Rooney has sold more than six million books globally, including 2.3 million in the UK, according to NielsenIQ BookData.

Normal People was released in 2018 and turned into a hit TV series two years later, effectively launching the acting careers of Paul Mescal and Daisy Edgar-Jones.

Rooney's other novels are Intermezzo, Conversations With Friends and Beautiful World, Where Are You.

Publisher Faber told BBC News: "Current legislation in the UK has led to circumstances where Faber cannot pass on UK earnings to Sally Rooney for her work.

"To sell a writer's work and not be able to pass on earnings is an unconscionable situation for a publisher.

"As such, and in full agreement with Sally, we have taken the decision that we can no longer supply her works in the UK in any format."

Faber added: "We remain the proud publisher of her remarkable body of work, which we will continue to sell in other territories."

World.title: Anthropic flags revenue surge to investors ahead of stock market debut
World.content:
Artificial intelligence (AI) giant Anthropic saw its revenue surge by 45% to $16.8bn (Â£12.7bn) in the three months to the end of September, the BBC understands.

The figures were revealed by the Claude-developer as it briefed prospective investors on Wednesday at its headquarters in San Francisco as it lays the groundwork for a stock market listing, which is expected to take place before the end of the year.

It comes as some tech stocks, including firms that make the chips and other hardware that power data centres, have fallen in recent days over concerns about the hundreds of billions of dollars being spent on AI infrastructure.

An Anthropic spokesperson declined to comment.

Anthropic's revenue has risen in successive quarters this year, from $4.7bn in the first three months to $11.6bn the following period.

The company also reportedly said that it made a profit for the second quarter in a row.

Its revenue figures, along with those of rival OpenAI, offer an important gauge of the AI industry's growth and ability to finance the infrastructure needed to develop the technology.

Stocks in some US technology companies fell on Wednesday over concerns around investments in AI.

Share in chip makers - including AMD, Nvidia and Intel - fell sharply.

In Asia, shares in Japanese tech investment firm Softbank fell by more than 9% on Thursday morning. South Korean semiconductor giants were also down, with Samsung falling by 9.4% and SK Hynix dropping 10.8%.

Tech-heavy indexes in the region were also down. Trading on South Korea's Kospi and Kosdaq was temporarily halted after falling by more than 8%, while Japan's Nikkei 225 fell by over 5%.

World.title: 2027: Tinubu to skip some APC campaign rallies, cites governance demands
World.content:
President Bola Tinubu said he may not attend every campaign rally ahead of the 2027 general election, citing governance demands and the need to meet Nigeria’s financial obligations.

Mr Tinubu made this known on Wednesday during the inauguration of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council at the Banquet Hall of the Presidential Villa in Abuja.

Addressing party leaders and members, the president said his responsibilities as head of state would require him to remain focused on governance. At the same time, campaign officials coordinate activities across states and local government areas.

“Nigeria needs more attention now than ever before. The responsibility of this office does not pause,” he said.

He added that he would continue to address Nigerians directly but would not necessarily accompany the campaign team to every engagement.

“So, you will excuse me from going everywhere with you; we have bills to pay. The American creditors cannot wait,” Mr Tinubu said.

He said the government also needed to attract investors willing to make long-term commitments to Nigeria, suggesting his administration would keep economic and financial responsibilities a priority during the campaign.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The president said he agreed with party members who advised him not to let campaign activities distract him from governing the country.

“You’ve warned me not to allow the rigour of the campaign to distract me from governance, I hear you. I am in full agreement with your decision. Nigeria needs more attention now,” he said.

Tinubu pledges loyalty to APC manifesto

Despite indicating that he might be absent from some campaign engagements, Mr Tinubu pledged to remain committed to the APC’s manifesto and objectives as he seeks re-election in 2027.

“To me, I am your errand man. Even for the president, I raise my hand for full commitment that we abide by my promises and the manifestos, the objective, the intention of our party. That’s all I give you,” he said.

He also praised the party for conducting its congresses and electing leaders at ward, local government, state and national levels, despite predictions that the process could trigger an internal crisis.

Mr Tinubu recalled that the party’s 15th National Executive Committee (NEC) meeting, held on 19 December 2025, ratified the congress programme.

“We conducted it. They said there would be implosion. We passed through it. We did not fail. You did not let us down,” he said.

The president described the campaign council as a vehicle for taking the administration’s record and agenda to Nigerians across the country.

“This council will carry our vision, our record and our agenda to every Nigerian, and it will carry them to every ward of this country. We arrive at this moment strong, united and renewed,” he said.

He warned, however, that the party’s work would not be complete until it secured votes in the next election.

“But no one gets credit for an incomplete assignment. So, until you deliver the next election, until you deliver your wards, until you deliver the votes, before we can say thank you,” he said.

Shettima questions opposition unity

Vice President Kashim Shettima used the occasion to question the ability of opposition politicians seeking to unseat Mr Tinubu to manage Nigeria’s diverse interests, arguing that some had struggled to maintain unity within their own parties.

“Meanwhile, those offering to rescue Nigeria cannot keep their own political households intact,” he said.

Mr Shettima asked how politicians who could not reconcile disagreements among party leaders would manage the competing interests of a country with more than 200 million people.

“So I ask, if reconciling a few party leaders defeats you, how will you reconcile the interests of over 200 million citizens?” he said.

He described the 2027 election as an opportunity for Nigerians to assess the competence, character and policy positions of those seeking the presidency.

The vice president also urged members of the campaign council to engage communities, listen to grievances and present the administration’s case through sustained grassroots mobilisation.

“Every committee of the Presidential Campaign Council must earn its place through hard work, every community must hear our case, and every grievance must receive a patient hearing,” he said.

Defending the administration’s economic reforms, Mr Shettima said Mr Tinubu inherited an economy under severe fiscal pressure and made difficult decisions previous administrations avoided.

“President Bola Tinubu inherited immense expectations on an economy approaching fiscal catastrophe. He confronted the subsidy burden and the currency distortion that rewarded access above enterprise,” he said.

He argued that the administration had prioritised long-term economic stability over immediate political popularity.

Akpabio cautions APC governors

Senate President Godswill Akpabio also addressed the political calculations surrounding the 2027 elections, warning APC governors against abandoning their states in pursuit of other political offices.

“For my brothers who are governors, I want you to know that you must not abandon your people,” he said.

Mr Akpabio, a former governor of Akwa Ibom State, urged the governors to complete their constitutionally permitted eight-year tenure before pursuing other positions.

“I did eight years as a governor. And the constitution says you should do eight years. There’s no need for you to start eyeing another position that is not available,” he said.

He said his experience in politics had taught him the importance of maintaining a strong relationship with the electorate.

“I have been in this business for over 25 years, and I always win. And why I always win is because I stand with people. Go and mend your clothes when they are not torn,” he said.

APC chairman urges campaign team to acknowledge challenges

In his welcome address, APC National Chairman Nentawe Yilwatda urged the campaign council to acknowledge the challenges facing the federal government, explain the administration’s record, and make the case for Mr Tinubu’s re-election.

“We have made so much progress but must acknowledge where we have challenges while explaining the objectives, progress and continuing work of the administration,” he said.

Mr Yilwatda said the campaign should combine an account of the government’s achievements with an honest assessment of its shortcomings and a credible vision for the future.

He said the council must explain what the administration completed, what remains in progress, and what it intends to achieve if returned to office.

“Our responsibility is to explain clearly what has been completed, what is progressing and what remains to be done,” he said.

He added that the party needed to show how its policies and investments would improve the daily lives of Nigerians.

The APC chairman said the party would seek another mandate for Mr Tinubu, arguing that the administration’s reform agenda and development priorities deserved the chance to deliver more results.

The inauguration marked the formal launch of the APC’s presidential campaign structure ahead of the 2027 general election, with party leaders urging members to defend the administration’s record, strengthen grassroots mobilisation and secure support across the country.

World.title: 11th Senate Race: Akpabio courts Tinubu, warns Uzodimma over ambition
World.content:
Senate President Godswill Akpabio openly asked President Bola Tinubu on Wednesday to support his bid for re-election as leader of the 11th Senate in 2027.

He also appealed to the president to discourage Governor Hope Uzodimma of Imo State from aspiring to replace him as Senate president.

Mr Akpabio made the dramatic request at the inauguration of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council at the State House, Abuja.

“Mr President, you already know that we (the National Assembly) are with you. Please, take the advice of Governor Soludo seriously. He (Soludo) said if the cloth is not torn, why try to amend it? If you try to amend it, you are going to tear the cloth,” Mr Akpabio said to Mr Tinubu, in an apparent request for political support in the race for the leadership of the 11th Senate.

“If the National Assembly is so much with you, why not encourage them to come back and support you in your second term?”

Continuing, Mr Akpabio sent a veiled warning to Mr Uzodimma, cautioning him to concentrate on his current responsibilities as governor.

“And for my brothers who are governors, I want you to know: you must not abandon your people. I did eight years as a governor. The constitution says you should do eight years. There is no need for you to start eyeing another position that is not available,” said Mr Akpabio, a former governor of Akwa Ibom State.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“I have been in this business for over 25 years, and I always win,” he added.

Although Mr Akpabio did not mention Mr Uzodimma by name, his warning against governors eyeing other political offices was clearly targeted at the Imo governor, who is the APC senatorial candidate for Imo West District for the 2027 elections.

PREMIUM TIMES understands that Mr Uzodimma has perfected plans to resign as governor before his tenure expires and switch to the Senate if he wins the general election.

Mr Uzodimma’s second term as governor will end in January 2028, while the 11th Senate is expected to be inaugurated in June 2027.

‘I’ll be on the ballot as senatorial candidate’ – Uzodimma

Mr Uzodimma, the secretary of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, told the gathering that the president’s re-election bid was inseparable from the electoral fortunes of other APC candidates, including himself.

“Mr President, you will be on the ballot on 16 January 2027. But if we are honest with ourselves, so will we,” he said.

“I will be on the ballot as a senatorial candidate. So, all of us. The challenge of re-electing Mr President is the challenge of re-electing every member of APC.”

The governor urged party members to resolve internal disagreements and work together to secure victory.

“We must jettison every misgiving we have against each other. We must reconcile our differences. We must rally as one family behind the party and all the candidates,” he said.

He added that the APC had an advantage ahead of the elections because of the “acceptance” of the party by Nigerians and Mr Tinubu’s “record” in office.

“Mr President has made our task easier by giving us a record we can defend with pride,” Mr Uzodimma said.

Senate presidency contest

The Senate presidency is decided by senators, not directly by the president or state governors. The outcome depends on the Senate’s composition after the elections and contenders’ ability to secure their colleagues’ support. However, the president’s support often plays a key role in who emerges as Senate president.

Mr Akpabio’s call for continuity signals his preference to preserve the current legislative arrangement, with him as Senate president.

Mr Uzodimma’s senatorial ambition, meanwhile, introduces another influential political figure into the contest for positions in the next Senate.

I won’t go everywhere with you, Tinubu tells campaign council

President Tinubu, while inaugurating the campaign council, said the council would coordinate campaign activities across states and local government areas, while he would concentrate on running the government.

“The responsibility of this office does not pause,” the president declared.

“I will still make time to speak directly with Nigerians, even as you lead the campaign in the states and local government areas.

“So you will excuse me from going everywhere with you. We have bills to pay.”

The APC Presidential Campaign Council, led by Director-General Abdulaziz Yari, is set to kick off its presidential campaign in Kaduna on 24 October.

Vice President Kashim Shettima, Speaker of the House of Representatives, Abbas Tajudeen, governors, top politicians, and APC youth and women groups, among other dignitaries, attended the event.

World.title: Lagos govt announces demolition of fire-damaged GNI building
World.content:
The Lagos State Government has announced plans to demolish the fire-damaged Great Nigeria Insurance (GNI) building on Lagos Island, warning residents and motorists to keep away from the area during the operation.

The Permanent Secretary of the Lagos State Emergency Management Agency (LASEMA), Olufemi Oke-Osanyintolu, announced the plan in a statement on Wednesday.

He said access to the area would be restricted during the exercise and that temporary traffic diversions might be introduced. He urged motorists to use alternative routes and advised residents to obey instructions from emergency responders and traffic officials.

The planned demolition follows a fire that gutted the building on Martins Street on 24 December 2025, killing 12 people, according to an earlier report by PREMIUM TIMES.

The federal government, through the National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA), deployed heavy-duty equipment provided by the China Civil Engineering Construction Corporation (CCECC) to assist ongoing recovery operations at the site.

NEMA described the multi-agency effort as complex due to the precarious condition of the building.

“Significant progress has been recorded with the controlled removal of debris and recovery of four bodies,” the agency said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Recovery operations were coordinated by NEMA alongside CCECC, with supervision from LASEMA, Lagos Waste Management Authority (LAWMA), and other stakeholders.

The agency stated that the recovered bodies have been documented and handed over to the Lagos State Environmental Health Monitoring Unit (SHEMU) for forensic identification and dignified handling.

Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu subsequently ordered the building’s demolition following concerns about the safety of the fire-damaged structure.

Speaking at the site, the governor confirmed five victims had been identified while three remained unaccounted for as of that time. He said emergency responders continued to search the debris to ensure no one remained trapped.

The governor announced the closure of nearby markets, restricting access to first responders only, and described the tragedy as a reminder of the risks posed by unsafe practices around commercial structures, including improper generator use and shops built close to electricity transformers.

He pledged to personally oversee the recovery process and stressed that surrounding structures may also be removed to prevent further hazards.

The Lagos State Fire and Rescue Service confirmed that the fire started on the fourth floor of the building and spread to adjoining structures and nearby shops, leading to a partial collapse estimated at seven floors. Eight males, including a firefighter, were rescued with varying degrees of injuries, while three males and two females with minor injuries were treated and discharged at the scene.

Mr Oke-Osanyintolu said LASEMA would work with other government agencies to coordinate safety measures during the exercise. However, Wednesday’s statement did not specify when the demolition would begin.

World.title: WAFU B U-17 Qualifiers: Nigeria’s Golden Eaglets lose to Niger in opening game
World.content:
Nigeria’s Golden Eaglets began their 2026 WAFU B U-17 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers campaign with a 2-1 defeat to Niger in Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso.

Abdoul Razaq Zada opened the scoring for Niger in the 19th minute before Abdoul Rakilou doubled the advantage in the 86th minute.

Mubarak Fasiu pulled one back for Nigeria in the fifth minute of added time, but the late goal was insufficient to prevent the Eaglets from suffering defeat in their opening Group B fixture.

The result handed Niger all three points and moved them to the top of the group with four points from two matches.

Niger also secured qualification for the semi-finals following the victory, while Nigeria and Côte d’Ivoire remain in contention for the remaining spot.

Côte d’Ivoire have one point from their opening match, while Nigeria are yet to earn a point. Both teams have a game in hand.

The Eaglets will now need a positive result in their next outing to strengthen their chances of advancing to the semi-finals and keeping their hopes of qualifying for the continental tournament alive.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Niger’s Saminou Salissou Nouhou, who wore the number four shirt, was named Man of the Match for his influential performance in the victory.

The 2026 WAFU B U-17 tournament serves as a qualifying competition for the Africa Cup of Nations, with teams seeking to secure places at the continental finals.

World.title: APC campaign council tasks governors, lawmakers with grassroots mobilisation for Tinubu’s re-election
World.content:
The All Progressives Congress (APC) has charged its governors, lawmakers, council chairmen and party executives to take President Bola Tinubu’s 2027 re-election campaign to the grassroots, saying the party’s control of the three tiers of government gives it an advantage that must be converted into votes.

Hope Uzodimma, Imo State governor and Secretary of the APC Presidential Campaign Council (PCC), gave the charge on Wednesday in Abuja at the inauguration of the council for the 2027 election, where the party’s leadership acknowledged that its extensive political structure would not by itself guarantee victory.

Mr Uzodimma said the party must use its control of the federal, state and local governments to build a coordinated campaign reaching wards and polling units across the country.

Mr Uzodimma said the gathering, which included APC governors, members of the National Assembly, party executives and local government chairmen, represented the party’s political structure across the federation.

“Every campaign is, at heart, local,” Mr Uzodimma said, adding that governors would lead campaigns in their states, council chairmen would take the message to local governments and wards, while legislators and party executives would work through their constituencies and polling units.

He said the party controlled the federal government, majorities in both chambers of the National Assembly, 31 of the 36 states and about 685 of the 774 local government councils.

“This is the strongest position any party has occupied in the Fourth Republic,” he said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

But Mr Uzodimma warned that the APC’s dominance could create complacency if the party assumed its structures automatically translated into voter support.

“A party that controls every tier of government can easily grow comfortable and begin to mistake the size of its structure for the depth of its support,” he said.

“As critical as structures are, it is citizens who vote, and each one of them has to be persuaded.”

He urged party members to campaign peacefully and within the law, saying the conduct of the governing party would influence the tone of the 2027 election.

The governor also asked Mr Tinubu to remain focused on governance rather than allow the campaign to distract him from implementing his policies.

“Please, Your Excellency, leave the heavy lifting of this campaign to us,” he told the president.

Mr Uzodimma said the APC would defend the administration’s economic reforms, including the removal of petrol subsidy and reforms to the tax system, while highlighting what he described as improvements in economic indicators and government programmes.

He cited the Nigerian Education Loan Fund, consumer credit scheme, Renewed Hope Conditional Cash Transfer and infrastructure projects as areas the campaign would present to voters.

Mr Uzodimma said the APC had no excuse not to win the election, but stressed that its members must first reconcile their differences and present a united campaign.

“The primaries are behind us,” he said. “Whatever disagreements they may have left, the success of any one of us cannot be built on the failure of another.”

He said the election would also serve as a referendum on the performance of APC governors, lawmakers and local government chairmen because voters would judge the party across all levels of government.

“Mr President will be on the ballot on 16 January 2027, but if we are honest with ourselves, so will we,” he said.

The governor eventually moved for a vote of confidence in Mr Tinubu’s leadership and committed the council to the Tinubu-Shettima ticket for a second term.

The campaign council secretary said the party’s argument for a second term would be based on the claim that Mr Tinubu’s first term had laid the foundation for economic recovery and that abandoning the reforms midway would amount to starting the process again.

The Speaker of the House of Representatives, Abbas Tajudeen, who is also a member of the campaign council, similarly framed the 2027 election as a choice between continuing Tinubu’s reforms and reversing them.

He said the council’s responsibility was not merely to organise rallies but to explain why “continuity under President Bola Ahmed Tinubu serves Nigeria better than reversal.”

Mr Tajudeen said the APC campaign should acknowledge the economic difficulties faced by Nigerians while presenting evidence of what he described as improvements in the economy.

He said the Nigerian economy grew by 4.2 per cent in the first half of 2026, while external reserves rose above $54 billion in September and the current account surplus reached $12 billion.

He also said non-oil exports exceeded $6 billion in 2025, which he described as the highest figure in the country’s history.

“Stability must reach every household. Revenue must improve public services. Reform must create real opportunities. Growth must produce jobs,” the speaker said.

He said the House had supported the Tinubu administration through legislation on student loans, the minimum wage, tax reforms, the Electoral Act 2026 and other measures.

According to him, the House received 2,747 bills and passed 363 in three years, while more than 70 of the bills had received presidential assent.

Mr Tajudeen told campaign council members to act as “ambassadors of truth, urging them to avoid insults and respond to opposition criticism with evidence.

“An ambassador does not invent evidence. An ambassador masters it,” he said.

“An ambassador does not insult the public. An ambassador respects its intelligence.”

He said the campaign would be taken “constituency by constituency, ward by ward, street by street, door to door.”

Also speaking, Ibrahim Masari, Special Adviser to the President on Political and Other Matters, challenged members of the council to shift their attention from meetings in Abuja to grassroots mobilisation.

Mr Masari said the campaign should focus on polling units, wards, local governments and communities rather than “opening and painting offices” or holding unnecessary meetings.

“Stop talking to yourselves and start talking to the people,” he said.

He said the performance of members of the campaign council would be assessed based on actual results at the grassroots, rather than the number of promises they made.

He also urged party members to avoid hate speech, gossip and personal grievances, and to work for the success of all APC candidates.

World.title: Tinubu’s re-election: Don’t allow repeat of 2023, Tompolo tells Lagos
World.content:
The Leader of the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement, Government Ekpemupolo (alias Tompolo), has advised Lagos State residents not to allow a repeat of what played out in the 2023 election in the state in the 2027 presidential election.

He called on people to take advantage of the ongoing voter registration exercise by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) and get their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) so they can vote massively for one of their own, President Bola Tinubu.

Tompolo, represented by Kestin Pondi, delivered the charge at a campaign rally for Mr Tinubu’s reelection in Lagos on Tuesday, where he presented 57 campaign vehicles to state coordinators.

“What happened in 2023 must not be repeated. He must win convincingly in 2027,” he said.

He described Mr Tinubu as a selfless, courageous leader who did not care about reelection but went on to carry out bold reforms that are already yielding results and benefiting many Nigerians.

Tompolo pointed out that Lagos is now referred to as a city for all Nigerians, thanks to the foundation laid by President Tinubu, which successive governors have built on, and that, now that he has greater responsibility, his own people needed to stand solidly behind him.

“Lagos is the city for all Nigerians because someone stood firm to restructure and reform it. “From the time he came into office in 1999 up to 2007, when he left, Lagos was the envy of other states.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“Today, he has a higher responsibility, an opportunity to replicate the Lagos success story in Nigeria through reforms. “There is massive development across the states today because reforms are working,” he stated.

Tompolo said that to ensure the reforms continue, the people of Lagos and all Nigerians must take the message to every door and everyone.

Also speaking, Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu said Nigeria is attaining economic stability under the Tinubu-led administration.

He advised the people to ignore the antics of opposition politicians who have no plan for Nigeria, are only desperate to win elections, and move from one party to another, showing a lack of consistency, which he emphasised is a bad quality in any leader.

Mr Sanwo-Olu said Mr Tinubu has built more roads than previous administrations in three years, given succour to students, increased the minimum wage, and made money available to pay pensions.

“Why won’t we vote for him? The entire Lagos is for Tinubu. All our votes are for Tinubu. You’ve done it before, you’ll do it again. “We will touch every corner of Lagos with our message to reelect Tinubu. Go out and convince everyone that Tinubu is the candidate to vote for,” the governor stated.

Earlier, the National Coordinator of the movement, Sunday Asuku, urged Lagos residents to get their PVCs so they can vote massively for Tinubu.

“We must stand our ground and deliver Tinubu with PVCs, not with guns or intimidation. Lagos must not put their son, Tinubu, to shame,” he said.

He said, in the 2027 presidential election, Nigerians must make a bold statement by retiring”serial contenders “, whom he described as “enemies of Nigeria.”

World.title: Tinubu urges judges to close loopholes delaying corruption trials
World.content:
President Bola Tinubu has urged Nigerian judges to close procedural loopholes that politically exposed persons and organised crime suspects exploit to delay or frustrate criminal trials.

He said the fight against corruption would make little progress without an independent judiciary willing to adapt to emerging forms of financial crime.

Mr Tinubu spoke on Tuesday in Abuja at the eighth annual capacity-building workshop for judges and justices organised by the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) and the National Judicial Institute (NJI). He was represented by Vice President Kashim Shettima.

“Probe prosecution strategies, dismantle outdated precedents, and seal procedural gaps that politically exposed persons and organised crime actors exploit to delay or frustrate trial,” the president said.

In a statement shared with PREMIUM TIMES on Wednesday by Stanley Nkwocha, the media aide to the vice president, Mr Tinubu explained that corruption was not the responsibility of the executive alone, as it affected all arms of government and the wider society.

“We must no longer permit legal pyrotechnics and procedural pedantry to shelter criminality,” he said.

He urged judges to ensure that legal procedures did not become a shield for wrongdoing, adding that the courts must uphold the public interest.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Digital crimes pose new challenges

Mr Tinubu said advances in blockchain technology and artificial intelligence had made financial crimes more sophisticated, requiring investigators, prosecutors and judges to strengthen their capacity to respond.

At the workshop, themed “Investigation and Prosecution of Economic and Financial Crimes in a Digital Age”, he cited the EFCC’s recovery of cryptocurrency and other digital assets as evidence of progress in tackling technology-related financial crimes.

According to the president, the commission secured the forfeiture of $22,417.91 worth of Bitcoin, 1,001,301.87 USDT in digital assets and $5.6 million linked to the CBEX scheme in 2025.

He also stated that 192 foreign nationals arrested for cyberterrorism and cryptocurrency fraud had been prosecuted and deported.

Mr Tinubu urged the judiciary to improve its capacity to handle cases involving digital evidence and virtual assets, warning that the justice system risked falling behind technological developments.

He commended Chief Justice of Nigeria (CJN) Kudirat Kekere-Ekun for her efforts to reform the judiciary and pledged the federal government’s support for improving justice delivery in the digital age.

CJN calls for better case management

In her remarks at the event, Ms Kekere-Ekun stated that technological developments had changed how digital evidence was obtained and recorded, making effective case management increasingly important.

She said continued training for judicial officers was helping to improve case management and the administration of justice.

The Senate Committee Chairman on Anti-Corruption and Financial Crimes, Emmanuel Udende, noted that the workshop was timely given the growing sophistication of financial crimes, particularly cases involving politically exposed persons.

He said the National Assembly would continue to support the fight against corruption through legislation.

The Attorney-General of the Federation (AGF) and Minister of Justice, Lateef Fagbemi, represented by the Director of Public Prosecution, Rotimi Oyedepo, called for greater cooperation among government institutions and other stakeholders.

Mr Fagbemi, a Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN) urged judges and lawyers to use the workshop to improve their capacity to support thorough investigations and diligent prosecutions.

The Administrator of the NJI, Babatunde Adejumo, said the institute’s partnership with the EFCC had become an important part of efforts to strengthen the judiciary’s response to financial crimes.

EFCC Chairman Ola Olukoyede stated that the workshop was an important part of both institutions’ annual programmes.

He said the commission had recorded significant convictions and financial recoveries over the past three years and stressed the need for recovered funds and assets to be managed transparently.

Mr Olukoyede also expressed concern that technological developments were advancing faster than the legal tools available to investigate and prosecute financial crimes.

World.title: Kenya confirms second Ebola case as contact develops symptoms in quarantine
World.content:
Kenya has confirmed a second case of Ebola, involving a 39-year-old man who developed symptoms while in quarantine, 10 days after the country’s first confirmed patient died.

The development comes barely a week after PREMIUM TIMES reported Kenya’s first imported case of the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola virus, linked to the ongoing outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC).

In a report by the BBC, the second patient was identified as a close relative of the first case and developed symptoms on Tuesday, 13 October, while already in quarantine under health authorities’ monitoring.

The Kenyan Ministry of Health said the two cases were linked and there was no evidence of transmission in the wider community.

Contact tracing continues

The first patient, a 40-year-old Kenyan man who had travelled from the DRC through Uganda, died on 5 October after testing positive for Ebola in Nairobi.

As previously reported by PREMIUM TIMES, his infection raised concerns about the risk of cross-border transmission and prompted Nigeria to review its preparedness for a possible imported case.

Following the second confirmation, Kenyan health authorities continued efforts to trace people who had contact with the first patient.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Of the 128 contacts identified, 113 had been located as of Tuesday, including 108 who were in quarantine in Kenya. Efforts to trace the remaining 15 contacts were continuing.

The health ministry said the early detection of the second case had improved the patient’s chances of recovery and reduced the risk of further transmission.

It advised residents to seek prompt medical attention if they developed fever, unusual tiredness, muscle or joint pain, vomiting, diarrhoea or unexplained bleeding.

Ebola

Ebola is a severe viral disease that can cause serious illness and death. It spreads through direct contact with the blood or other bodily fluids of an infected person who is showing symptoms, or the body of someone who has died from the disease.

Symptoms may include fever, fatigue, muscle pain, vomiting and diarrhoea. The incubation period ranges from two to 21 days, meaning symptoms can develop several weeks after exposure.

The current outbreak in the DRC is caused by the Bundibugyo species of Ebola virus. The outbreak has also been linked to cases reported in other countries, including Uganda.

Unlike some other Ebola virus species, Bundibugyo has no specifically approved vaccine or treatment. However, supportive medical care can improve a patient’s chances of survival.

World.title: 2027: We’re preparing to win, Atiku, Obi ‘shooting the breeze’  —  APC spokesperson
World.content:
APC spokesman Felix Morka

The All Progressives Congress (APC) has expressed its readiness and preparedness to win the 2027 general elections, accusing opposition figures such as Atiku Abubakar and Peter Obi of simply “shooting the breeze” instead of speaking for themselves.

The APC National Publicity Secretary, Felix Morka, stated this on Channels Television’s Politics Today, while responding to questions about the party’s preparations for the next general elections, shortly after the inauguration of the ruling party’s Presidential Campaign Council on Wednesday, in Abuja.

Morka said the APC was leaving nothing to chance as it prepared for another electoral contest, adding that the party had won bye-elections since the last general elections.

“Virtually all elections that has been called, bye-elections, whatever election, since the last general elections, we’ve won fantastically. There is a reason for that. It is because we prepare, we do not take anything or leave anything to chance,” he said.

He added that the party was putting its structures and campaign machinery in place ahead of the elections.

“We prepare, we do our homework, we put together our systems and we trigger massive campaigns, which is what we are about to do,” Morka said.

The APC spokesman dismissed suggestions that the party’s preparations were a sign of desperation, arguing that the ruling party was focused on its electoral strategy.

“So, look, I don’t think it’s a sign of desperation to prepare. As a matter of fact, I think we are more preparing than the people in the opposition,” he said.

Morka specifically criticised Atiku and Obi, accusing them of focusing on the shortcomings of President Bola Tinubu’s administration rather than speaking for themselves.

“The Atikus, The Peter Obis, who are simply shooting the breeze, doing nothing to speak for themselves rather than tell you what you think the president is not doing or should be doing,” he said.

He maintained that the APC was focused on its own preparations and its ambition to retain electoral success in 2027.

“We mind our business and we are in this to compete and win the next election,” Morka added.

Earlier in the interview, when asked whether Nigerians liked and believed in the APC, Morka argued that the party’s position as the governing party at the federal level and in several states demonstrated public support.

“First of all, let me remind you that the APC is the governing party in this country, put in office by Nigerians. So, already, the answer to your question has been codified in an election of the APC, that is governing, not just at the centre but in so many states of our country. So, the answer is yes,” he said.

World.title: Death penalty: Foreign missions applaud Nigeria’s abolitionist shift
World.content:
Nigeria Flag

By Ikechukwu Nnochiri

As the number of death row inmates in the country continues to swell, stakeholders in the justice sector and concerned foreign missions have nonetheless commended Nigeria for going ten consecutive years without a state execution.

The Nigerian Correctional Service (NCoS) recently disclosed that 4,329 persons are currently awaiting execution in various custodial facilities across the federation.

Of this number, more than 82 are women.

In its presentation at an event commemorating the 2026 World Day Against the Death Penalty, the NCoS acknowledged the need for national action on capital punishment, a process it said would ultimately require a constitutional amendment.

“Everybody in our custody has a story, and the way we treat those stories says a lot about our society,” the Comptroller-General of the NCoS, Mr. Sylvester Nwakuche, stated.

The World Day Against the Death Penalty is observed every year on October 10.

This year’s event was jointly organised by the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) and Avocats Sans Frontières France (also known as Lawyers Without Borders), with support from the Australian High Commission in Nigeria, the Embassy of the Federal Republic of Germany, and the Embassy of Spain.

A key outcome of the programme was participants’ unanimous call for a moratorium on executions and for the commutation of existing death sentences to life imprisonment.

The last execution in Nigeria took place on December 23, 2016, when three death row inmates were put to death in Benin, Edo State.

Unsurprisingly, the executions drew varied reactions, with Amnesty International condemning them in strong terms.

It noted that they were carried out even though one of the inmates, Apostle Igene, was sentenced to death in 1997 by a military tribunal and was never afforded the opportunity to appeal the verdict.

The Executive Secretary of the NHRC, Dr. Tony Ojukwu, SAN, observed that, under Nigerian law, capital punishment presents a constitutional duality.

He stated that whereas Section 33(1) of the 1999 Constitution (as amended) protects the right to life, it also contains an explicit exception for court-ordered executions.

On the other hand, Section 34(1)(a) guarantees the right to human dignity and protection against inhuman or degrading treatment.

According to Ojukwu, the Supreme Court affirmed the constitutional validity of capital punishment in Onuoha Kalu v. The State (1998) 13 NWLR (Pt. 583) 531, reaffirmed in Joseph Amoshima v. The State (2011) 14 NWLR (Pt. 1268) 547.

“However, the constitutionality of the penalty does not dilute the non-negotiable requirement of fair trial guarantees under Section 36.

Systemic issues, such as inadequate pro bono defence, forced confessions, and pre-trial delays, undermine procedural justice,” he added.

Ojukwu, SAN, argued that Nigeria, having achieved 10 consecutive years without a state execution, has satisfied the international standard for a de facto moratorium.

“Yet, mandatory death sentencing continues, leaving over 3,000 individuals on prolonged death row detention.

“To resolve this limbo, statutory and executive mechanisms exist. Section 12(2)(c) of the Nigerian Correctional Service Act, 2019 authorises the commutation of death sentences for inmates who have exhausted appeals and remain unexecuted after a specified period.

“Furthermore, State Governors possess explicit constitutional powers of prerogative of mercy under Section 212 (and the President under Section 175) of the 1999 Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria.

“Pursuant to Section 5 of the NHRC (Amendment) Act 2010, the Commission calls for three immediate policy steps:

Transition Nigeria’s 10-year pause into an official executive moratorium on executions.

“Urge State Governors to systematically invoke Section 212 of the Constitution and Section 12(2)(c) of the NCoS Act to commute death sentences to life imprisonment.

“Re-evaluate mandatory death penalty statutes to allow judges to weigh mitigating circumstances and systemic vulnerabilities during sentencing,” he added.

Prior to 1990, only one country in Africa, Cape Verde, had abolished the death penalty.

However, of the 55 African Union member-states, 28 have now abolished it in law, with Zimbabwe the latest to join the list.

While 20 countries apply a long-term moratorium on executions, seven nations, including Nigeria, still retain and use capital punishment.

German Ambassador to Nigeria, H.E. Stefan Rössel, said that although the death penalty remains part of Nigerian law, the 10-year mark since the last execution is an important milestone that deserves to be celebrated.

Drawing on his country’s experience, the Ambassador said: “Germany opposes the death penalty unconditionally. Working towards its permanent abolition is a pillar of our human rights policy.

“We believe that the right to life is universal, as laid out in the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, and must not be denied by law.

“The last execution on German soil took place in 1981. Today, Article 102 of the German constitution states simply: ‘Capital punishment is abolished.'”

He said the death penalty raises important questions about justice, human dignity and the protection of human life.

“We recognise the deep suffering caused by serious crimes. The grief of victims and their families must be acknowledged, and their need for justice, truth and support deserves our continued attention.

“At the same time, every justice system must protect human rights and guard against the possibility of error. A death sentence is irreversible. If a conviction is later found to be wrong, the consequences cannot be undone.

“We must also not forget that those sentenced to death often spend years, sometimes decades, behind bars before being executed. At the same time, our understanding of crimes and justice continuously evolves.

“For instance, we have gained a much more nuanced understanding of mental illness in recent decades, and how that might affect the way we judge the circumstances of a crime committed many years ago.

“Ultimately, we need to ask ourselves: do we want to live in a society in which the state is tasked to take a human life?” he queried.

The German Ambassador concluded by recognising that the issue of the death penalty is complex, involving legal questions, public concerns and the needs of victims and their families.

“We hope that Nigeria’s approaching 10-year milestone can be a source of pride. We believe: not using this ultimate form of punishment is a sign of strength, not weakness,” he added.

Likewise, the Australian High Commissioner to Nigeria, H.E. Ms. Leilani Bin-Juda, PSM, described the 10-year non-execution achieved by Nigeria as “a significant milestone that calls for a reflection of how far Nigeria has come and the next step to be taken.”

She urged the country to build on the achievement and chart a way forward, insisting that capital punishment is a cruel, inhumane and degrading punishment that has no place in any modern justice system.

For his part, the Ambassador of Spain to Nigeria, H.E. Félix Costales Artieda, categorically opposed the use of the death penalty “under any circumstance and for any crime.”

He insisted that life is an inalienable fundamental right that no state has the right to take, stressing that there is no evidence that capital punishment has helped to reduce crime anywhere in the world.

The Ambassador noted that in the United States alone, 130 persons sentenced to death have been found innocent and released from death row since 1973.

He urged Nigeria to take appropriate measures to commute the sentences of those already facing the death penalty.

The Country Head of ASF France, Angela Uwandu Uzoma-Iwuchukwu, said the organisation, on the basis of its conviction that the right to life is sacrosanct, had embarked on a series of projects aimed at highlighting the need for Nigeria to do away with capital punishment.

She said it has since represented over 1,000 persons through its Right To Life project.

Referencing the case of Arthur Angel, who spent 16 years in prison, 10 of them on death row at Enugu Prison, before his release in 2000, she argued that lapses in a justice system run by humans cannot be overlooked.

“Arthur Angel spent 16 years in jail for a crime he did not commit,” she noted, insisting the death penalty is “discriminatory as it targets the weakest in the society.

“There are people who cannot afford the services of good lawyers. We all know that the quality of defence provided for a defendant matters so much.

“A lot of those on death row in Nigeria were represented by inexperienced lawyers, some of whom were National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) members.

“A mistake made at the trial stage may not be corrected at the appeal stage,” the ASF Country Head added.

She also referenced a recent case involving a poor farmer, Sunday Jackson, who was sentenced to death for self-defence but later pardoned by the Adamawa State Government.

For now, Nigeria’s position is a contradiction: a death penalty on the books, thousands waiting under sentence, and no one carrying it out.

Hopes are high that the 10-year milestone will become a step towards the abolition of capital punishment in the country.

World.title: Breaking: Popular gospel singer Toluwanisings is dead
World.content:
Nigerian gospel singer Olayemi Bolaji, popularly known as Toluwanisings, has died.

The singer reportedly passed away in the early hours of Wednesday, October 14, 2026, according to a statement released by his family on his Instagram account.

In the statement, the family identified him as Minister Olayemi Bayonile Bolaji of the Toluwani Gospel Music Ministry (TOGOMM), describing him as a beloved husband, family member and gospel minister.

The statement read, “With deep sorrow, the family announces the passing of Minister Olayemi Bayonile Bolaji, Toluwani Gospel Music Ministry (TOGOMM), who passed away in the early hours of 14 October 2026.

“A dearly loved husband, family member, and gospel minister.

“Please keep his wife, family, and loved ones in your prayers during this difficult time.”

The family added that details of his funeral arrangements would be communicated in due course.

News of his death has drawn emotional reactions from fans, colleagues and other public figures on social media, with many mourning the loss of the gospel artiste.

As of the time of filing this report, the cause of Toluwanisings’ death had not been disclosed.

World.title: Pope Leo XIV’s brother also battling cancer – report
World.content:
Pope Leo XIV delivers a speech during a ceremony following his meeting with France’s President at the Elysee Presidential Palace, in Paris on September 25, 2026 at the start of Pope’s four days visit to France. (Photo by Teresa SUAREZ / POOL / AFP)

A brother of Pope Leo XIV is receiving treatment for blood cancer, a report has said, a day after the pontiff underwent surgery that revealed a diagnosis of lung cancer.

A source close to the Prevost family told NBC 5 Chicago’s Mary Ann Ahern that the pope’s brother, Louis, was being treated for blood cancer.

However, no further details were available about Louis’ prognosis or how long he had been undergoing treatment.

The development comes after Pope Leo underwent surgery in Rome, during which doctors confirmed he had lung adenocarcinoma, a type of non-small cell lung cancer.

According to Harvard Medical School, lung adenocarcinoma develops when abnormal cells in the lungs multiply uncontrollably and form a tumour.

The Lung Cancer Foundation of America identifies the disease as the most common type of lung cancer, accounting for approximately 40 per cent of cases.

The Vatican said the lower lobe of the pope’s right lung was removed during the procedure earlier this week.

Although details of the pontiff’s prognosis have not been made public, Dr Stephen Liu, a lung cancer expert at Georgetown University’s Lombardi Comprehensive Cancer Center, said the outlook would depend partly on the stage of the disease.

“Adenocarcinoma is the most common (type of lung cancer), also with the most favorable prognosis,” Liu said. “While we know the diagnosis we now need to know the stage.”

World.title: UCL: Real Madrid stage dramatic comeback to beat Roma 4-3
World.content:
Real Madrid scored three late goals to overturn a two-goal deficit and secure a dramatic 4-3 victory over Roma in the UEFA Champions League on Jose Mourinho’s return to the Stadio Olimpico.

Madrid appeared destined for defeat after Roma took a 3-1 lead in the 83rd minute, but substitutes Carlos Espi and Endrick inspired a stunning comeback before Antonio Rudiger struck the decisive goal in the 90th minute.

The victory extended Real Madrid’s perfect start to their Champions League campaign, having won both matches, while Roma were left with one point from their opening two games.

Mourinho, who previously led Roma to the Europa Conference League title in 2021-22 and the Europa League final the following season, received a warm reception from the home supporters, who displayed banners celebrating his time at the Italian club.

Roma made a strong start and took the lead in the 20th minute when Marten de Roon fired a first-time effort from the edge of the box after being set up by Matias Soule.

Real Madrid responded five minutes later through Kylian Mbappe, whose effort took a deflection off Gianluca Mancini before looping over goalkeeper Pierluigi Gollini.

The goal was Mbappe’s 72nd in the Champions League, moving him ahead of Real Madrid legend Raul, who finished his career in the competition with 71 goals. The appearance also marked the French forward’s 100th match in the tournament.

Roma regained control after the break, with Donyell Malen scoring twice in a six-minute spell to put the hosts in a commanding position.

Malen made it 2-1 after capitalising on a mistake by Vinicius Junior, whose attempted flick gave away possession. The striker’s shot took a deflection off Real Madrid captain Federico Valverde before finding the net.

The Dutch forward struck again soon afterwards, finishing calmly to extend Roma’s advantage to 3-1. Although the goal was initially ruled out for offside, a video assistant referee review confirmed that Valverde had kept Malen onside.

Roma manager Gian Piero Gasperini introduced several defensive substitutes as he attempted to protect the lead, but Real Madrid’s late attacking changes proved decisive.

Espi pulled one back five minutes after coming on, converting the rebound after Gollini had parried Endrick’s header.

Endrick then levelled the contest by heading home from an Arda Guler corner, leaving Roma struggling to contain Madrid’s set-piece threat.

The visitors completed the turnaround in the 90th minute when Rudiger volleyed home from close range following another Guler delivery to seal a remarkable 4-3 win.

The result provides a boost for Real Madrid as they continue their Champions League campaign, while Roma will need to improve after failing to hold on to their advantage on home soil.

World.title: ‘Expanded APC Campaign Council a confession of fear’ — Atiku
World.content:
Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has described the expanded presidential campaign council of the All Progressives Congress (APC) as a “confession of fear”, accusing President Bola Tinubu of prioritising political alliances over Nigeria’s economic hardship and insecurity.

Atiku, the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), said the expansion of the council for the 2027 general election reflected the president’s concern about his political standing rather than the challenges facing Nigerians.

In a statement issued on Wednesday by Phrank Shaibu, director of strategic communication of the ADC presidential campaign council, Atiku argued that the inclusion of more political figures would not address hunger, violence, kidnappings and the rising cost of living.

“Only a man afraid of his record would think he could bury it under hundreds of names,” the statement reads.

“Tinubu can gather every governor, minister and political defector in Nigeria. None of them can erase the hunger in people’s homes, bring back those killed by violence or free Nigerians still held captive. Their families are waiting for answers, not another campaign list.”

The APC initially released its presidential campaign council list on August 22, naming Abdulaziz Yari, former governor of Zamfara State, as director-general. The expanded council includes Nyesom Wike, minister of the Federal Capital Territory;

Ademola Adeleke, governor of Osun State; and Chukwuma Soludo, governor of Anambra State.

Atiku also accused Tinubu of maintaining an extensive political structure while Nigerians grapple with the consequences of rising prices and declining purchasing power.

“Tinubu has room for an army of ministers and a stadium full of campaign officials, but no room in his plans for Nigerians crushed by the cost of living. He feeds his political machine and tells hungry families to sacrifice,” he said.

The former vice-president maintained that adding more names to the campaign council would not change Nigerians’ experiences under the current administration.

He also faulted the decision to inaugurate the APC campaign council at the Presidential Villa in Abuja, describing the venue as public property that should not be used for partisan political activities.

“The Presidential Villa belongs to the Nigerian people. It is not a campaign venue or the private property of any political party. Using it for an APC political event is a gross breach of public trust and a troubling abuse of public office,” he said.

Questioning the choice of venue, Atiku argued that Abuja had sufficient alternative locations for the event.

“Abuja has no shortage of halls and public spaces large enough to host a campaign gathering. Why, then, did Bola Tinubu choose to inaugurate his campaign council at night, behind the gates of the Presidential Villa?” he asked.

He said the decision raised questions about the president’s confidence in his performance, adding that Nigerians should assess his

administration based on their experiences.

“Nigerians may draw their own conclusions. But a president confident in his record should be willing to face the public in daylight and ask for another mandate,” he said.

Atiku further described the expanded council as an attempt to shield Tinubu from public criticism by recruiting more political figures, including members of other parties.

“When the first list drew criticism, Tinubu had a chance to show that he understood the country’s anger. Instead, he returned with an even longer list, reaching into other parties for more names. He is collecting politicians like shields against public judgment,” he said.

The ADC presidential candidate also cited a claim that 17.9 million more Nigerians were living in multidimensional poverty, linking the figure to the economic and security challenges confronting the country.

He argued that the enlarged campaign structure would do little to make food affordable or improve the purchasing power of workers and other citizens.

“No campaign council, however crowded, can make food affordable, restore a worker’s purchasing power or explain why the sacrifices demanded of ordinary Nigerians never seem to reach Tinubu’s own political circle,” he said.

Atiku said the ADC had assembled its own campaign team to offer Nigerians an alternative, insisting that voters would ultimately judge the president by their living conditions rather than the number of political figures backing his re-election bid.

“On January 16, the ballot will contain no column for the size of a campaign council. Nigerians will judge Tinubu by the lives they have lived under his government,” he added.
