World.title: PSG beat Manchester City 4-2 away in Champions League
World.content:
Manchester City’s Norwegian striker #09 Erling Haaland (2R) misses with this header during the UEFA Champions League, league phase football match between Manchester City and Paris Saint Germain at the Etihad Stadium in Manchester, north west England, on October 14, 2026. (Photo by Oli SCARFF / AFP)

Reigning champions Paris Saint-Germain staved off a second-half comeback to win 4-2 away to Manchester City in their Champions League showdown on Wednesday.

PSG were 3-0 up in the first half with goals by Desire Doue, Ousmane Dembele and Vitinha, but Erling Haaland scored twice after the break for City. Maghnes Akliouche got PSG’s fourth before Ferran Torres had a late penalty saved.

World.title: 2027: You’re tired, weak, go home – Adebayo tells Tinubu
World.content:
Presidential candidate of the Social Democratic Party, SDP, for 2027, Prince Adewole Adebayo, has urged President Bola Tinubu to go home and let Nigeria breathe.

Adebayo said this in a statement, in Abuja, on Wednesday.

He was responding to the President’s plan to excuse himself from the rigors of physical campaigns in some states ahead of the presidential polls.

Tinubu spoke at the inauguration of the APC Presidential Campaign Council in Abuja, where he urged members to take the party’s message to Nigerians across the states and local government areas while he continues to attend to matters of governance.

In response, Adebayo said if Tinubu is too tired to campaign, he is too weak to govern.

In a statement signed by his Presidential Campaign’s Chief Communications Adviser, Comrade Mark Adebayo, the SDP candidate described Tinubu as a “president in absentia” at a time Nigeria needs hands-on leadership.

Adebayo said, “Nigeria is too complex, too dynamic, and currently too distressed to be governed by remote control.”

He cited what he called repeated instances of the President governing from a distance, including prolonged medical vacations disguised as working visits, absence during national emergencies and reliance on proxies to announce state policies.

The SDP candidate further said, “We have seen repeated instances where the President is visibly missing when the country needs reassurance.

“From unannounced foreign trips during critical economic decisions to his complete silence during widespread regional protests, he has consistently acted like a president in absentia. If you are too tired to campaign, you are too weak to govern.”

Adebayo alleged that the decision to stay off the campaign trail was not about strategy but fear.

“The excuse of bowing out of the 2027 campaign is a cowardly smokescreen. The truth is that the President is terrified of the Nigerian people,” he argued.

According to him, the administration’s economic policies – fuel subsidy removal fallout, skyrocketing inflation and currency instability -have made the President unpopular.

“He knows the pain his bad policies have inflicted on families. He is hiding because he cannot face public anger, and he knows any appearance on a campaign trail will be met with collective booing of a betrayed populace.”

Adebayo also said, “It is time to face reality: step aside, go home, and let this country breathe.”

He called on the administration to prioritise national interest over political survival and be transparent about the President’s capacity to lead for the remainder of his term.

World.title: Tinubu: I’m Ready to Renew Pact With Nigerians, Inaugurates 2027 Campaign Council
World.content:
• Says governance must not be grounded, as Nigeria needs fixing

•Shettima throws jabs at Atiku, Obi, says nation can’t be governed with borrowed statistics

• Yari: campaign for Tinubu will be performance driven

•Wike to APC Govs: don’t claim Tinubu’s victory if you failed to deliver your states

• Yilwatda: Tinubu’s reforms deserve continuity

•Rainbow coalition on course for Tinubu’s 2027 victory, senate maintains

• Sani tasks appointees on president’s election

•Atiku: inauguration of Tinubu’s campaign council in Aso Rock abuse of public office

• APC’s campaign council a Nebuchadnezzar coalition heading for the rocks, says MDPCO

•Soludo, Adeleke optimistic about Tinubu’s victory

Deji Elumoye, Chuks Okocha, Emmanuel Addeh, Adedayo Akinwale, Sunday Aborisade in Abuja and John Shiklam in Kaduna





President Bola Tinubu, yesterday, declares his readiness to renew covenant with Nigerians ahead of the official launch of his second term campaign, billed to kick off in Kaduna on October 24.

The president, who foreclosed the possibility of being present at all the campaign grounds nationwide, said the pressing needs of the country required his attention, stressing that governance must continue side-by-side electioneering.

Speaking while inaugurating the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council for the 2027 poll, he said while the council would lead the party’s mobilisation across the states and local government areas, he would make time to address Nigerians directly without accompanying the campaign to every location.

Tinubu said he agreed with party leaders, especially Governor Hope Uzodinma of Imo State, who advised him not to allow campaign activities to distract him from official duties.

Vice President Kashim Shettima, speaking at the occasion, threw jabs at former Vice President Atiku Abubakar and Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) presidential candidate, Peter Obi.

Shettima questioned both candidates’ economic interventions and their readiness to lead Nigeria.

He said the country’s size, population, and economic realities made it unsuitable for policies copied from other countries without proper adaptation to local realities.

In his acceptance speech, Director-General of APC Presidential Campaign Council (APC-PCC), Senator Abdulaziz Yari, said Tinubu’s achievements since May 2023 and his future plans would form the basis of the party’s campaign for the January 16, 2027 presidential poll.

Yari said the campaign would focus on communicating the administration’s record to Nigerians, particularly its impact on ordinary citizens, and its infrastructure projects.

Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, who is also a member of the APC campaign council, told coordinators of Tinubu’s 2027 re-election campaign not to claim victory if they failed to deliver their respective states.

Wike, though a member of Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), said every campaign official must be held accountable for their electoral performance.

Relatedly, the Senate, yesterday, declared that the rainbow coalition incorporated into the APC-PCC for Tinubu’s re-election in 2027 was on course, describing the initiative as an unprecedented political alliance aimed at promoting national unity and inclusive governance.

President of the Senate, Godswill Akpabio, and Senate Leader, Opeyemi Bamidele, made the remarks yesterday at plenary.

However, Atiku, yesterday, condemned the inauguration of Tinubu’s campaign council inside the Presidential Villa, Abuja, describing it as an abuse of public office and a troubling breach of public trust.

He said this in a statement by Director of Strategic Communication of African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council (ADC-PCC), Phrank Shaibu.

Nonetheless, Tinubu, at the inauguration of the APC-PCC in Abuja, said, “As I stand before you with a heart full of gratitude and spirit full of resolve, it is my honour to inaugurate the presidential campaign council of the All Progressives Congress for the 2027 General Election.

“I thank all of you for the last election, but no one gets credit for an incomplete assignment until you deliver the next election, until you deliver your electoral wards, until you deliver the votes.”

Tinubu acknowledged Uzodinma’s advice not to let the rigours of the election campaign distract him from his responsibilities of governance, said, “I hear you. I am in full agreement with your decision. Nigeria needs more attention now than ever before. The responsibility of this office does not pause.”

Uzodimma, in his speech, had assured the president that the governors and other party leaders would do their best to deliver the right message to Nigerians during the campaign.

On why he would not travel to every campaign ground, the president said the government had pressing financial obligations and needed to attract investors to support the country’s future.

According to him, “The job must go on. We have bills to pay. The American creditors cannot wait. We want those investors to come in, be here to stay, to invest for the future of our children.

“However, I will still make time to speak directly with Nigerians even as you lead the campaign in the states and local government areas.”

He charged the campaign council to take the party’s record, vision and agenda to Nigerians nationwide up to the ward level.

“Let the word go out from this hall to every corner of our nation. The APC is ready,” Tinubu said, adding that APC is renewing its commitment to Nigerians and the responsibilities entrusted to it as the governing party.

The president stated, “We have gathered not merely to inaugurate a council. We have gathered to renew a covenant, a covenant with the Nigerian people and the historic responsibility they have thrust to us as Nigeria’s governing party. We promise we will not let them down.”

He also warned all the 31 APC governors, as well as federal lawmakers and other party leaders against taking previous electoral efforts for granted, insisting that their performance in the 2027 election would determine whether they have fulfilled their assignment.

He stated, “No one gets credit for an incomplete assignment. So until you deliver the next election, until you deliver your wards, until you deliver the votes, before we can say thank you.”

Tinubu pledged to support legislative efforts to increase women’s representation in the National Assembly and state-level legislatures, describing women as key mobilisers and voters.

He said, “Women are the greatest mobilisers and voters. And from this hall, I assure you, the sponsorship of the bill.”

He urged women to work towards securing greater representation, while promising to support efforts to increase their numbers at both national and sub-national levels.

The president said, “The women deserve seats. Go and work for it, come to fruition. We will increase the number of women’s representation at both National Assembly and sub-national level. I assure you that.”

Tinubu, while commenting on security, gave an assurance that state police would become a reality, signalling his support for the proposed restructuring of policing in the country.

“On security, state police will be a reality,” he declared.

The president lauded the party leadership for conducting its congresses and strengthening its structures from the ward to the national level, describing APC as increasingly united.

He charged party members to remain determined in their efforts to build the country, recalling measures taken during his tenure as Lagos State governor to address the threat of flooding from the Atlantic Ocean.

“There is a limit, but there is no limit in daring. We dared the Atlantic Ocean, and the result is the Atlantic City in Lagos,” he said.

He commended Lagos State Governor Babajide Samwo-Olu and his Deputy, Obafemi Hamzat, for their contributions to the success he recorded during his term as governor of the state, especially in taming the encroachment by the Atlantic Ocean.

Speaking at the inauguration, Shettima threw political jabs at Atiku and Obi, questioning their economic interventions and readiness to lead Nigeria ahead of next year’s general election.

Criticising Obi’s reliance on foreign economic comparisons, Shettima said, “A country of over 250 million people cannot be governed through borrowed statistics and economic prescriptions detached from its peculiarities.”

According to him, policies that worked in Bangladesh could not simply be replicated in Nigeria without considering differences in population, economic structures, institutions and national circumstances.

He stated, “I respect Peter Obi. But he has gone beyond his mastery of philosophy to make an august claim about winning the 2023 presidential election without adducing a shred of evidence to buttress his assertion.

“Obi is the master of bogus statistics and incoherent economic prescriptions.”

Shettima compared the challenge of applying foreign policies to Nigeria to transferring a cloth meant for a smaller body onto a much bigger one.

He also faulted Atiku, who had several times in the past sought the presidency, saying political ambition must be matched by character, discipline and an understanding of the responsibilities attached to public office.

He was, however, quick to add that political opponents should be treated with respect, as they were fellow Nigerians and not enemies.

Shettima said, “For the rest of the duration of this campaign, we’ll discuss ideas, we’ll discuss policies, but we’ll treat all our opponents with respect and dignity. They are not our enemies. They are our brothers. They are our countrymen. They are our leaders.”

Shettima told the party leaders not to insult opponents in the course of the campaign, urging them, instead, to respond to criticism with evidence and reason.

He said, “We have the capacity to respond to all sorts of innuendos and outright lies that our political opponents are taking on. But we won’t fall into their traps. We’ll give them facts. We’ll give them statistics. We argue with reason, not with sentiments, not with exaggerated truth or fabricated lies.”

The vice president said the Tinubu administration over three years ago inherited an economy facing severe fiscal pressures and it had taken difficult decisions, including removing the petrol subsidy and addressing distortions in the foreign exchange market.

He explained that the reforms were necessary to address longstanding economic challenges, while acknowledging the responsibility to ensure that their benefits reached Nigerians.

“The next obligation is to turn these gains into jobs, meaningful earnings and meaningful planning,” Shettima stated, maintaining that the administration’s priority should be to protect the reforms, improve their implementation, and ensure that public resources deliver results for households and businesses.

He said, “We must protect the reforms, improve their execution, and carry their benefits from the treasury to the household.”

He said Tinubu deserved a second term because the government’s reform programme had gained momentum, which the country could not afford to squander.

“President Tinubu deserves a second term because the work has acquired momentum that Nigeria cannot afford to squander,” Shettima said.

Yari said Tinubu’s achievements in office and his future plans for the country would form the basis of the party’s 2027 campaign.

He stated, “As we start going around to royal fathers and clerics, this is the message I have been sending today: our campaign is going to be centred on what you have done and what you are going to do in the future.”

Yari commended the president for his achievements in infrastructure development and improving the lives of ordinary Nigerians, adding that his record has made the campaign team’s assignment easier.

He said, “You have touched the life of the ordinary man. You have been there in infrastructure, building the iron road as if the money is nothing.”

The former two-time governor of Zamfara State assured the president that members of the campaign council would work together to secure his re-election, describing the assignment as a collective responsibility.

“We are going to do it all honestly with the trust and, by God’s grace, we are going to deliver,” Yari said.

Wike, for his part, said securing a national victory for Tinubu would not excuse campaign coordinators who failed to mobilise sufficient votes in their assigned territories. He stressed that appointments and positions in the campaign council must translate into tangible electoral results.

The FCT minister said, “If you don’t deliver your state and the president wins, don’t say we have won. It is not a question of I am chairman of this, I am secretary of this, I am a member of this.”

The minister, who is the coordinator of Tinubu’s campaign in Rivers State and the FCT, said campaign officials must take personal responsibility for delivering their areas rather than rely on the overall outcome of the presidential election.

He illustrated the point with Lagos State, recalling a conversation with the Chief of Staff to the President.

“If you don’t win in Lagos, don’t say we have won,” Wike said.

The minister expressed confidence in his own assignment, saying Rivers and the FCT would deliver massive votes for Tinubu in the January 2027 presidential election.

Wike stated, “Simple, there is not too much work for me. It’s Rivers and FCT, and let me say and pledge, by the grace of God, Rivers and FCT will vote massively for Bola Tinubu. That is my job.

“Rivers and FCT, it is taken. I challenge any area council that can say they don’t see the presence of Mr President.

“For me, as an opposition party member, as the leader of the Peoples Democratic Party, there are not two leaders of the PDP. I’m the leader of the PDP, so I speak on behalf of the Peoples Democratic Party.”

Defending his support for Tinubu, Wike said being an opposition party member should not prevent politicians from acknowledging what they consider positive actions by the ruling party.

He said, “Democracy allows the opposition to be there to look at things that the ruling party has not concentrated on and say these are the issues you are not tackling. Democracy is not that if the ruling party is doing well, because you are in opposition, you say they are not doing well. That is not democracy.”

Anambra State Governor Charles Soludo and his Osun State counterpart, Ademola Adeleke, also expressed optimism about Tinubu’s re-election.

Soludo, a member and national leader of the opposition All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA), disclosed that his party would campaign round the clock for Tinubu’s second term.

He told the president, “Count on us, the All Progressives Grand Alliance, 24/7. We are with you because we believe.”

The former Governor of Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) declared that the president’s return for a second term was already settled in the minds of his supporters.

He said, “We are talking about when you get into the second term. It is the acceleration in the transformation process — from stability and reform to shared prosperity.”

Soludo described Tinubu as a symbol of “the unity of Nigeria, the security of Nigeria and the shared prosperity of Nigeria”, saying those values informed APGA’s decision to back him.

He also defended the government’s economic reforms, acknowledging their difficulty but insisting they were necessary.

“The path you have chosen, that you have had the courage to take, is the difficult but necessary path,” he said.

Adeleke also declared that no one could stop the second term movement of Tinubu.

Adeleke of the opposition Accord Party said the president would emerge victorious during the January poll.

He stated, “I can see the victory in 2027. Nobody can stop this movement. I am going to lead. We will sing and dance all the way back to Aso Rock. Four years isn’t enough, that’s why I am here to throw my weight.

“Let us rise from all nooks and crannies to ensure his victory. Let us pray for Mr President and, by the grace of God, we shall be there.”

Yilwatda: Tinubu’s Reforms Deserve Continuity

APC National Chairman, Professor Nentawe Yilwatda, said the various reforms introduced by the Tinubu administration deserved continuity.

Yilwatda added that under Tinubu, the government had pursued major economic reforms that addressed longstanding structural challenges and established a stronger foundation for sustainable growth.

He spoke yesterday in Abuja during the inauguration of the Presidential Campaign Council of the party ahead of the 2027 general election.

He stressed that the inauguration marked the beginning of a coordinated and credible campaign to secure the re-election of Tinubu.

Yilwatda stated that the presence of party leaders reflected shared commitment and confidence in the party’s collective capacity to present a compelling vision for Nigeria’s future.

He charged the council to organise effectively, communicate the achievements and policies of the administration, and engage Nigerians with confidence.

Yilwatda stated, “Today, we begin an important assignment of bringing together the strength of our national structures, the experience of our leaders and the energy of our members to build a coordinated and credible campaign.

“We have made so much progress but must acknowledge where we have challenges while explaining the objectives, progress and continuing work of the administration.”

The chairman stated that the party must communicate its critical infrastructure investments in roads, power, gas projects, railways, ports, agricultural infrastructure, and digital connectivity, and explain how they translated into practical improvements in daily lives.

“This is the substance of our campaign: a clear record, an honest assessment of the challenges and a credible vision for the future,” he said.

Yilwatda assured party members at all levels that they mattered and that the party’s strength depended on their effectiveness.

He called for direction, coordination and clear responsibilities among governors, legislators and campaign officials.

Senate: Rainbow Coalition on Course for Tinubu’s 2027 Victory

Senate said the rainbow coalition incorporated into the APC Presidential Campaign Council was on course to deliver victory. It said the initiative was an unprecedented political alliance aimed at promoting national unity and inclusive governance.

The declaration came as the upper chamber called on the federal government to prioritise the completion of abandoned and ongoing road projects across the country before embarking on new ones.

It warned that the continued deterioration of critical highways was endangering lives, disrupting economic activities, and imposing additional hardship on Nigerians.

Akpabio and Bamidele made the remarks yesterday during plenary, shortly before the chamber adjourned proceedings to enable senators attending the inauguration of the APC Presidential Campaign Council at the Presidential Villa participate in the event.

Bamidele, who sought the indulgence of his colleagues to make what he described as a historic observation before moving the motion for adjournment, said the composition of the campaign council demonstrated the emergence of a broad political alliance cutting across party lines.

He cited the involvement of Soludo of APGA; Adeleke of Accord Party; Wike of PDP; and Senator Ibrahim Dankwambo of Gombe North as coordinators of different segments of the campaign council.

The senate leader said the arrangement represented an opportunity to deepen democratic engagement and promote a political campaign focused on ideas rather than partisan divisions.

He stated, “My point, Mr. President, is that in this country, in the best interests of the Nigerian people, a rainbow coalition, indeed, is on the move and very much on course.

“I think it is something that should not go unnoticed. We will proceed out of this chamber as members of the ruling party, accompanied by our colleagues, to go to the presidential campaign council. We look forward to a campaign that will really celebrate ideas and celebrate our democracy. I really congratulate you, Mr. President.”

Responding, Akpabio described the coalition as historic, stating that its composition reflects an effort to bring political interests together under a common platform ahead of the 2027 presidential election.

He said the arrangement went beyond infrastructure development, revenue allocation, and economic reforms to embrace national cohesion and unity of purpose.

Akpabio stated, “Let me also note, like you said, that this is historic and this is uncommon. This has never happened in the history of our democracy since 1999, that a sitting president will constitute his presidential campaign council with almost all the parties in Nigeria inclusive.

“So, this is not just an inclusive government in terms of infrastructure; it’s not just an inclusive government in terms of revenue allocation and allotments; it’s not just an inclusive government in terms of giant strides in reform. It’s also an inclusive government in terms of unity, unity of purpose in democracy.”

He said the composition of the campaign council suggested that Tinubu’s second-term agenda would place considerable emphasis on political cooperation.

The senate president said, “The coalition is evidence of the fact that President Tinubu’s second term is going to be a unity government, just like his campaign council is a unity campaign council made of almost all the political parties in the country.”

The political discussions came against the backdrop of mounting concerns over the condition of federal roads, with Senate urging the federal government to concentrate resources on completing existing projects while limiting new construction to essential interventions, including roads needed to reconnect communities cut off by flooding and provide access to underserved areas.

The resolution followed the adoption of a motion sponsored by Senator Tony Nwoye on the deplorable condition of the Ogbaru-Ndoni-Rivers Federal Highway, a strategic transport corridor linking communities in Anambra State to Ndoni in Rivers State.

Senate urged the Federal Roads Maintenance Agency (FERMA), South-East Development Commission, and the Federal Ministry of Works to undertake emergency palliative repairs on failed sections of the highway pending comprehensive rehabilitation and reconstruction.

It also called on the Ministry of Works to commence the immediate rehabilitation and reconstruction of the Ogbaru-Iyiowa-Odekpe-Atani-Ogwuikpele-Ndoni Federal Highway through a special intervention programme or another appropriate funding arrangement.

The lawmakers mandated Senate Committee on Works to inspect the highway, engage relevant stakeholders, and report back within four weeks. The committees on works and appropriations were also directed to ensure adequate budgetary provision for the project.

Sani Tasks Appointees on Tinubu’s 2027

Kaduna State Governor, Uba Sani, tasked political appointees in the state and at the federal level to deepen grassroots engagement and work towards delivering a resounding victory for Tinubu in 2027.

Speaking at a strategic meeting with the appointees at Government House, Kaduna, Sani charged them to mobilise for a successful presidential campaign flag-off scheduled for Kaduna on October 24.

He urged the appointees to “strengthen coordination of political activities, towards the success of the All Progressives Congress(APC) in the coming elections.”

According to the governor, “President Bola Tinubu has demonstrated an unprecedented commitment to Kaduna State through transformative investments in infrastructure, education and economic development.

“Such extraordinary commitment deserves more than expressions of gratitude; it demands collective responsibility to consolidate these gains and sustain the momentum of development.

“We must translate our appreciation into decisive political action. I charge every federal appointee and stakeholder to close ranks, deepen grassroots engagement and work towards delivering a resounding landslide victory for President Tinubu in 2027.”

Sani said Tinubu’s support for the Kaduna Light Rail, Abuja–Kaduna–Kano Highway, Kaduna–Birnin Gwari Road, Kaduna–Kano Rail Project and investments in federal tertiary institutions underscored the president’s commitment to the development of Kaduna State.

He emphasised that sustained collaboration between federal appointees and the state government was critical in translating the investments into lasting economic opportunities, improved security and better living conditions for the people.

Atiku: Inauguration of Tinubu’s Campaign Council in Aso Rock Abuse of Public Office

Atiku, yesterday, condemned the inauguration of Tinubu’s Presidential Campaign Council inside the Presidential Villa, Abuja, and described it as an abuse of public office and a worrying violation of public trust.

He stated that the seat of government belonged to all Nigerians and should not be used to host partisan political activities, particularly when alternative venues were available in Abuja.

Atiku, in a statement by Director of Strategic Communication of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential campaign, Phrank Shaibu, said the size of the APC campaign structure further reflected a president more concerned about political endorsements than accounting for the difficulties Nigerians had endured under his administration.

The statement said, “The Presidential Villa belongs to the Nigerian people. It is not a campaign venue or the private property of any political party. Using it for an APC political event is a gross breach of public trust and a troubling abuse of public office.”

Atiku questioned why the president chose to inaugurate the council at night within the Villa rather than use a conventional event venue. He said the decision raised questions about the administration’s commitment to separating state institutions from party politics.

Atiku stated, “Abuja has no shortage of halls and public spaces large enough to host a campaign gathering. Why, then, did Bola Tinubu choose to inaugurate his campaign council at night, behind the gates of the Presidential Villa?

“Nigerians may draw their own conclusions. But a president confident in his record should be willing to face the public in daylight and ask for another mandate.

“Tinubu cannot expect Nigerians to renew a mandate built on a promise of renewed hope when, for millions, that promise has given way to hardship and disappointment.”

Atiku also described Tinubu’s expanded campaign council as a “crowded confession of fear”.

He accused the president of assembling hundreds of politicians to shield himself from public anger over worsening economic hardship and insecurity.

MDPCO: Tinubu’s Campaign Council a Nebuchadnezzar Coalition Heading for the Rocks

The Makinde/Daura Presidential Campaign Organisation (MDPCO) dismissed the APC-PCC as a “Nebuchadnezzar Coalition” on a collision course with the will of the Nigerian people.

In a statement by Richard Ihediuwa, the campaign’s director of communications and strategies, the organisation described APC’s presidential campaign council as a haven of internationally discredited and politically inconsistent characters and corrupt politicians intoxicated by the arrogance of power, imperial ambition, and the dangerous illusion that political influence could substitute for public trust and democratic legitimacy.

The Makinde/Daura campaign council said, ‘’This Nebuchadnezzar Coalition is headed for the rocks as it cannot whitewash the failures of the Tinubu administration, nor rewrite the painful realities confronting citizens.

“It cannot manufacture public acceptance through a parade of ‘political predators’ and power drunk elites, who are mistaking political dominance for public acceptance.

‘’With the high confidence that President Tinubu reposes in this alliance of failed governors, yes-along legislators, and discredited politicians some of whom are fleeing from corruption investigations; even as his administration presides over an unprecedented economic crisis, worsening insecurity and a devastating collapse of public confidence, we see in the APC Presidential Campaign Council imminent political humiliation.”

The campaign council added, ‘’History is replete with the humiliation of those who mistake transitory power for permanence while reinforcing their illusions by surrounding themselves with compensated loyalists and sycophantic, who do not command the loyalty or followership of the people, rather than confront stark reality of failures.’’

World.title: AFC Appoints CBN Governor, Yemi Cardoso Board Chairman
World.content:
Nume Ekeghe in Bangkok, Thailand





The Africa Finance Corporation (AFC), the continent’s leading infrastructure solutions provider, yesterday announced the appointment of the Governor of the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), Mr. Olayemi Cardoso as Chairman of its Board of Directors. He succeeds the immediate-past Chair, Ireti Samuel-Ogbu, who served the Corporation meritoriously during her tenure and continues to serve as a board member.

The Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele and Cardoso, yesterday wooed investors with commitments to sustain economic reforms, improve the investment climate and attract long-term capital as the federal government seeks to mobilise $78.5 billion for 65 projects across key sectors of the economy.

Also yesterday, the Dangote Group endorsed the federal government’s reforms, with its Group Chief Economist, Hassan Mammud, saying fiscal and monetary policy changes had helped stabilise investments in the Dangote Refinery and other subsidiaries. He urged international investors to invest in Nigeria, describing the country as an emerging model for other African economies.

At an investors’ forum in Bangkok, Thailand, held on the sidelines of the ongoing International Monetary Fund and World Bank Group Annual Meetings, the federal government’s officials outlined the government’s priorities, including reducing inflation to single digits, addressing power sector constraints, improving regulatory efficiency and providing clearer fiscal data to support investment decisions.

A new feature introduced this year was a deal room that designed to connect investors with key policymakers, guide them through available investment opportunities and answer questions about investing in Nigeria.

The initiative is intended to give investors direct access to relevant government officials and help convert interest in the country’s investment pipeline into actual commitments.

The pipeline comprises 65 projects requiring a total of $78.5 billion, with energy and transport accounting for almost four-fifths of the funding requirement.

According to the project breakdown presented at the forum, oil, gas and power account for 25 projects requiring $36.4 billion, while transport and maritime account for eight projects valued at $25 billion.

Agriculture and agro-processing account for six projects requiring $9.8 billion, while industry, manufacturing and mining comprise 17 projects requiring $6.6 billion.

Technology, health and urban services account for the remaining nine projects, with a combined capital requirement of $700 million.

The government presented investment opportunities across different funding categories, from projects requiring less than $100 million to those needing $1 billion or more.

The pipeline ranges from $1 million to $15 billion per project, with a median capital requirement of $153 million. Of the 65 projects, 48 require less than $500 million, while 17, valued at a combined $72.3 billion, require at least $1 billion each.

The government is also seeking to strengthen investor participation by highlighting the protections available to foreign investors.

These include permission for 100 per cent foreign ownership in most sectors, full repatriation of capital and profits with a Certificate of Capital Importation, double taxation and bilateral investment treaties, and Nigeria’s membership of the International Centre for Settlement of Investment Disputes (ICSID).

The investment framework also includes a five per cent annual tax credit on qualifying capital expenditure for five years under the Economic Development Tax Incentive.

Oyedele called on investors to consider longer-term commitments, particularly as interest rates begin to decline and the relative attractiveness of fixed-income investments changes.

He asked investors what the government needed to do to encourage them to commit capital for longer periods and shift from foreign portfolio investment to foreign direct investment.

“We know that, for example, as interest rates start to come down, fixed income may be less attractive, but actually, if you consider the risk and the reward, it remains attractive. But what is even better is that the Internal Rate of Return (IRR) for equity investment and FDI gets more attractive, and this is where we want to go to attract more patient capital,” he said.

Speaking at the forum, Oyedele said the government was strengthening collaboration between fiscal and monetary authorities. He added that reducing inflation would help lower borrowing costs and ease pressure on public finances.

“If I want to even just sound selfish from the fiscal side, whatever we do to bring inflation to a single digit, thereby creating the conditions for interest rate to also be single digits will save the fiscal side as of 2026 numbers more than $10 billion. So, this is this is a top priority for us,” he said.

He added that the stability and gradual appreciation of the naira were helping to moderate inflationary pressures.

“The good thing is because of the way the central bank has been able to help us manage the FX environment generally, we have seen the naira not only being stable but steadily appreciative, and the impact on that on inflation is downward, right? So, which is good.”

Oyedele said the government would focus on five major areas of reform: agriculture, power, inflation management, regulatory efficiency and data transparency.

On power, he said, “You cannot power a $1 trillion economy in darkness. It’s impossible.”

He explained that the government was examining market-reflective pricing, transmission challenges and efficiency in the electricity sector, which remain important considerations for investors seeking to establish or expand businesses in Nigeria.

On regulatory reform, Oyedele said excessive regulation, unclear rules and administrative burdens imposed significant costs on businesses.

“We estimate that overregulation, regulatory burden, lack of clarity, and all of those excessive burden that we post on businesses actually are costing us more than the combined revenue from corporate tax, personal income tax and VAT combined,” he said.

He added that the government was developing a framework for economic policy to prevent the arbitrary introduction of new rules, fees and licences.

On data transparency, Oyedele acknowledged concerns about the availability and consistency of Nigeria’s fiscal statistics, particularly the tax-to-GDP ratio. He said the Ministry of Finance was finalising arrangements to make relevant information available and accessible on its website.

“So, we are currently finalising all of that, and it will be available on the website of the Ministry of Finance, finance.gov.ng. It will be updated timely. It will be accessible. It will be credible,” he said.

Cardoso, in his remarks, said the government’s reforms were beginning to provide greater stability for investment and economic growth. He emphasised that lower inflation remained critical to improving the welfare of ordinary Nigerians.

“The reason why we felt it was important to give ourselves this as a target is to recognise the fact that inflation is probably the biggest stance on the poor, and so it is critical that we bring it down to levels that are more manageable, rather than the situation where you feel okay, you’re lower double digits, and it’s okay. It isn’t okay,” he said.

Cardoso said inflation had declined from about 34–35 per cent to approximately 15 per cent, describing the reduction as significant but insisting that the central bank would not become complacent.

“Our medium-term target is to bring it down to single digits. Of course, as we embrace inflation targeting, that will obviously be a lot more open and transparent, and people will be able to have a clearer sense of the road of travel,” he said.

He also pointed to Nigeria’s external reserves, which he said had reached their highest level in 18 years, describing them as a buffer against external shocks.

According to Cardoso, the reforms had helped Nigeria withstand global pressures, including the effects of war and discussions around tariffs, while the exchange rate had remained stable and appreciated.

Responding to concerns that ordinary Nigerians were yet to feel the benefits of the reforms, Cardoso said the stability provided by the policies had helped prevent a worse outcome.

AFC Appoints Cardoso Board Chairman

The Africa Finance Corporation (AFC), the continent’s leading infrastructure solutions provider, yesterday announced the appointment of Mr. Olayemi Cardoso as Chairman of its Board of Directors.

A statement which announced this yesterday, stated that Cardoso brings extensive experience spanning international banking, investment management, economic policy and public sector leadership.

“Since assuming office as Governor of the CBN in September 2023, he has led a far-reaching programme of monetary, financial-sector, and institutional reforms to restore macroeconomic stability, strengthen policy credibility, and rebuild investor confidence in Nigeria’s economy.

“Under his leadership, the CBN has implemented significant reforms to Nigeria’s foreign exchange market, addressed longstanding foreign exchange obligations, strengthened monetary policy transmission, and enhanced institutional governance and transparency.

“The Bank has also concluded a recapitalisation programme for the banking sector, aimed at strengthening the resilience and capacity of Nigeria’s financial system to support sustainable economic growth.

“Prior to his appointment as Governor, Mr. Cardoso built a distinguished career in international banking and public service, including a 12-year tenure as Chairman of Citibank Nigeria and service as Commissioner for Economic Planning and Budget in Lagos State.

“In the latter role, he contributed to economic planning and fiscal management in one of Africa’s largest economies. He holds a degree from Aston University in the United Kingdom and a master’s in public administration from Harvard Kennedy School, where he also served on the Alumni Board,” it added.

It further stated that Cardoso’s appointment came as the AFC continued to expand its role in financing and developing strategic infrastructure assets that address Africa’s infrastructure gap, accelerate industrialisation and strengthen regional integration.

“His experience in financial sector reform, institutional governance and capital markets will provide valuable perspective on the Corporation’s strategic direction as it mobilises investment to unlock Africa’s economic potential,” it added.

President & CEO of AFC, Samaila Zubairu, was quoted to have said: “We are delighted to welcome Mr Cardoso as our Board Chairman. He shares our conviction that Africa’s lasting stability depends on its productive capacity. His leadership will strengthen AFC as we advance The Africa We Build 2050, mobilising African capital to build the infrastructure and industries that create jobs, prosperity and dignity for our people. We also sincerely thank Mrs Samuel-Ogbu for her dedication and contribution to AFC’s board during her tenure.”

Commenting on the appointment, Cardoso said: “A more productive Africa is a more stable Africa. AFC has the credibility and track record to mobilise capital and build the infrastructure and industries that drive transformation. I look forward to working with the Board, management and member states to advance The Africa We Build 2050. Our measure of success must be the productive capacity we create, the industries we enable and the jobs we support.”

Dangote Group Applauds FG’s Reforms, Says Policy Stability Boosted Confidence in Refinery Investment

The Dangote Group also endorsed the government’s reforms, with its Group Chief Economist, Hassan Mammud, saying fiscal and monetary policy changes helped the Group stabilise its operations and improve investment projections.

Mammud, who represented the President of the Dangote Group, Alhaji Aliko Dangote, at the forum, said the transparency and credibility of monetary policy supported the group’s investment in its refinery investment.

He said policy consistency and incentives available to businesses operating in an export-free zone were important factors in building investor confidence.

“The transparency and the credibility we have seen in that has significantly enabled the Dangote Group to have good projections and was able to come out of the woods from his investment of about $20 billion in the refinery,” he said.

Mammud urged international investors to consider Nigeria, describing the country’s reform experience as a model for other African economies.

“Please come into Nigeria, bring your investment. Nigeria is actually a symbol to other African countries now,” he said.

Cardoso welcomed the group’s comments, noting that the reforms had helped address the challenges businesses faced when exporting at one exchange rate and importing at another.

“The ability of Dangote to take bull by the horns and at least break that cycle and enter the value-added chain is one to be commended,” he said.

The endorsement came as the government sought to use the investors’ forum and its new deal room to present specific projects, clarify investment conditions and encourage investors to commit capital to Nigeria.

World.title: Nigeria’s Sacrifices for Peace in Sierra Leone Will Never Be Forgotten, Says Ex-VP
World.content:
• Calls for Africa’s economic independence

Linus Aleke in Abuja





A former Vice-President of Sierra Leone, Mr Samuel Sam-Sumana, has expressed profound gratitude to Nigeria for its sacrifices in restoring peace to his country, saying the contributions of Nigerian troops would remain indelible in Sierra Leone’s history.

The former Vice-President also called for Africa’s economic independence to discourage young people from migrating to Europe and America in search of better opportunities and living conditions, often at the risk of their lives, owing to a lack of opportunities at home.

Sam-Sumana made these remarks when the leadership of the Defence Correspondents Association of Nigeria (DECAN) paid him a courtesy visit in Abuja.

He said Nigeria had played a pivotal role in supporting Sierra Leone during its conflict by providing troops and other forms of assistance that helped restore peace and stability.

He acknowledged that military personnel and civilians had paid the ultimate price in the struggle, stressing the need to ensure that their sacrifices were never forgotten.

“As a Sierra Leonean, I wish to express my profound gratitude for the role Nigeria and other countries played in helping Sierra Leone regain peace and stability,” he said.

The former Vice-President described Nigeria as a big brother in West Africa, stressing that the country’s stability and prosperity had far-reaching implications for the subregion.

“When Nigeria catches a cold, the rest of us sneeze,” he said, underscoring the interconnectedness of West African countries.

Sam-Sumana also urged DECAN to sustain its engagement with the military and strengthen professional cooperation between defence correspondents and security institutions.

He described journalists as indispensable partners in governance, accountability and national development, warning against the tendency of political leaders to regard critical reporting as an act of hostility.

“Constructive criticism is essential to improving public institutions and ensuring that those entrusted with public responsibilities remain accountable,” he said.

In his remarks, DECAN President, Mr Odita Sunday, said the courtesy visit was intended to express the association’s appreciation to Sam-Sumana for accepting its invitation and participating in the DECAN Conference and Awards 2026.

World.title: Atiku Urges Nigerians to Collect PVCs, Promises Economic Relief If Elected in 2027
World.content:
• ADC condemns Akpabio’s seven virgin’s remark

Chuks Okocha in Abuja





Presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar, has pledged to make life more affordable and improve security across Nigeria, blaming President Bola Tinubu’s administration for the rising cost of living.

Atiku made the promise in a post on his official X account yesterday, while urging registered voters to collect their Permanent Voter Cards ahead of the 2027 elections.

The former vice-president said Nigerians of different ages and economic backgrounds were grappling with financial hardship and insecurity.

“Parents go to bed worried about what they will feed their children tomorrow. Pensioners must choose between buying medicine and buying food. Young people work hard, yet transport, rent and basic needs consume what they earn,” Atiku said

“And across the country, families live with the fear of kidnapping, attacks and whether their loved ones will return home safely,” he added.

Atiku warned that Nigerians should not have to contend with hunger and insecurity at the same time, urging the country to prevent the current challenges from becoming the inheritance of future generations.

He called on eligible voters to collect and keep their PVCs, describing the cards as a means of exercising their democratic rights and seeking change through the ballot.

“If you are a registered voter, please go and collect your PVC. Hold on to it. It is your voice, your choice and your peaceful power to demand change,” he said.

Atiku also accused Tinubu’s administration of making life more expensive and pledged to reverse the trend if given the opportunity to govern.

“Bola made life expensive. I will work to make life affordable again and restore the security every Nigerian deserves,” he said.

“Let us stand together, across generations, and vote for a Nigeria where every family can live with dignity, safety and hope,” he added.

ADC Condemns Akpabio’s Seven Virgin’s Remark

Meanwhile, the ADC, has condemned Senate President Godswill Akpabio’s reported remarks on attempted suicide, describing his reference to “seven virgins” as a cynical and offensive comment that potentially promoted religious stereotyping.

In a statement issued by its National Publicity Secretary, Mallam Bolaji Abdullahi, the party also described the Senate President’s defence of imprisonment for suicide survivors as a disgraceful endorsement of what it called “an outdated colonial relic” that preferred to punish citizens who ordinarily required help.

The ADC commented on the National Suicide Prevention Bill which the Senate President had supported via imprisonment as punishment for failed suicide attempts.

In a video that went into circulation afterwards, Senator Akpabio could be heard saying, as he laughed, “why death may be attractive to some young people is that they have seven virgins waiting for them.”

The opposition party said it took strong exception to the Senate President’s remarks.

According to Abdullahi, “We find the ‘seven virgins’ remark particularly disturbing because it introduces religious stereotyping into a discussion that should be about protecting human life. Such a lurid comment is not only careless and insensitive. It also trivialises an issue that is, literally speaking, a matter of life and death.”

The party however declared its support for the position that suicide is a mental health issue rather than a criminal act.

“The criminalisation of attempted suicide is a colonial legacy. These laws belong to an era when people experiencing profound distress were treated as offenders who, by trying to take their own lives, wanted to deprive ‘the Crown’ of the services they could render and the taxes they could pay, rather than as human beings in need of care.

“It is shameful that, when presented with an opportunity to reform this punitive inheritance, the head of the Senate chose to champion its preservation. Nigeria cannot continue to punish people for surviving a crisis that nearly claimed their lives, especially when those who handed us those laws have long abolished them,” the party said.

World.title: NAF Moves to Prevent Air Crashes as CAS Orders Stronger Flight Safety Oversight
World.content:
• Ondo orders fumigation, water supply as residents fear disease outbreak

Linus Aleke in Abuja and Fidelis David in Akure





The Chief of the Air Staff (CAS), Air Marshal Sunday Kelvin Aneke, has directed strengthened flight safety oversight across the Nigerian Air Force (NAF) as part of efforts to prevent air crashes involving NAF aircraft.

Air Marshal Aneke also reaffirmed the Service’s commitment to personnel safety, professional standards and institutional accountability following the tragic accident involving NAF ATR 42-500 aircraft NAF 931 on 5 October 2026.

In a statement, the Director of Public Relations and Information of the Nigerian Air Force, Air Commodore Ehimen Ejodame, said the directive was issued during a meeting with branch chiefs, Air Officers Commanding (AOCs), principal staff officers and other senior commanders on Wednesday.

During the meeting, the CAS emphasised the need for sustained vigilance, strict adherence to established procedures and continuous improvement in safety management.

Expressing profound sorrow over the loss of personnel, Air Marshal Aneke acknowledged the grief of the bereaved families and the wider NAF community.

He stressed that operational effectiveness must be underpinned by sound judgement, professional discipline and the highest standards of flight safety.

Accordingly, he directed commanders to maintain rigorous oversight of aircraft airworthiness, maintenance quality assurance, operational procedures and aircrew competence.

He also emphasised proactive safety monitoring, prompt reporting of potential hazards and the effective implementation of safety measures, noting that flight safety remained a shared command responsibility.

Meanwhile, search and recovery operations at the accident site in Igbokoda, Ondo State, continued with the involvement of specialist personnel and equipment from relevant agencies.

The Head of the Recovery and Investigation Team, Air Vice Marshal EOE Ebiowe, disclosed that the operation had involved extensive mud excavation and water pumping to facilitate access to relevant areas.

Ondo Orders Fumigation, Water Supply as Residents Fear Disease Outbreak

In a related development, the Ondo State Government has ordered the fumigation of the river around the crash site following complaints by residents over foul stench and fears of possible environmental contamination.

The government also directed the provision of potable water to residents if the river was found to be severely polluted and unsuitable for use, while nose masks and other essential health kits were to be distributed to protect the community against potential health hazards.

The directives followed growing concerns among residents over the condition of the swamp where the aircraft crashed on October 5, killing all 25 persons on board, comprising 20 passengers and five crew members.

More than a week after the incident, residents said the stench from the crash site had spread to residential areas, with reports of human remains floating in the water.

In a statement by the Commissioner for Information and Orientation, Idowu Ajanaku, Governor Lucky Orimisan Aiyedatiwa had directed the Ministries of Environment and Health to commence extensive fumigation of the affected river to prevent a possible outbreak of diseases.

According to the statement, the governor also directed the Ilaje Local Government to arrange water tankers for the continuous distribution of potable water if the river was confirmed to be severely polluted and unsuitable for use.

The arrangement, it said, would remain in place pending a lasting intervention to address the pollution concerns.

The governor further directed the Ministries of Health and Environment to provide nose masks and other essential health kits to residents.

World.title: Dino Melaye Accuses National Assembly of Surrendering Powers to President Tinubu
World.content:
• Says Rivers emergency rule, electoral law controversies, budget lapses expose weakening legislative oversight

Sunday Aborisade in Abuja





Senator Dino Melaye has accused the 10th National Assembly of weakening its constitutional independence and failing to hold President Bola Tinubu’s administration accountable, warning that the legislature risks becoming an extension of the presidency.

Melaye, who made the allegations at a press conference in Abuja, yesterday, said the handling of constitution amendments, electoral reforms, budget implementation, security matters, and other critical national issues raised questions about the commitment of Senate President Godswill Akpabio and House of Representatives Speaker Tajudeen Abbas to legislative oversight.

He described the 10th National Assembly as having become a “department of the Villa”, stating that the legislature is increasingly failing to exercise the institutional independence required to restrain executive power.

In a paper, titled, “The 10th Assembly: The Pathway to Tinubu’s ‘Lifetime Presidency’,” Melaye stated that a president did not need to abolish constitutional term limits to accumulate excessive power if the institutions designed to check executive authority failed to perform their duties.

He said, “A lifetime presidency does not begin with the abolition of term limits. It begins when the institutions created to restrain a president stop restraining him.

“Nigeria’s constitution does not establish an elected monarchy. It establishes a presidential democracy deliberately divided among institutions so that no individual, however popular or politically powerful, exercises the authority of the Nigerian state without constitutional restraint.”

According to him, the president possesses extensive executive powers, but the legislature retains independent authority over legislation, appropriation, and oversight, while the judiciary interprets the law.

He stated, “Cooperation is different from submission. The president may request. Parliament must scrutinise. The president may propose. Parliament may accept, amend or reject. The president may exercise power. Parliament must ensure that power remains within the constitution.”

Melaye acknowledged that the National Assembly had passed legislation, conducted investigations, and held public hearings. However, he questioned whether it had demonstrated sufficient independence when confronted with issues affecting the exercise of presidential power.

He cited the March 2025 declaration of a state of emergency in Rivers State, controversies surrounding the passage and gazetting of the 2025 tax laws, disagreements over the Electoral Act 2026, delayed budget implementation, rising Service-Wide Votes, and the handling of constitutional amendments.

He also questioned the legislature’s response to the deaths of 37 people in the custody of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps in Niger State in September and the constitutional implications of Tinubu’s three-week vacation abroad.

World.title: N’Delta Group Cautions against Attacks on PINL
World.content:
Olusegun Samuel in Yenagoa





The Niger Delta Ambassadors for Good Governance (NDAGG) has warned against what it described as unwarranted attacks on Pipeline Infrastructure Nigeria Limited (PINL), saying such actions could undermine the interests of Ijaw communities benefiting from the company’s operations.

The group commended PINL for its role in protecting critical national infrastructure and assets, particularly oil and gas pipelines, while contributing to employment generation, economic activities and community development across the Niger Delta.

NDAGG also said the House of Representatives Committee on Host Communities had cleared PINL and its principal, Osahon Okunbo, of allegations of ineffectiveness and financial recklessness in the management of the pipeline security contract.

In a statement signed by its President, Zipamoh Moses, on behalf of the executive council and members, the organisation urged the public to disregard the allegations, insisting that the company’s contributions to pipeline security and host communities should not be overlooked.

The group maintained that PINL’s operations had brought considerable benefits to Ijaw communities through employment opportunities, economic empowerment and other forms of support.

It noted that the impact of the company’s activities extended beyond individual beneficiaries to community institutions and socio-cultural organisations, including the Ijaw National Congress (INC) and the Ijaw Youth Council (IYC).

According to NDAGG, the widespread benefits associated with PINL’s presence in the region made it necessary for stakeholders to carefully consider the implications of allegations capable of damaging the company’s reputation and its relationship with host communities.

The organisation argued that attempts to discredit the company without due consideration of its contributions could ultimately affect the interests of the communities that had benefited from its operations.

NDAGG stressed that pipeline surveillance and the protection of oil and gas infrastructure were critical to Nigeria’s economic stability, given the Niger Delta’s strategic importance to the country’s petroleum industry.

It said effective pipeline security was essential to curbing vandalism, preventing disruptions to oil and gas operations and sustaining economic activities in host communities.

The group therefore urged community leaders, stakeholders and members of the public to exercise restraint and responsibility when making allegations concerning pipeline surveillance operations, noting that such issues should be addressed based on verifiable facts and the performance of the companies involved.

It further maintained that companies operating in the Niger Delta should be assessed on their contributions to infrastructure security, community welfare and peaceful engagement with their host communities, rather than being subjected to what it described as unwarranted attacks.

NDAGG reaffirmed its support for initiatives that promote the protection of national assets, peaceful coexistence and sustainable development in the Niger Delta.

It called for stronger collaboration among pipeline surveillance companies, host communities and relevant government institutions to address security challenges in the oil and gas sector while ensuring that the benefits of such operations continue to reach the people of the region.

World.title: 64 Years After Father, Isiaka Abdulrazaq Inherits Tafidan Zazzau Title
World.content:
Kuni Tyessi in Abuja





Sixty-four years after his father was turbaned as Tafidan Zazzau, former Chief Financial Officer of the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited, NNPC Ltd, Isiaka Abdulrazaq, has been confirmed as the new Tafidan Yamman Zazzau.

The Emir of Zazzau, His Highness, Ahmed Nuhu Bamalli, approved the appointment in a letter dated October 7, 2026 signed by the Magatakardan Zazzau, Malam Yusuf Abubakar Hayat.

The Emirate Council said the title recognizes Abdulrazaq’s contributions to peace-building, philanthropy and community development, and his service to the Zazzau Emirate, Kaduna State and Nigeria at large.

The appointment marks the continuation of a family legacy in the Emirate, as Abdulrazaq is the son of the late Alhaji A.G.F. Abdulrazaq, SAN, a foremost lawyer who held the title of Tafidan Zazzau from 1962 until his death.

The Abdulrazaq family has lived in Zaria since the mid-1950s and has maintained enduring relationships with the Zazzau Emirate.

A Barewa College alumnus, Isiaka Abdulrazaq is a lawyer and finance professional who rose to Executive Director, Finance and Accounts at NEPA/PHCN and retired as Chief Financial Officer of the NNPC in 2019.

Born in Zaria, Abdulrazaq attended Barewa College, Zaria, one of Northern Nigeria’s oldest and most reputable educational institutions. His personal and family connections to Zaria reflect a longstanding relationship with the Zazzau Emirate and its people.

Beyond his professional accomplishments, Abdulrazaq is widely recognised for his community engagement and philanthropic activities over the years, demonstrating a sustained commitment to the welfare and development of the people.

The Emir and the Zazzau Emirate Council congratulated him, expressing confidence that he would uphold the dignity of the title and discharge its responsibilities with integrity, and prayed that Almighty Allah would guide him and grant him wisdom and strength to fulfil the expectations of the office.

World.title: HERE are your revised SASSA payment dates for November 2026
World.content:
After two weeks of indecision, revised SASSA payment dates for November 2026 have finally been announced. The agency confirmed earlier this week, on Wednesday 14 October, of next month’s payment schedule.

As beneficiaries already know, local government elections fall on Wednesday 4 November, which is the date originally set for the Disability Grant. As such, the agency said a new schedule had to follow consultations with all stakeholders, including the National Treasury.

The South African Social Security Agency said the aim of the date change was to keep payments “administered efficiently, securely and with minimal disruption during the election period.” Accordingly, here are your revised SASSA payment dates for November 2026, with one actually falling in October:



Older Person’s Grant: Friday 30 October (was 3 November)

(was 3 November) Disability Grant: Monday 2 November (was 4 November)

(was 4 November) Children’s Grants: Tuesday 3 November (was 5 November)

(was 5 November) ‘Fourth’ under review payment date: Thursday 5 November (was 6 November)

In practice, state pensioners are paid four days earlier than planned. Disability and Children’s grants are now two days earlier, and review cases one day earlier.

HOW LONG BETWEEN PAYDAYS?

Counting from October 2026 disbursements, which carried no top-up, it’s exactly four weeks gap for the three ‘core’ SASSA Grants. Under the original schedule, pensioners would have waited 32 days. Now, Older Person’s is 28 days, as are Disability and Children’s Grants. So, all in all, the reshuffling has worked serendipitously, you could argue.

However, only the timing has moved. With no October top-up, the amounts stay at R2 400 for pensioners aged 60 to 74, Care Dependency and Disability. And R2 420 for those 75 and older. Same deal with the three Childcare Grants.

Moreover, SASSA urges beneficiaries not to visit its offices just to ask about dates, and to be wary of any false information about payments. Anyone whose grant is under review should respond to SASSA’s communications and attend any appointments they’re given in time for the fourth payment date.

But what do you think? Are you happy with the revised SASSA payment dates for November 2026? Please share your thoughts in the comments section below …

World.title: Update: Safa’s R20 Million VAR plan faces major hurdles
World.content:
Safa have revealed they are facing enormous technical and operational challenges before bringing VAR to life.

Sharing the latest developments, Sports Minister Gayton McKenzie and SAFA president Danny Jordaan engaged the media at Freedom Park in Pretoria on Wednesday.

It was highlighted that four local football competitions will benefit. The Betway Premiership, Hollywoodbets Super League, ABC Motsepe League and SAFA Women’s Provincial League national play-offs.



“VAR is not an easy thing, but I will say this to you, VAR is going to happen. VAR is busy happening,” McKenzie said, confirming that discussions with FIFA would begin on Thursday, 15 October.

The FA’s CEO Lydia Monyepao explained that the association initiated the project in 2024. It is focused on referee development, football modernisation and compliance with international requirements.

The project has been accelerated by a R20 million funding from the Department of Sport, Arts and Culture. Additional funding from SAFA, COSAFA, CAF and FIFA is set to follow.

Safa say the funding does not mean VAR can be introduced immediately. Stakeholder alignment, technical assessments and procurement requirements are still outstanding.

Jordaan also highlighted the technology’s potential to improve officiating and player protection by giving referees a more comprehensive view of matches.

TRAINING AND TRIALS FIRST

SAFA confirmed that eight South African referees have received VAR training through COSAFA, with three fully approved as referees, VARs and AVARs. Namely Tom Abongile, Luxolo Badi and Akhona Makhalima.



The association expects the broader training and certification process to take approximately six months, involving theoretical lessons, simulator sessions and practical field training.

SAFA is also scheduled to engage FIFA from 15 October to seek approval to begin training additional officials.

Meanwhile, discussions with the Premier Soccer League and broadcasters, including SuperSport/Canal+ and the SABC, remain necessary to establish technical compatibility and operational readiness.

Rather than immediate full implementation, SAFA’s next major milestone is a controlled trial phase, potentially involving selected SAFA competitions, ABC Motsepe League play-offs, suitable cup competitions or approved international friendlies.

The broader rollout will depend on FIFA approval, successful training, technical readiness and procurement compliance.

SAFA maintains that the additional scrutiny is necessary to protect public funds and establish a sustainable system. For South African football supporters, VAR is progressing, but its arrival in domestic competitions still depends on several crucial steps.

World.title: Angelique Gerber to DIVORCE ex-Bok Jacques Potgieter
World.content:
Angelique Gerber will reportedly proceed with her divorce to former Springbok, Jacques Potgieter, four years after their marriage separation.

This comes as the ex 7de Laan actress reportedly had a brief reconciliation with her ex, who is the father of her three children.

During the time apart, Jacques had a relationship with another woman, whom he recently split from.



ANGELIQUE GERBER TO DIVORCE EX JACQUES POTGIETER

According to reports, Angelique Gerber is proceeding with her divorce from Jacques Potgieter after allegedly giving him a second chance.

Sadly, their recent reconciliation was short-lived, with Angelique’s lawyer confirming that the second split was in the best interests of their three children.

The actress and influencer reportedly had enough of Jacques’s lifestyle and is now ready to close the chapter.

The news that Jacques and Angelique are still legally married, despite their messy relationship split, came as a surprise to many followers.

On her social media platforms, Jacques had liked comments urging the couple to rekindle their romance. When one follower commented, “You know you two can marry again”, Jacques responded, “We were never divorced”.

TIMELINE OF MESSY MARRIAGE SPLIT

Take a look at this relationship timeline between Angelique Gerber and Jacques Potgieter…



2014: Angelique and Jacques begin dating. At the time, the red-haired actress appeared as the character “Clara” on SABC 2 soapie, 7de Laan, which her rugby player boyfriend played for both the Waratahs and the Munakata Sanix Blues

2016: Angelique and Jacqued married at a Durbanville estate.

2016-2018: The couple would welcome their three children.

2021: Jacques Potgieter denies posting several Instagram Stories confessing to cheating on his wife, Angelique. He claims his account was “hacked”. On her IG, Angelique posted the cryptic message “The truth always comes out”. The couple again deny posting the messages. They claim they are happier and more in love than ever.

2022: The couple appeared in public separately and deleted all images of themselves together. Jacques goes public with a woman named Lizane “Lalla” Wagner.

2023: Angelique Gerber puts Jacques Potgieter on blast over a dispute over financial support for their children. She also expressed her annoyance at his posts praising his girlfriend as a stepmother.

June 2026: Jacques and Lizane Wagner split after their four-year relationship. Lizane denied allegations that she had been responsible for the breakdown of Jacques’s marriage.

July – September 2026: Jacques and Angelique appear to rekindle their romance. Jacques likes comments from the public encouraging the couple to give their marriage a “second chance”

October 2026: Jacques deletes all of his new images with Angelique, who also allegedly accuses him of “betraying” his family in various cryptic IG reposts.

World.title: ‘The R2 400 is just an insult’: Pensioner speaks out on SASSA grant
World.content:
A pensioner in Limpopo who receives the Older Person’s Grant says his monthly SASSA payment does not cover his household’s basic needs.

The grant recipient, who asked not to be named in this article, has received the grant for three years. He lives in a shared family home where three to five people depend on his income, and he uses his grant for a mix of essential expenses.

Despite this, he regularly struggles to make ends meet. He runs out of money before the month ends.



SASSA grant falls short for pensioner

The pensioner said the cost of living and rising food prices are his biggest financial concern. When asked what he would change about SASSA, he chose an increase in the grant amount.

“SASSA must stop harassing and stopping us when we try to find other income streams because the R2 400 is just an insult, period,” he said.

The Older Person’s Grant increased by R80 to R2 400 per month in April 2026, following Finance Minister Enoch Godongwana’s Budget Speech.

The grant recipient has experience in administrative and office work. He is currently unemployed and not looking for work.

Payment problems and poor communication

The pensioner said he has experienced a late or missing grant payment. He rated SASSA’s communication with recipients as very poor.

He receives his grant through a bank deposit. He has never applied for additional government support because he did not know what else was available.
