World.title: UNDP chief sounds alarm on growing poverty after Iran war shock
World.content:
Bangkok – Millions could be thrown into poverty by surging energy costs, the impact of an intense El Nino phenomenon and higher interest rates, with vulnerable countries being pushed to the brink by repeated crises, the UN’s development chief told AFP.

Global fuel prices have soared since the United States launched its war on Iran in late February, with Tehran’s retaliations against Washington’s Gulf allies curtailing major oil and natural gas supplies.

Fiscal deficits and debt-to-GDP ratios around the world have ballooned since the 2008 global financial crisis, with governments firefighting against a series of shocks including the pandemic and wars in Ukraine and the Middle East.

Speaking on the sidelines of the IMF-World Bank Annual Meetings in Bangkok, UN Development Programme (UNDP) head Alexander de Croo said many developing countries had responded to the current spike in energy prices with blanket subsidies, but a succession of crises had left them with limited resources to keep that up.

“You have to repair your roof while at the same time your home is on fire,” he told AFP, adding governments in the developing world did not have time to rebuild buffers or resolve previous shocks before being hit by new crises.

The IMF warned this week that while global growth had held up in the face of the energy crisis, that resilience was highly dependent on the boom in AI technology investments, and poorer countries not exposed to that were still struggling.

IMF chief Kristalina Georgieva had warned that “winter is coming” — an allusion to popular fantasy book series “Game of Thrones” — implying that a cataclysm was around the corner if the world did not prepare for it.

And De Croo added: “Some countries have a well-insulated house with money in the bank. Other countries have a house without a roof and no money in the bank.

“We’re stumbling from one crisis into the other, and what countries need is some space, and some time, and access to financing.”

Not getting the response right could be devastating. The UNDP warned in a new report that about 130 million people were at risk of being pushed into poverty this year if energy and food price increases were fully passed on without subsidies.

People in South and East Asia and sub-Saharan Africa are at particular risk, the agency said.

– ‘Difficult to manage’ –

With advanced economies seeing bond yields surge — owing to elevated inflation expectations, surging debt ratios and AI capital-raising activities — global borrowing costs have been rising.

That in turn, de Croo warned, had tightened space for developing countries to access the capital they needed to combat the shocks, with rising interest rates feeding into increasing debt payments.

According to UNDP, the median developing country now spends about 9.5 percent of government revenue on interest payments — the highest in a quarter of a century, and more than three times that in high-income countries.

“It starts to be a difficult situation to manage, and it takes away all their margin for policy,” de Croo said.

The former Belgian prime minister said he would spend the week in Bangkok — where world economic policy leaders have gathered since Monday — pushing for advanced economies and multilateral agencies to invest in economic growth, resilience and job creation in the developing world.

He also said recent stark cuts in international aid were having an impact on those countries.

The UNDP warned there was potentially more pain to come, with this year’s El Nino climate phenomenon forecast to be the strongest on record.

That is expected to have widespread effects including flooding, droughts and other extreme events that are estimated to peak in early 2027.

De Croo also said private capital needed to step in to help fight some of the worst consequences of climate change.

“We see that the impact of climate has an economic cost. Avoiding that cost has a business case,” he said.

World.title: Tech stock lead rout after US inflation fuels rate hike bets
World.content:
Hong Kong – Asian stocks plunged Thursday as tech firms suffered another painful rout after forecast-topping US inflation data fuelled expectations the Federal Reserve will have to ramp interest rates higher.

Seoul and Tokyo again bore the brunt of the selling as traders bailed out of once-imperious chipmakers, though the selling was heavy across the region, tracking sharp losses on Wall Street.

Markets, already struggling with concerns about the outlook for the AI investment boom, were stung after data showed the US consumer price index hit 3.7 percent in September, sharply up from the previous month and more than the 3.6 percent forecast.

The reading is the highest in five months and was largely driven by the surge in energy costs caused by the more than seven-month Iran war, which saw Tehran effectively choke off the Strait of Hormuz, through which a fifth of global crude passed.

Gasoline costs accounted for more than half of the monthly CPI jump, surging 9.1 percent in September.

The figures will put pressure on the Fed to hike rates at least once more, following September’s lift, with the bank’s decision due on October 28, a week before the US midterm elections.

Bets on a second successive hike rose after the release. There is now a 37.1 percent chance officials will announce a 25-basis-point increase this month, according to CME Group’s FedWatch tool. The probability was around 22 percent before the data.

“This CPI report is a headache for the Fed, which had been indicating a willingness to pause this month,” said Neil Wilson at Saxo Markets, referring to several board members who had suggested they favoured a go-slow approach to assess last month’s lift.

“Markets too had all but priced out a hike later this month but repriced for the Fed to move a bit quicker after US inflation came in a little hotter than expected.”

– December lift ‘fully priced’ –

Pepperstone’s Chris Weston wrote: “Further evidence of right-tail inflation risk in the US has reinforced the higher-for-longer rates narrative, with sellers emerging across risk assets and interest rate-sensitive equities coming under renewed pressure.

“The breadth of price pressures across the CPI basket has been particularly concerning, challenging a market desperately in need of evidence of disinflation.”

He said “a December hike is now effectively fully priced”, adding that there was also a 66 percent probability of a January lift.

Tech firms — which rely on borrowing to fund their huge AI investments — led the losses Thursday, tracking their counterparts in New York.

Seoul’s Kospi dived more than seven percent, with SK hynix sinking more than 10 percent and Samsung more than nine percent.

And in Tokyo the Nikkei 225 shed more than four percent as Kioxia also dived more than 10 percent and Advantest plunged 12 percent. Tech investment titan SoftBank lost 9.5 percent.

Taipei lost almost three percent as market-heavyweight TSMC gave up around two percent.

The selling came after many tech firms had clawed back some of the huge losses sustained in a summer rout that came on the back of worries about elevated valuations and questions over when firms would see returns on their colossal investments.

Hong Kong, Shanghai, Singapore, Wellington, Manila and Jakarta were also deep in negative territory.

US government borrowing costs surged on the news, with 10-year Treasuries hitting fresh 24-year highs, though they later retreated on investor demand owing to their attractive yields above 5.3 percent.

The dollar gave back most of the gains sparked by bets on higher interest rates, while the yen was also helped by comments from Japan’s finance minister warning Tokyo was ready to step in with support.

World.title: Behind AI’s carbon footprint, a potential climate tool
World.content:
Paris – Artificial intelligence has become a lightning rod in climate debates over concerns about the growing carbon footprint of the data centres powering the technology.

The issue will be in the spotlight at the COP31 climate summit in Turkey next month, with the hosts saying they will push for “climate-responsible AI”.

But the discussion over the technology’s environmental impact — along with fears that it could pose an existential threat to humanity — has overshadowed its potential as a tool to combat climate change.

AI is being deployed in a broad range of applications, from improving weather forecasts to monitoring industrial emissions and optimising renewable energy.

Many of these applications are less energy-hungry than general-purpose language models such as OpenAI’s ChatGPT or Anthropic’s Claude, according to experts.

“Data centres have come in as a challenge… There are genuine concerns about what all of this could mean for the energy system, for the energy sector, for climate,” Siddharth Singh, an AI expert at the International Energy Agency (IEA), told AFP.

“At the same time, because (AI) is a tool, it’s an opportunity. It really comes down to how it is deployed,” Singh said.

– Renewables efficiency –

AI is already being used to make electricity grids more efficient in complex energy systems, helping operators manage the variability of solar and wind power.

The technology can produce localised forecasts of cloud cover, sunlight and wind, allowing companies to predict renewable output more accurately.

Singh said it can help limit the amount of “curtailment” — the practice of reducing certain types of electricity because the grid cannot handle it.

If deployed across the economy, from transport to industry and buildings, the technology could save 13.5 exajoules of energy by 2035, equivalent to Indonesia’s annual energy demand, according to the IEA.

Emissions reductions can be made, for example, by using AI to schedule a washing machine to run when solar electricity is abundant, Singh said.

WattTime, an environmental tech nonprofit, helps companies time their electric vehicles, phones or other devices to periods when the energy is coming from cleaner power sources.

“One of the things AI is very good at is forecasting,” WattTime co-founder Gavin McCormick said.

– Weather forecasting revolution –

AI is transforming weather forecasting by producing high-quality projections much faster, said Florian Pappenberger, director-general of the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF).

“AI has really revolutionised weather forecasting in the sense that you can actually now predict weather much faster, with a really high skill and with a high performance,” Pappenberger told AFP.

He said AI forecasting is still grounded in physics-based models, while allowing the ECMWF to achieve in two years what would traditionally have taken 10 years to accomplish.

It is also much cheaper than traditional methods, enabling the ECMWF to produce more forecasts.

The technology can also improve early warning systems.

A Google system can forecast river floods up to seven days in advance in over 150 countries, according to the US tech giant.

Rather than replacing humans, Pappenberger said, “I think (AI) is more like giving us superpowers to be even better or do things even better than we ever did before.”

– Spotting emissions –

Satellites and AI are also used to spot greenhouse gas emissions from individual facilities such as oil and gas sites, mines or landfills.

An initiative co-founded by McCormick, Climate TRACE, harnesses the technology to track emissions around the planet and build an inventory of the pollutants.

“Climate TRACE is 20 years more advanced because of AI,” McCormick said.

“We have been able to provide emissions inventories to every city and a lot of them now can make a climate action plan,” he said. “Without AI this would not have been possible.”

– Oil AI –

But while AI could boost the efficiency and use of renewables, the technology has long been used by oil and gas companies to sift through geological data, identify underground reservoirs and streamline fossil fuel production.

“AI can also have a detrimental impact on climate change from that angle,” said Maria Joao Sousa, executive director of Climate Change AI, a nonprofit promoting the use of AI for climate action.

“AI will never be a silver bullet,” she said. “Technology itself will never be the solution alone.”

World.title: Trump’s new press secretary faces scrutiny over credentials
World.content:
Washington – The White House was facing mounting questions Wednesday over new press secretary Katie Zacharia’s legal credentials, after a faltering first day in the job when she gave an inconclusive answer about where she had passed the bar exam.

A US watchdog group filed a complaint with the State Bar of California, asking it to investigate whether President Donald Trump’s spokeswoman — the public face of the administration — had broken the law by repeatedly presenting herself as a lawyer without a license.

Campaign for Accountability said Zacharia had described herself as a lawyer during television appearances and listed herself as general counsel of a California-based conservative nonprofit.

“Ms. Zacharia has represented herself as a lawyer repeatedly to buttress her reputation and credibility,” said the group’s executive director, Michelle Kuppersmith.

“The State Bar should investigate whether Ms. Zacharia has misled the public about her credentials,” she added.

Trump described Zacharia as “an attorney” when announcing her appointment Friday, but journalists have found no record of her being licensed to practice law in any US state.

“I practiced international transaction law, with all the appropriate credentials,” Zacharia said in a statement to AFP, without clarifying whether she held a US law license.

Zacharia has not specified where, if anywhere, she was admitted to the bar. Asked by reporters Tuesday where she had passed the bar exam, Zacharia replied: “When I moved to China.”

California’s state bar confirmed to US media that it had no record of Zacharia holding a license under either her married or maiden name.

Zacharia, 41, graduated from Pepperdine University’s law school in 2011, but obtaining a law degree does not automatically qualify someone to practice law.

Foreign nationals cannot sit China’s bar exam, although they can undertake certain legal work at Chinese law firms.

Zacharia previously worked for a law firm in Beijing, according to her professional profile.

The controversy followed a rocky first appearance as White House press secretary on Tuesday, when Zacharia read extensively from prepared notes during a briefing lasting just 14 minutes.

She took questions from only three news organizations, all considered sympathetic to Trump, and stumbled over some answers, at one point accidentally referring to the president as her husband.

Her performance drew criticism from former White House press secretary Jen Psaki, now a TV news host, who compared it to a “Saturday Night Live” comedy sketch.

Trump, however, praised Zacharia’s debut, telling reporters: “I thought she was very good.”

Zacharia succeeded Karoline Leavitt, who stepped down in August after becoming one of the most prominent public defenders of Trump’s second administration.

World.title: Musk suggests US govt behind any slowdown in Ukraine’s Starshield system
World.content:
Washington – SpaceX boss Elon Musk said Wednesday that any disruptions reported by Ukraine in using the Starshield satellite communications system would be the responsibility of the US government, not his company.

“Starshield systems are owned and controlled by the US government. Any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS,” Musk said, referring to US President Donald Trump.

Musk drew a distinction between the Starshield system, which Ukraine relies on for battlefield communications, and the parallel Starlink civilian satellite system, which Ukraine also deploys but is not allowed to use for offensive operations. Both were designed by Musk’s SpaceX.

Musk was responding to a post on X by Ukraine’s former defense minister Mykhailo Fedorov, who said that “Starlink connectivity at speeds of up to 160 km/h is being restored,” but that “removing Starshield’s speed limit entirely is now critical for Ukraine’s defense.”

Fedorov then thanked Musk for his “continued support.”

Ukrainian defense officials have suggested Washington is behind slower speeds reported on some internet terminals that help the country’s military hit Russian-occupied territory and operate interceptor drones.

Ukraine has also accused the United States of helping Russia by failing to warn it of incoming missile strikes, with Kyiv hit by ballistic missiles for two nights in a row before air raid sirens could sound to warn people to take cover.

Opposition Democrats in the US Senate and House denounced the Trump Administration over the reported interrupted connections.

“Trump’s making a choice — and it directly aids Putin’s slaughter of Ukrainian civilians,” House Foreign Affairs Committee Democrats said in a post on X, describing restrictions as “unconscionable” while Ukraine faced an onslaught of Russian drones and missiles.

In the Senate’s Foreign Relations Committee, top Democrat Jeanne Shaheen said the “restrictions on Ukraine’s access to Starshield must stop immediately,” adding that “lives are at stake.”

Shaheen also said that the defense department is required to notify “Congress if it pauses or downgrades intelligence sharing with Ukraine,” and called on Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth to immediately provide that notification if there are changes.

Republican Senator Tom Tillis also voiced concern, posting on X: “Supporting Ukrainian sovereignty — or at the very least, allowing for it — should not be a gray area for the US government or for American corporations.”

Trump, facing key midterm elections next month in which fuel prices are a major issue, has blamed Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil refineries for the squeeze on supplies and increase in prices at the pump.

A senior official in Kyiv confirmed that the United States had in recent days threatened to stop providing intelligence about Russian missile launches that Ukraine uses to thwart attacks.

Trump denied doing so on Tuesday.

World.title: Mourinho blasts ‘shameless’ timing of Vinicius ban decision
World.content:
Rome – Jose Mourinho hit out at the “shameless” decision by Spanish football authorities to announce that Real Madrid winger Vinicius Junior had been slapped with a four-match ban just hours before their Champions League clash with Roma kicked off.

The Brazil international was handed the punishment on Wednesday after being sent off during Saturday’s 1-0 La Liga win over Villarreal for pulling the hair of an opponent.

It is a costly ban, depriving Mourinho of one of his star attackers for an important run of league games that includes a Clasico clash with rivals Barcelona, who hold a six-point lead over Real at the summit of the table.

Vinicius started as Mourinho’s side pulled off an incredible late comeback to beat Roma 4-3 in the Champions League, having trailed 3-1 with seven minutes remaining.

But the Portuguese made his feelings clear about how the timing of the announcement had disrupted preparations in a post-match press conference.

Mourinho said: “Do you think it’s normal that a player from a Spanish team, who has to play a match that is also important for Spanish football, that two hours before the match a player knows he’s been given a four-match suspension?

“Couldn’t they do it now? Couldn’t they do it tomorrow morning? Do we have to come by bus and almost arrive at the stadium when we find out Vinicius has a four-match suspension?”

Mourinho added: “They do things shamelessly now. The cat is out of the bag now. Two hours before the match, a player must know he has a four-match suspension.

“A Spanish team that has earned three points for Spanish football, for the rankings, for the prestige of Spanish football. You want to kill a player two hours before the match; it doesn’t seem normal to me.”

– Scheduling complaints –

Mourinho also highlighted his unhappiness with scheduling, with his side set to face AEK Athens in the Greek capital on 4 November, before travelling to Valencia in La Liga on 7 November.

Asked what the Vinicius ban announcement says, Mourinho replied: “At the very least, a lack of respect.

“Playing in Athens on Wednesday night, arriving in Madrid probably at 5am, something like that, and then playing Saturday in Valencia, on a weekend that precedes a week of national team matches.

“It makes absolutely no sense, they make you play on Saturday in Valencia, which is an extremely difficult match, it doesn’t seem innocent to me.

“The usual excuses, I don’t buy them, because this wasn’t 25 years ago. The excuses from TV, that it was TV that decided, that it was TV that chose the match for Saturday, I don’t buy this anymore. I’m too old to swallow this.

“And this Vinicius story, two hours before a match, knowing that he has a four-match suspension, doesn’t deserve comment. Real Madrid fans aren’t stupid and I will do everything possible to open people’s eyes.”

It was a good night for Mourinho on the pitch, as his substitutions turned the game in Real’s favour after they were outplayed for much of the game until the closing stages.

Donyell Malen’s double had given Roma a 3-1 lead early in the second half, but two of Mourinho’s substitutes scored, Endrick and Carlos Espi, and another, Arda Guler, provided two assists in the late rally.

“I’m not going to be a genius and say I had prepared everything for a 3-1 to 4-3 victory, it’s not true,” Mourinho said.

“But I genuinely thought that in the last 20 minutes I had substitutions I could make, and I had substitutions that could change things.”

World.title: PSG beat Man City in Champions League thriller, Barcola hits Liverpool hat-trick
World.content:
Paris – Reigning champions Paris Saint-Germain romped to a 4-2 victory away to embattled Manchester City in the UEFA Champions League on Wednesday, while Bradley Barcola hit his first Liverpool goals with a hat-trick in a 6-3 win over LASK in Austria.

Elsewhere on a prolific night of European action, Real Madrid came from 3-1 down to beat Roma 4-3 and Aston Villa demolished Fenerbahce 6-0 at Villa Park.

City were playing at home at the Etihad Stadium for the first time since being found guilty of serious breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules over almost a decade that have left them facing the prospect of severe sanctions.

That verdict appeared to be hanging over the City team as PSG raced into a three-goal lead just past the half-hour mark, with Desire Doue, Ousmane Dembele and Vitinha all netting for the French side.

With former boss Pep Guardiola watching on, City produced a second-half fightback as Erling Haaland scored twice to take him to four Champions League goals already this season.

However, PSG got a fourth in between the Norwegian’s strikes, with City goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma unable to keep out a Maghnes Akliouche shot.

Donnarumma later made some amends by saving a Ferran Torres penalty, but City succumbed by the same margin as in their last Champions League meeting with PSG in January 2025.

“In the first half we were far superior to a great City side,” Paris coach Luis Enrique told broadcaster Canal Plus. “You can think these games are over but it is never the case at this level, and we could have ended up losing.”

Back-to-back title-holders PSG have won both Champions League games this season, scoring 10 goals in the process. They face Barcelona next week.

“Even with 3-0 in the first half, with the amount of chances we created in the second half, we deserved more,” City coach Enzo Maresca told TNT Sports.

Barcola, a big-money summer signing from PSG, had not found the net for Liverpool before scoring three times at the Raiffeisen Arena after Ronald Araujo had broken the deadlock against the Austrian champions.

Jeremie Frimpong and Lewis Koumas also netted for Andoni Iraola’s side, who were 4-0 ahead at one point before LASK scored three times in the space of 15 second-half minutes through Robert Ljubicic and Florian Flecker’s brace.

“Obviously I think he has to enjoy this because to score a hat-trick in the Champions League is always very difficult,” said Iraola of France forward Barcola.

– Real late show, Villa hit six –

There was a dramatic denouement in Italy, where a Marten de Roon goal and a Donyell Malen brace had Roma 3-1 up against Real Madrid inside the final 10 minutes.

However the visitors, who had earlier seen Kylian Mbappe score on his 100th Champions League appearance, produced an incredible late fightback.

Carlos Espi pulled one back in the 82nd minute and Brazil forward Endrick equalised before Antonio Rudiger grabbed a last-minute winner for Jose Mourinho’s men.

Swiss international Johan Manzambi opened the scoring for Villa against Fenerbahce on his 21st birthday, setting his club up for their biggest ever European victory.

Nicolas Jackson scored twice before half-time, and Ross Barkley bagged a second-half brace including a penalty. Tammy Abraham completed the scoring, leaving the Turkish side stunned.

Fredrik Sjovold got the only goal of the game as Norway’s Bodo/Glimt beat former European champions Borussia Dortmund 1-0, while Real Betis beat Porto 3-2 in Spain.

Abde Ezzalzouli put Betis ahead just after half-time, only for Gabri Veiga and Samuel Aghehowa to hit back for the Portuguese champions. However, Juan Hernandez levelled again and veteran Isco got a late winner.

In Rotterdam, Feyenoord beat Como 3-2 as the Dutch side’s coach Giovanni van Bronckhorst got the better of Cesc Fabregas.

Assane Diao gave the Italians the lead but Gjivai Zechiel and Anis Hadj Moussa struck for Feyenoord before an own goal by goalkeeper Robert Sanchez made it 3-1. Anastasios Douvikas then pulled one back.

Ukraine’s Shakhtar Donetsk were playing at home for the first time at Chelsea’s Stamford Bridge stadium, and they marked the occasion with a 3-1 win over AEK Athens.

Lovro Majer gave AEK the lead, but a Pedrinho penalty levelled matters before Vinicius Tobias and Gleiker Mendoza sealed the win to leave Shakhtar on four points from two outings.

Stuttgart won 3-0 away to Slovan Bratislava in the night’s other game.

World.title: Real Madrid comeback stuns Roma as Mourinho enjoys happy reunion
World.content:
Rome – Jose Mourinho enjoyed a Roma reunion to remember as Real Madrid completed an astonishing comeback by scoring three late goals to claim a 4-3 away win in the Champions League on Wednesday.

Marten de Roon gave the hosts a deserved opener before Kylian Mbappe struck back on his 100th Champions League appearance to level the scores at the break.

Two Donyell Malen strikes in the space of six minutes early in the second half seemed to take the game away from the 15-time European champions as Roma ran rampant.

But Real scored three goals in the final six minutes, all stemming from corners, to turn the game on its head as Carlos Espi, Endrick and ex-Roma defender Antonio Rudiger struck at a stunned Stadio Olimpico.

Mourinho was a popular figure as he led Roma to the UEFA Conference League title and Europa League final during two-and-a-half years in charge.

The Portuguese was honoured with banners and chants by the home crowd in Roma’s first home Champions League match in more than seven years, and the hosts started strongly as Mario Hermoso forced Thibaut Courtois into a flying fingertip save.

Roma took a deserved lead when De Roon swept a shot past Courtois from 25 yards in the 20th minute, and almost doubled it when Malen’s powerful shot squirmed under Courtois before being plucked off the line.

However, one costly moment of switching off proved enough to send them back to square one within five minutes of the opener being scored.

Hermoso misjudged an interception to allow Mbappe a clear run at goal and the France striker’s deflected shot flew into the roof of the net to level the scores with Real’s first meaningful chance of the game.

Mbappe marked his Champions League centurion status, something he is the youngest player to achieve aged 27, with his 72nd tournament goal – one that moved him into the all-time top five ahead of Real legend Raul Gonzalez.

The equaliser appeared to subdue Roma and steady Mourinho’s men, who twice threatened a second before the break as Marc Cucurella and Jude Bellingham came close.

– Roma take game to Madrid –

But Roma boss Gian Piero Gasperini insisted pre-match that Roma would not compromise on their full-throttle style regardless of opposition, and he was true to his word as they came out firing after the break.

Roma quickly re-took the lead when half-time substitute Rodrigo Mora fed the ball to Malen, who finished brilliantly by taking the ball in his stride with his first touch and lifting it over Courtois with his second.

Things got even better for the Italians just six minutes later when Malen raced onto a through ball to power home his second, given following a VAR review after initially being flagged for offside.

Real looked for a response as Mbappe twice tested Pierluigi Gollini, before having his second goal of the night ruled out for offside.

But set-pieces proved to be the key to unlock the Roma defence, as Espi tucked home a close-range rebound from a header to pull one back before Endrick powered home a header from another corner just two minutes later.

The final blow was struck by Rudiger in the 90th minute, the defender getting in front of his marker to guide home a close-range finish and complete an extraordinary turnaround.

The result leaves Real Madrid with six points from their opening two league phase matches, while Roma are on one point.

has been asked by

World.title: 'Can Hindus Eat Beef? BJP IT Cell Part 2': Dhruv Rathee faces two defamation cases in 24 hours
World.content:
NEW DELHI: YouTuber Dhruv Rathee is facing two separate legal proceedings in Delhi. A fresh defamation suit has been filed against him at the Saket court over a video allegedly claiming that Lord Ram and Goddess Sita consumed meat and alcohol during their exile.

Separately, Rathee has been served fresh summons in a 2018 criminal defamation case filed by BJP IT Cell member Vikas Pandey over a video titled "BJP IT Cell Part 2".

Fresh suit over Ram-Sita video

Supreme Court Advocate-on-Record Amita Sachdeva and other petitioners had approached the Delhi high court over the video titled âCan Hindus Eat BEEF? and prayed before the court to issue directions granting an interim restraint on Rathee from creating, uploading, or publishing similar content.

"Some time ago, Dhruv Rathee published a video claiming that Lord Shri Ram and Mother Sita consumed meat and alcohol during their exile. We took the matter regarding that video to the Delhi High Court, and the Delhi High Court directed the Govt of India to have the video removed."

"On July 15, 2026, the Govt of India directed YouTube to take down the video, after which that petition was disposed of. Following the disposal of the petition, someone extracted a three-minute segment from that 21-minute video and re-uploaded it,â she added.





According to Sachdeva, the petitioners approached the Delhi High Court again, which granted them liberty to initiate fresh legal proceedings against Rathee.

"We approached the Delhi High Court again. The Court granted us the liberty to file a fresh petition or suit against Dhruv Rathee and seek appropriate relief. Acting on that liberty, we filed a suit today in the Saket Court, before the Learned District Judge, seeking a declaration, an injunction, and damages for defamation; the matter was listed for hearing today," she said.

Sachdeva said the petitioner's senior counsel, Makarand Natkar, appeared through video conferencing but could not complete his submissions because of technical difficulties. The court subsequently adjourned the matter to November 5.

"Today, my senior counsel, Makarand Natkar, presented his submissions. He appeared via video conferencing (VC), but due to some technical issues with the VC connection, the submissions could not be completed.

Consequently, the Learned District Judge adjourned the matter to November 5, when we will present our fresh submissions," she added.

The complainants, who identified themselves as Hindu devotees, alleged that the video hurt their religious sentiments. The suit also seeks an ex-parte ad-interim injunction restraining Google from restoring, hosting, uploading, sharing or disseminating the video, or any video identical or similar in content, after notice and verification of the URL, during the pendency of the suit.

Fresh summons in 2018 defamation case

Separately, a Delhi court has issued fresh summons to Rathee in a defamation case filed by BJP IT Cell member Vikas Pandey in 2018. The court noted that attempts to serve Rathee had continued for several years.

Judicial Magistrate Rahul Jain was hearing Pandey's plea seeking fresh summons. In an order dated October 12, the court said, "From the available record, it is clear that the complainant has been trying to serve the accused no.

1 (Rathee) since the last several years..."

Appearing for Pandey, advocate Samaksh Sharma submitted that Rathee ordinarily resides in Austria and had come to India for the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) protests in Delhi. He argued that fresh summons were necessary to ensure prompt steps could be taken to serve the accused.

The court permitted fresh summons to be served through dasti service, allowing the complainant to accompany the process server.

Rathee has since been physically served at his Gurugram residence. The proceedings had remained pending amid unsuccessful attempts to serve him since 2019.

Speaking about the notice served on Rathee, Pandey said, "The court summons has been pasted outside Dhruv Rathee's home because he was not coming out. This stems from eight years ago when Dhruv Rathee created around three videos alleging that I offered Rs 50 lakh to someone to spread fake news against him.â

âWhen Arvind Kejriwal amplified this fake news by tweeting and retweeting it, I filed a case against both Kejriwal and Dhruv Rathee. While Arvind Kejriwal offered an apology, Dhruv Rathee never appeared before the court. Consequently, a notice and summons were issued, which my lawyer pasted outside his Gurugram home..." he added.

The case also reached the Supreme Court in connection with a retweet of the video by Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) national convenor Arvind Kejriwal.

In February 2024, Kejriwal told the apex court that he had made a mistake by retweeting it.

The cases come days after Delhi and Gurugram Police detained Rathee at his Sector 56 residence in Gurugram on October 10, ahead of his planned participation in a CJP protest at Jantar Mantar. He was released after around 22 hours.

The detention took place amid protests in Delhi led by the CJP, which has been demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The protests saw extensive security arrangements, barricading, traffic restrictions and the detention of protesters.

World.title: Oct 10 Jantar Mantar protest permission denied due to violence during CJP protest on Jul 20: Delhi Police
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar on Thursday filed an affidavit in the Supreme Court saying permission for Oct 10 CJP protest at Jantar Manor was denied due to past experience of large-scale violence during its July 20 protests, inability of organisers to control supporters and the grave inconvenience caused to general public because of string of protests from Oct 6-8 that choked the central Delhi for days together.

Narrating the sensitivity of central Delhi housing Rashtrapati Bhavan, Parliament, Supreme Court, embassies and other institutions requiring a complex security arrangement as well as measures for maintaining public order, the police commissioner said, âNo police administration can permit any breach of public order in the national capital, particularly when a call is given by an organisation with a recent history of mob violence, and incidents resulting in injuries to several individuals and the subsequent events of Oct 6, 7,8.

â

âDue to all these marches, the central Delhi areas got completely choked and there were huge traffic snarls for long hours, resulting in students and innocent citizens getting stuck in traffic jams, resulting in them missing their trains, airlines etc,â he said.

âThe gatherings were very aggressive, fuelled by persons adoring cover of âfreelance journalismâ, who were physically harassing policemen, some miscreants were misbehaving with lady police personnel resulting gin injuries to over a dozen police personnel,â he said on the Oct 10 protest which was called despite denial of permission and attempts to illegally gather people.





As per the SC laid down law, the Police removed the illegally gathered people from the site where prohibitory orders were in place but those detained punctured the tyres of the buses in which they were kept and broke window shields in acts of violence, the commissioner said.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

CJP did not seek permission for holding protest on Oct 10 but merely sent an intimation to the police, the CP said, adding that preventive measures were taken in view of intelligence inputs that despite denial of permission, people would attempt to gather at Jantar Mantar on Oct 10 to create a dangerous situation and cause serious public order problem.

All those detained for attempting to protest in violation of prohibitory orders were released after a few hours and were kept in make-shift centres, not police lock ups. Police provided them with hot, fresh and good meals and were permitted to leave after the requirement of detention ceased to exist, he said.

The political leaders removed from illegal protest were requested to sit in the chambers of SHOs and were provided with tea, coffee, meals and other refreshments while fully maintaining the dignity of the office they held or holding, the CP said.

World.title: ‘Timely action’: India welcomes US response after Illinois teen held over Hindu temple attack plot
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Consulate General of India in Chicago on Wednesday welcomed the timely action taken by US law enforcement authorities after the arrest of 19-year-old man accused of plotting a mass shooting at a Hindu temple in Illinois.

In a statement, the Indian Consulate said it was aware of reports about an alleged plot to attack a place of worship in Illinois's Aurora. It added that it was closely monitoring the situation and was in touch with members of the Indian diaspora.

"The Consulate is aware of reports concerning a foiled attempt to target a place of worship in Aurora, Illinois. We appreciate the timely action by law enforcement authorities.

We are in touch with members of the Indian diaspora and are closely monitoring developments," the Consulate General of India in Chicago said.

According to the Palatine Police Department, the 19-year-old suspect, identified as Alexandros Paporakis, was arrested after an investigation into threats of a possible mass shooting at a Hindu temple.

The investigation began on October 11, when the Palatine Police Department received information from the Mount Prospect Police Department about a possible mass shooting.





The information came from a person who reported receiving concerning electronic messages from Paporakis.

Investigators said Paporakis had shared a document describing an alleged plan to carry out a mass shooting at the Hindu temple. He had also shared images of a rifle, rifle magazines, body armour and other tactical equipment.

Police arrested Paporakis as he was leaving his home. Detectives later searched his residence and recovered a rifle, several loaded rifle magazines, hundreds of additional rounds of ammunition, tactical equipment and other items linked to the investigation.

The items included a tactical vest with body armour and a patch displaying imagery associated with white supremacist extremism.

Investigators also examined electronic communications and a document attributed to Paporakis titled "Why I Fought: A.K.A.: (Aurora Shooterâs Manifesto)."

According to police, the document contained white supremacist and extremist views, including references to violence against people of South Asian heritage, particularly those of Indian descent.

Detectives believe Paporakis may have been planning an attack on October 11, possibly targeting a Hindu place of worship in the Aurora area. Following the investigation, police contacted Hindu places of worship within their jurisdiction to alert them to the reported threat.

Paporakis was charged with one count of Making a Terrorist Threat, a Class X felony, and one count of Unlawful Possession of Weapons. He appeared for a detention hearing on Wednesday, where a judge ordered that he remain in custody.

Palatine Police chief William Nord stressed the seriousness of the alleged threat and credited the quick response of the two police departments and the person who first reported the messages.

"The seriousness of this alleged threat cannot be overstated. Through the immediate sharing of information and coordinated response by the Palatine and Mount Prospect Police Departments, officers were able to identify and take the suspect into custody.

We are grateful for the FBIâs assistance in the subsequent investigation and commend the individual who initially came forward with this information. Protecting our communities and places of worship remains a priority, and we will continue working with our law enforcement partners as this investigation moves forward," Nord said.

The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) also highlighted its work with local and state police to investigate threats allegedly linked to extremist ideologies.

"The FBI aggressively works alongside our local and state law enforcement partners to identify, investigate, and dismantle any threats of violence driven by radical ideologies," said FBI Chicago Special Agent in Charge Ryan Whalen.

He added that the suspect had been arrested without causing harm to the community and said the agency would continue to pursue those responsible for threats of violence.

"Thanks to the swift action by the Palatine and Mount Prospect Police Departments, the subject was taken into custody without harm to our community.

The FBI values these strong partnerships and will continue to use every law enforcement and prosecutorial resource available to bring any offender using fear or violence to justice," Whalen said.

The Indian Consulate's statement comes as US authorities continue to investigate the alleged plot and examine evidence recovered during the probe. Police have also alerted Hindu places of worship in their jurisdiction about the reported threat.

World.title: 'Pakistan needs to look inwards': India questions UN rights body's silence on PoK unrest
World.content:
NEW DELHI: India has asked the UN human rights body when it would issue a report seeking answers from Pakistan on steps taken to address concerns over the situation in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK), including investigations into killings and restrictions on internet access.

First Secretary at the Permanent Mission of India, Anuj Swarup, delivered the statement during an interactive dialogue with the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights at the 81st session of the UN General Assemblyâs Third Committee on Wednesday.

âWhen can we expect OHCHR to issue a report on the steps taken by the Government of Pakistan on this? Pakistan would do well to look inwards and reflect on how such rights are not being enjoyed in its large part, including Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, and for that matter, in Rawalakot, which is under its illegal occupation,â Swarup said.

Swarup referred to detailed statements by the Office of the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR) and the High Commissioner on the situation in PoK. The statements called for prompt, thorough and impartial investigations into killings allegedly carried out by armed and security forces.

They also urged authorities to ensure that detained leaders of the Joint Awami Action Committee had access to legal representation and their families, and were afforded due process and a fair trial.





The statements further called for lifting internet restrictions across Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir and holding meaningful political dialogue to address the grievances of the local population.

The High Commissioner had also noted that dozens of people, mostly protesters but also law enforcement personnel, had reportedly been killed since June, ahead of the July 27 Legislative Assembly elections. Swarup said the OHCHR had adopted an approach of âextreme selectivityâ in addressing such incidents.

âViolent responses to protests in our neighbourhood as well as in the west have gone uncommented. Needless to say, such double standards contribute to loss of trust in multilateralism and the work of OHCHR,â he said.

Swarup said Indiaâs freedom movement, led by Mahatma Gandhi, championed non-violence and equality, values that also shaped the Constitution, which guarantees fundamental rights to every citizen.

âIndian citizens exercise rights subject to maintenance of public order and safety. Our law enforcement authorities act strictly in accordance with the law, and our courts remain available for redressal of any grievance,â he said.

Swarup said India, as a member of the UN Human Rights Council, had contributed constructively to discussions on contemporary issues and would continue to engage with the High Commissioner and OHCHR in a âspirit of trust and partnership without selectivity and double standardsâ.

He also stressed that the Indian Constitution guarantees people in Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh the same fundamental rights as citizens in other parts of the country, adding that both regions are integral and inalienable parts of India.

Indiaâs remarks came days after New Delhi described comments by the Office of the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights on protests in the national capital as âunwarrantedâ and âunacceptable interferenceâ in the countryâs internal affairs.

Last week, the UN Human Rights Office expressed concern over âreports of mass detentions of demonstrators, protest leaders, members of civil society organisations, lawyers and journalists, before and during todayâs large-scale demonstrations in Delhi.â

In a statement, the ministry of external affairs (MEA) said, "India is the worldâs largest democracy, where the right to peaceful assembly is guaranteed by our Constitution and safeguarded by robust institutions, an independent judiciary and a free media."

âAs in every democracy, Indian citizens exercise this right subject to the maintenance of public order and safety. Our law enforcement authorities act strictly in accordance with the law, and our courts remain available to all for the redressal of any grievances,â the ministry said.

The MEA also accused the Office of the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR) of selectivity in its public statements, alleging that it had remained silent on violent responses to protests in neighbouring countries and law enforcement actions closer to its own headquarters.

Police in Palatine, Illinois, arrested a 19-year-old man following an investigation into threats of a potential mass shooting at a Hindu temple.The investigation began on October 11, when the Palatine Police Department received information from the Mount Prospect Police Department about concerning electronic communications allegedly sent by Alexandros Paporakis.Investigators said Paporakis had shared a document outlining an alleged plan for a mass shooting at the Hindu temple. We are grateful for the FBIâs assistance in the subsequent investigation and commend the individual who initially came forward with this information. Protecting our communities and places of worship remains a priority, and we will continue working with our law enforcement partners as this investigation moves forward," Palatine Police Chief William Nord said, as cited by ANI.Paporakis was arrested as he was leaving his residence.
